data.title: Ruby 3.5 Feature: Namespace on read
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Ruby中一个新的实验性功能提案，即通过“读取时命名空间”（Namespace on Read）来定义虚拟顶层命名空间。该功能允许在不同命名空间中分别加载和要求库文件，从而避免库之间的名称冲突，并支持加载同一gem的不同版本。该功能最初通过环境变量`RUBY_NAMESPACE=1`启用，默认情况下是禁用的。

文章详细说明了“写入时命名空间”（On Write）和“读取时命名空间”（On Read）两种方法的区别，并展示了如何使用`Namespace.new`创建新命名空间及其实现细节。不同命名空间中的常量、类变量、全局变量和方法相互隔离，确保独立运行。文章还提供了示例代码，展示了如何在不同命名空间中加载和使用模块及类。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby新命名空间功能的实用性及其实现方式

不同观点：
• 反对该功能的实际需求：
  - ezekg认为该功能解决了一个实际中很少存在的问题，尤其是像byroot这样在Shopify处理大规模Rails代码库的人也持相同观点，因此建议废弃该功能。
  - gitroom表示经过15年的Ruby开发经验，质疑新语言特性是否带来更多麻烦而不是解决问题。

• 支持该功能在特定场景下的实用性：
  - jacobevelyn分享了一个实际使用场景，在维护的gem中需要对不同git分支和多个可能命名冲突的gem进行基准测试，目前使用了一些不太优雅的技巧来解决问题，但对该功能是否应加入语言特性持中立态度。
  - JohnBooty认为该功能在处理全局常量命名冲突时是有用的，但担心这会鼓励不良编码实践。

• 对功能实现方式的争议：
  - semiquaver指出该功能虽然解决了Ruby长期缺乏的功能，但其通过方式存在重大概念问题、bug和性能回退，引发了广泛反对。
  - usrbinenv比较了Ruby和Go在命名空间处理上的不同，认为Go的默认命名空间处理可能更好。

• 对现有语言特性的满意与否：
  - irjustin希望Ruby采用像Python或JavaScript那样的显式导入机制，以解决“魔法”问题。
  - kristel100认为该更新是干净且实用的，可能会吸引那些对全局命名空间感到不适的开发者。

• 对gem生态系统的影响：
  - baggy_trough担心该功能会鼓励gem捆绑版本锁定的依赖，从而损害gem生态系统。

补充讨论：
- felipemesquita引用了David Bryant Copeland关于npm安全性的文章，讨论了允许多个依赖版本同时加载的复杂性。
- Alifatisk询问了该功能的适用场景，并指出Ruby已有模块可以用于命名空间，质疑新功能的必要性。
- krispyfi幽默地表示命名空间是一个伟大的想法，鼓励更多类似改进。

争议焦点：该功能是否真正解决了实际问题，以及其对编码实践和gem生态系统的潜在负面影响。

Description
This replaces
#19744
Concept
¶
This proposes a new feature to define virtual top-level namespaces in Ruby. Those namespaces can require/load libraries (either .rb or native extension) separately from other namespaces. Dependencies of required/loaded libraries are also required/loaded in the namespace.
This feature will be disabled by default at first, and will be enabled by an env variable
RUBY_NAMESPACE=1
as an experimental feature.
(It could be enabled by default in the future possibly.)
"on read" approach
¶
The "on write" approach here is the design to define namespaces on the loaded side. For example, Java packages are defined in the .java files and it is required to separate namespaces from each other. It can be implemented very easily, but it requires all libraries to be updated with the package declaration. (In my opinion, it's almost impossible in the Ruby ecosystem.)
The "on read" approach is to create namespaces and then require/load applications and libraries in them. Programmers can control namespace separation at the "read" time. So, we can introduce the namespace separation incrementally.
Motivation
¶
The "namespace on read" can solve the 2 problems below, and can make a path to solve another problem:
Avoiding name conflicts between libraries
Applications can require two different libraries safely which use the same module name.
Avoiding unexpected globally shared modules/objects
Applications can make an independent/unshared module instance.
Multiple versions of gems can be required
Application developers will have fewer version conflicts between gem dependencies if rubygems/bundler will support the namespace on read. (Support from RubyGems/Bundler and/or other packaging systems will be needed)
For the motivation details, see [Feature
#19744
].

Namespace specification
¶
Types of namespaces
¶
There are two namespace types, "root" and "user" namespace. "Root" namespace exists solely in a Ruby process, and "user" namespaces can be created as many as Ruby programmers want.
Root namespace
¶
Root namespace is a unique namespace to be defined when a Ruby process starts. It only contains built-in classes/modules/constants, which are available without any
require
calls, including RubyGems itself (when
--disable-gems
is not specified).
At here, "builtin" classes/modules are classes/modules accessible when users' script evaluation starts, without any require/load calls.
User namespace
¶
User namespace is a namespace to run users' Ruby scripts. The "main" namespace is the namespace to run the user's
.rb
script specified by the
ruby
command-line argument. Other user namespaces ("optional" namespaces) can be created by
Namespace.new
call.
In user namespace (both main and optional namespaces), built-in class/module definitions are copied from the root namespace, and other new classes/modules are defined in the namespace, separately from other (root/user) namespaces.
The newly defined classes/modules are top-level classes/modules in the main namespace like
App
, but in optional namespaces, classes/modules are defined under the namespace (subclass of Module), like
ns::App
.
In that namespace
ns
,
ns::App
is accessible as
App
(or
::App
). There is no way to access
App
in the main namespace from the code in the different namespace
ns
.
Constants, class variables and global variables
¶
Constants, Class variables of built-in classes and global variables are also separated by namespace. Values set to class/global variables in a namespace are invisible in other namespaces.
Methods and procs
¶
Methods defined in a namespace run with the defined namespace, even when called from other namespaces.
Procs created in a namespace run with the defined namespace too.

data.title: The FTC puts off enforcing its 'click-to-cancel' rule
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）将原定于5月14日生效的“点击取消”规则 enforcement 推迟至7月14日。该规则要求订阅服务的取消流程必须与其注册流程一样简便，例如如果注册可以在线完成，那么取消也必须可以在线进行。此次延期是由于对企业在原定日期前 compliance 的负担进行了重新评估，FTC 以3-0的投票结果通过了延期决定。不过，FTC 表示在新截止日期后将严格执行该规则，但不排除在执行过程中根据暴露的问题对规则进行修改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：消费者在取消服务过程中遇到的困难及相关问题，以及企业和政府在消费者保护方面的角色。

不同观点：
• **消费者遇到的实际困难**：
  - arwhatever 描述了在尝试取消DSL服务时遇到的繁琐过程，包括难以理解的客服口音、长时间的等待音乐以及被转接到不同的号码。
  - RankingMember 认为这种注册和取消服务的不对称处理是荒谬的，但在此政府执政下并不令人惊讶。

• **企业和政府责任**：
  - nixpulvis 希望看到一个主要以消费者保护为平台的候选人，认为公司越来越肆无忌惮地侵害消费者权益。
  - SoftTalker 提出如果可以在线订阅服务，那么取消服务也应同样方便，并质疑取消选项是否应与订阅选项同样显眼。

• **企业和消费者行为的关系**：
  - bilsbie 认为繁琐的取消过程实际上会损害企业的销售，因为消费者会因为取消麻烦而选择不加入服务。
  - sillystu04 认为像Visa/Mastercard这样的大公司有能力自行执行一些保护消费者的措施，但更希望通过监管来解决问题。

• **系统设计和信息安全**：
  - OptionOfT 指出服务通常在收费前提供访问，因此如果无法收费，应立即暂停或终止服务，但公司通过获取大量消费者信息（如SSN）使得取消变得困难。
  - typedef_struct 提出“点击收费”的概念，即如果不使用服务就不应被收费。

• **政治背景和政策影响**：
  - Gud 作为欧洲人，对美国消费者在取消服务时面临的困难表示惊讶。
  - Suppafly 和 kylehotchkiss 提到在共和党执政期间，对消费者有利的政策经常被取消或推迟。

• **哲学和社会心理学角度**：
  - twoquestions 对为什么有人会支持这种对消费者不利的政策表示困惑，并将其与“政府故意让事情变得更糟”联系起来。

补充讨论：
- arwhatever 进一步指出，延迟执行反欺诈行为实际上增加了这些行为的平均利润，从而鼓励了更多类似欺诈行为。
- lenerdenator 提到在拜登政府最后一年联邦机构在消费者保护方面的努力，但预测这些措施在政权更替后将不再重要。

争议焦点：企业和政府在消费者保护中的角色，以及消费者在取消服务时面临的繁琐过程是否合理。

News
The FTC puts off enforcing its ‘click-to-cancel’ rule
Companies now have until July 14th to make it as easy to cancel subscriptions as it is to sign up for them.
Companies now have until July 14th to make it as easy to cancel subscriptions as it is to sign up for them.
by
Wes Davis
May 10, 2025, 10:14 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
The FTC seal.
Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge
Wes Davis
is a weekend editor who covers the latest in tech and entertainment. He has written news, reviews, and more as a tech journalist since 2020.
The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) was set to start enforcing the remaining provisions of its “click-to-cancel” rule on May 14th, requiring that subscriptions be as easy to cancel as to start. Now,
the agency says
it won’t enforce the rule until July 14th, as
TechCrunch
reports
.
Also known as the Negative Option Rule, the big component of click-to-cancel is that it forbids companies from making customers jump through hoops that differ from the process to sign up for an account. If you can sign up online, you must be able to cancel online, too. As the FTC points out, the original May 14th deadline was already a deferral for that and related provisions.
Related
The FTC is finally making it easier to cancel your gym membership
Guess who’s suing the FTC to stop ‘click to cancel’
The agency says it chose to push enforcement back even further after “a fresh assessment of the burdens that forcing compliance by this date would impose.” The FTC voted 3-0 for the delay, but as
TechCrunch
notes, two of a typical five commissioners were absent from the vote. That’s because they were
illegally fired by Donald Trump
in March.
Perhaps on the bright side for consumers, the FTC says that starting on the new deadline, “regulated entities must be in compliance with the whole of the Rule because the Commission will begin enforcing it.” However, it doesn’t rule out changing any of the regulation’s provisions, writing that it’s “open to amending the Rule” if enforcing it “exposes any problems.”

- arwhatever 进一步指出，延迟执行反欺诈行为实际上增加了这些行为的平均利润，从而鼓励了更多类似欺诈行为。
- lenerdenator 提到在拜登政府最后一年联邦机构在消费者保护方面的努力，但预测这些措施在政权更替后将不再重要。

争议焦点：企业和政府在消费者保护中的角色，以及消费者在取消服务时面临的繁琐过程是否合理。

data.title: Demonstrably Secure Software Supply Chains with Nix
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了如何利用Nix实现高度安全的软件供应链，满足各国政府对关键系统软件安全性的严格要求。传统方法如气隙环境和软件源本地分支维护虽然提升安全性，但会减慢开发速度并增加成本。Nix作为一个强大的包和依赖管理器，能够在不影响开发效率的情况下，提供可验证的供应链完整性。它通过保证构建完整性、追踪源代码、审计输出等功能，确保软件从源到成品的透明性和可验证性，满足监管要求。开发者、DevOps团队和合规官员都能从中受益，实现安全、可重现的构建和可验证的审计证明。文章还提供了一个GitHub项目示例，展示如何从零开始重建系统以证明供应链完整性。Nix的这些特性使其在未来可能成为显著的竞争优势。

43963747.article_content:
Demonstrably Secure Software Supply Chains with Nix
📆
Mon May 12 2025 by Jacek Galowicz
(9 min. reading time)
Maintaining secure software development environments, especially those that require
high levels of integrity guarantees, often comes with significant overhead.
Organizations frequently resort to air-gapped environments, extensive employee
vetting, and local forks of all software sources.
While these methods aim to enhance security, they can drastically slow down development,
introduce vulnerabilities due to outdated packages, and thus increase costs.
What if you could achieve ironclad supply chain integrity without these burdens?
Government authorities worldwide are demanding stronger proof that software used
in critical systems is secure.
Agencies like the USA’s
CISA
/
DISA
,
Germany’s
BSI
/
DeuMilSAA
,
France’s
ANSSI
/
DGSE
,
Italy’s
ACN
,
Spain’s
CCN
, etc.
are setting strict requirements.
Meeting these rules is not optional for many organizations.
This article explores how Nix, a powerful package and depencency manager, offers a unique
and robust solution to meet these security standards while simultaneously saving costs,
freeing up developers to work with practically unconstrained software, and eliminating the
need for restrictive, air-gapped environments.
Nix allows you to prove the exact origin and integrity of your software before delivery without
impeding your development workflow.
Let developers use the latest and greatest toolchains and provide the supply chain
integrity proof for the release later!
Using Nix, you can achieve the high levels of transparency and verifiability required by regulators. It allows you to:
Prove Integrity
: Guarantee that this exact set of sources produced this
image without third-party interference, satisfying regulatory requirements.
Track Sources
: Include all application sources and toolchains (e.g., compilers and their compilers)
for complete transparency and fully hermetic offline rebuilds.
Audit Outputs
: Export and archive the exact sources (typically a few GB of tarballs) of each release for
third-party audits, ensuring trust and accountability for compliance.
While organizations are just starting to use Nix to address these requirements,
we believe that as regulators become more familiar with its capabilities,
demonstrating verifiable supply chain integrity with Nix will become a significant competitive advantage.
This article explains how Nix makes this possible.
Who Benefits?
Developers and DevOps Teams
: Ensure reproducible, secure builds without maintaining forks of open source packages
and patch lists on top. Use the latest tools to meet your tight deadlines.
Compliance Officers
: Provide verifiable proof for audits required by government agencies.
Security Professionals
: Mitigate supply chain attacks with full transparency to meet regulatory demands.
What’s Included in the Example
Our example
GitHub project applicative-systems/secure-supply-chain
shows this vision in action.
It provides a relatively minimal bootable NixOS live CD/USB image with halfway realistic demo applications:
C++ Database Writer
: Listens on a TCP port, pipes the user input to a PostgreSQL
database.
Rust Database Reader
: Serves database content over HTTP.
The booted ISO runs these services.
We use this image as a halfway realistic demonstrator:
This could be your product image and we show how to rebuild everything completely from scratch to demonstrate your supply chain integrity.
The project’s
README.md
explains the full steps without much detail.
Follow the rest of this article for the explanation of what it does.
The Nix Deep Dive: From Package Derivations to Verifiable Closures
The bootable ISO/USB image in the repository can be built by a simple
nix build .#iso
call.
This is great as it will work on any machine/computer the same, but it doesn’t explain where the sources really come from.
Also, it will not rebuild everything from source bacause it can download most of the packages from the typically
trusted
cache.nixos.org
- but that won’t give us the government authories’ acceptance.
When we run
nix derivation show
on the output of our system image Nix recipe, we get output like this:
$ nix derivation show $(nix build --print-out-paths .#iso)
{
"/nix/store/sd3cmxsjpjpl298v88csr96ywph1s39g-nixos-supply-chain-25.05pre-git-x86_64-linux.iso.drv"
: {
#
...
"inputDrvs"
: {
#
list
of
derivations
that
this
derivation
depends
on
"/nix/store/abc123-bla.drv"
: {
#
...
},
},
"inputSrcs"
: [
#
list
of
source
folders
,
scripts
,
and
other
directly
#
referenced
files
],
"name"
:
"nixos-supply-chain-25.05pre-git-x86_64-linux.iso"
,
"outputs"
: {
"path"
:
"/nix/store/xvrwkzlz8a1jbvn910kvc0k27j6qhmjx-nixos-supply-chain-25.05pre-git-x86_64-linux.iso"
}
},
}
This is the JSON-structured content of the
Nix derivation
.
(Nix expressions that describe packages, evaluate to derivations.
Derivations are more machine-readable data structures that describe a complete build environment)

data.title: Why GADTs matter for performance (2015)
data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了广义代数数据类型（GADTs）在OCaml中对性能的重要性。作者起初认为GADTs主要用于编译器相关的功能，对系统编程不重要，但后来发现GADTs在优化内存表示方面非常关键。

OCaml的 polymorphism 导致某些数据结构在内存上不够高效，例如数组无论存储何种数据类型都占用相同空间。为了优化，作者尝试设计一个能根据元素类型选择不同内存表示的紧凑数组类型。然而，不使用GADTs时，类型推断会导致函数（如`get`和`set`）只能处理特定类型（如字符），限制了通用性。

解决方法之一是使用类似面向对象的方式，通过闭包记录实现不同类型的处理函数。GADTs则提供了一种更优雅和安全的方式来实现这种优化，从而提高性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OCaml中GADTs（广义代数数据类型）的使用及其优缺点，包括性能、实际应用案例和学习曲线。

不同观点：
• [cryptonector] 认为GADTs提供了一种单一的抽象，可以为特定类型和泛型类型提供多种不同的实现，开发者不需要过多考虑具体实现，但需要在接口定义中使用类型提示来引导编译器行为。他还提到Yaron Minsky和Stephen Dolan等人在OCaml领域的影响力，并对Stephen Dolan的工作表示赞赏。

• [cosmic_quanta] 表示对GADTs在Haskell中的实际应用感到困惑，认为虽然GADTs的概念听起来很强大，但缺乏非编译器相关的具体使用案例，因此不知道何时应该使用GADTs。

• [rbjorklin] 关注GADTs的性能提升，询问是否有人有关于使用GADTs时预期性能提升的具体数据，指出文章中未提及任何相关数字。

• [hyperbrainer] 提供了一个相关的OCaml RFC链接，可能暗示对GADTs或相关特性的讨论在OCaml社区中是一个持续的过程，并邀请其他人查看该链接以获取更多信息。

• [goldchainposse] 对Jane Street大量使用OCaml表示质疑，认为虽然该公司的技术选择使他们成为知名OCaml用户，但这种选择可能在开发速度和维护成本上付出了代价。

补充讨论：
• 关于GADTs的具体应用场景和其实际效果的讨论较为缺乏，尤其是在非编译器相关领域。
• 对于GADTs的性能提升，目前缺乏具体的数据支持，用户希望看到更多量化的性能分析。
• 对OCaml在实际商业环境中的使用成本和效益存在争议，特别是对开发速度和维护的影响。

OCaml, I wasn’t particularly happy about it. I assumed that it was the kind of
nonsense you get when you let compiler writers design your programming language.
Which is to say that the standard GADT examples all seem to be about the kinds
of things that compiler writers do, like embed domain-specific languages or
build typed abstract-syntax trees. But it didn’t seem particularly relevant for
the kind of systems programming that I think about.
But it became apparent pretty quickly that I was wrong. In particular, since
GADTs have landed, at Jane Street we’ve found lots of examples where GADTs are
important for performance, of all things. The theme in these examples is that
GADTs enable you to tweak your memory representations in ways that would
otherwise be painful or impossible to do safely in OCaml.
The Problem of Polymorphism
I’d like to walk through a simple example that illustrates this aspect of GADTs,
but first, a few words about OCaml’s memory representation. OCaml’s polymorphism
is in an important way backed on that memory representation. In particular,
consider a simple polymorphic function like
List.iter
, which has the following
type:

->
unit

unit
The polymorphic type tells you that
List.iter
can operate on lists of any
type, and in OCaml, this is achieved with a single compiled version of the code.
This is possible because the memory representation of the elements of a list are
uniform: you can always refer to an OCaml value in a single word, either as a
pointer to a heap-allocated value, or as an immediate that fits inside that
word.
That means that some OCaml datatypes are less efficient space-wise than you
might imagine. Arrays, for example, take the same amount of space per element
whether those elements are bytes, 32-bit ints, or 64-bit ints. (There’s actually
some special magic in the compiler for float arrays, though this is probably
more trouble than it’s worth, as described by Alain Frisch
here
. But let’s ignore
float arrays for now.)
OCaml does have a tighter representations for byte arrays, called
bytes
. But
it’s a completely different type, and so building a general purpose data
structure that uses
bytes
when it would make sense, and ordinary arrays
otherwise, is a little awkward.

Let’s see what happens if we try to design (without GADTs) an array type that
sometimes uses the general array representation and sometimes uses

43945660.article_summary:
文章讨论了广义代数数据类型（GADTs）在OCaml中对性能的重要性。作者起初认为GADTs主要用于编译器相关的功能，对系统编程不重要，但后来发现GADTs在优化内存表示方面非常关键。

OCaml的 polymorphism 导致某些数据结构在内存上不够高效，例如数组无论存储何种数据类型都占用相同空间。为了优化，作者尝试设计一个能根据元素类型选择不同内存表示的紧凑数组类型。然而，不使用GADTs时，类型推断会导致函数（如`get`和`set`）只能处理特定类型（如字符），限制了通用性。

解决方法之一是使用类似面向对象的方式，通过闭包记录实现不同类型的处理函数。GADTs则提供了一种更优雅和安全的方式来实现这种优化，从而提高性能。

data.title: Writing N-body gravity simulations code in Python
data.author: dargscisyhp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由“CFD Python: 12 steps to Navier-Stokes”课程启发的教程，目标是教导初学者如何用Python编写高效且简洁的N体重力模拟代码。教程假设读者具备基本的Python和微积分知识，并详细解释每个步骤，适合初学者跟随学习。教程包含五个步骤：初始设置、重力计算、第一个N体程序、高级算法和自适应时间步长，此外还包括绘图和动画的额外内容。完整代码可在每一步的末尾获取，但也鼓励读者自行翻译代码以加深理解。教程源代码和相关资料可在GitHub和作者网站上找到。完成后，读者应能够独立编写N体模拟代码，并被鼓励开展相关项目。参考文献包括Lorena Barba等人的CFD Python教程以及其他相关书籍和论文。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：N-body问题模拟的技术、优化及其相关经验分享

不同观点：
• [技术实现与优化]
  ◦ [antognini] 提出通过使用Jax和GPU来加速N-body模拟，特别是对于大量天体系统，能够显著提升速度。
  ◦ [the__alchemist] 建议使用Barnes Hut算法进行优化，通过递归立方体树对天体进行分组，以提高计算效率，并提到更复杂的FMM方法。
  ◦ [munchler] 对重力计算中距离立方作为分母的实现提出疑问，并自行解答该方法是为了标准化向量并应用平方反比定律。

• [个人经验分享]
  ◦ [umpalumpaaa] 分享了自己高中时使用C++编写N-body模拟的经历，尽管硬件条件不佳且结果不理想，但从中获得了乐趣。
  ◦ [kristel100] 认为N-body问题是数值物理的入门问题，从零开始编写是必经之路，并在性能优化上获得额外加分。
  ◦ [eesmith] 回忆了1990年代在大学图书馆阅读数值计算结果书籍的经历，特别提到三体问题中特殊处理近距离交互的必要性。
  ◦ [quantadev] 分享了1980年代使用C语言进行粒子模拟的经历，并提出了关于广义相对论中时间变慢的个人理论。

• [时间积分策略]
  ◦ [mkoubaa] 强调了时间积分策略的多样性和复杂性，指出这更像是工程问题，需根据系统类型进行权衡和选择。

补充讨论：
• [历史背景与技术发展]
  ◦ [eesmith] 提到的1990年代数值计算书籍显示了技术发展的历史背景。
  ◦ [quantadev] 的个人理论虽未经证实，但反映了模拟中遇到的问题如何激发深入思考。

争议焦点：
• 在N-body问题模拟中，不同优化方法（如Jax与GPU结合，Barnes Hut算法）的适用场景和效果存在讨论，特别是对不同规模天体系统的效率影响。

总结：
评论主要围绕N-body问题模拟的技术实现、个人经验分享以及时间积分策略展开，讨论了各种优化方法的适用性和实际效果，并分享了不同时期的技术发展与个人感悟。

43944007.article_content:
5 steps to N-body simulation
This is a series of tutorials inspired by the course "CFD Python: 12 steps to Navier-Stokes".
The goal is to teach beginners how to write fast and clean N-body gravity simulations code in Python.
Although basic knowledge in Python and Calculus is assumed, everything is explained in detail so
beginners should be able to follow along. After completing this tutorial, you would be able to
write your own N-body simulation code in Python.
At the end of the tutorial, you are encouraged to make your own project related to N-body simulation.
How to use this tutorial?
The source code for the python scripts and the markdown files are available on
https://github.com/alvinng4/grav_sim/tree/main/5_steps_to_n_body_simulation
but I strongly recommend reading this tutorial on our website:
https://alvinng4.github.io/grav_sim/5_steps_to_n_body_simulation/
Snippets of the code will be shown as we progress, but you don't have to copy them one by one as the full code is always available at the end of each step. However,
I do recommend you to translate it into your own code in order to have a better understanding.
Contents
Step 1: Initial setup
Step 2: Gravity
Step 3: Your first N-body program
Step 4: Higher-order algorithms
Step 5: Adaptive time-stepping
Extra: Plotting and animation
Conclusion and Final Project
References
Lorena Barba and Gilbert Forsyth. CFD Python: the 12 steps to Navier-Stokes equations.
Journal of Open Source Education
, 2(16):21, 2019.
doi:10.21105/jose.00021
.
Javier Roa, Adrian S. Hamers, Maxwell X. Cai, and Nathan W. C. Leigh.
Moving Planets Around: An Introduction to N-Body Simulations Applied to Exoplanetary Systems
. MIT Press, 2020.
Richard L. Burden and J. Douglas Faires.
Numerical Analysis
. Cengage Learning, nineth edition, 2011.

data.title: Ex-UK Special Forces break silence on 'war crimes' by colleagues
data.author: tartoran
data.article_summary:
前英国特种部队成员首次公开指控同事在伊拉克和阿富汗犯下战争罪。这些老兵描述了目睹SAS成员杀害手无寸铁的平民，包括在阿富汗处决一名戴手铐的男孩。他们称，这种行为变得“ routine”（常规化），俘虏常常在被搜查、戴上手铐后遭枪杀，手铐随后被剪掉，武器被放置在尸体旁以伪造现场。皇家海军特种舟艇部队（SBS）也被首次指控参与了类似的处决行动。

这些指控涵盖超过十年的时期，远超目前英国公开调查的范围。一些老兵提到，部分士兵表现出严重的心理变态特征，行为野蛮且自认为不受惩罚。时任首相卡梅伦曾被警告有关特种部队在阿富汗杀害平民的指控。英国国防部表示全力支持正在进行的公开调查，并敦促相关老兵提供信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于西方国家（尤其是澳大利亚和英国）特种部队在战争中的不当行为及其背后的原因和影响，以及对战争罪行的责任追究和系统性问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **axus**：引用了BBC的文章，提到澳大利亚已经发布了关于其行为的报告，并指出只有举报人和另一名人员被审判和定罪。这表明对这类战争罪行的追责可能存在局限性。
• **moomin**：认为面对极端分子所憎恨的“自由”，西方必须表现得比他们更好，避免为他们提供下一代的招募素材。这暗示了道德优越性的必要性，以对抗极端主义。
• **huhkerrf**：反思在面对集体不当行为时，个人是否能做出正确选择，并指出特种部队文化中可能存在鼓励或忽视这些行为的因素。强调这不是为不当行为开脱，而是思考个人在极端环境下的行为选择。
• **rich_sasha**：补充了关于阿富汗特种部队被拒绝英国签证的报道，指出这使得他们无法在英国作证，导致在塔利班接管后出现了可预见的后果。这引发了对证人保护和国际责任的关注。
• **harddrivereque**：认为战争中的不当行为并不仅限于某国，而是普遍存在，例如关塔那摩的酷刑和欧洲的类似事件。指出系统的不完善和缺乏执行力是根本问题。
• **psunavy03**：讨论了特种部队中“坏分子”的问题，提出是否是由于选拔过程的问题，或者是因为长期战斗导致的“暴力疲劳”。质疑是否需要对军事人员的心理健康和战斗负荷设定限制。
• **WatchDog**：质疑为什么美国特种部队没有类似的战争罪行指控，是由于美国有更好的文化，还是因为缺乏问责。提到对某些军事人物的英雄化可能掩盖了他们的不当行为。
• **blotfaba**：讽刺西方国家多年来的战争罪行，并暗示这可能与“优等种族”的思维有关。
• **Yeul**：主张西方国家不应将公民送入战争的“黑暗之心”，提到塞尔维亚人将荷兰军官用作人体盾牌的例子，强调战争对个体的摧毁性影响。
• **croes** 和 **tiahura**：对战争罪行的普遍性和历史性提出看法，认为在缺乏背景信息的情况下难以判断特种部队的行为是否相对更残酷，并指出系统性改进的必要性，而非单纯依赖司法追责。

补充讨论：

43964885.article_content:
Ex-UK Special Forces break silence on 'war crimes' by colleagues
13 hours ago
Share
Save
Hannah O'Grady, Joel Gunter & Rory Tinman
BBC Panorama
Share
Save
A video compiled by UK Special Forces shows how members of one squadron kept count of their kills
Former members of UK Special Forces have broken years of silence to give BBC Panorama eyewitness accounts of alleged war crimes committed by colleagues in Iraq and Afghanistan.
Giving their accounts publicly for the first time, the veterans described seeing members of the SAS murder unarmed people in their sleep and execute handcuffed detainees, including children.
"They handcuffed a young boy and shot him," recalled one veteran who served with the SAS in Afghanistan. "He was clearly a child, not even close to fighting age."
Killing of detainees "became routine", the veteran said. "They'd search someone, handcuff them, then shoot them", before cutting off the plastic handcuffs used to restrain people and "planting a pistol" by the body, he said.
The new testimony includes allegations of war crimes stretching over more than a decade, far longer than the three years currently being examined by a judge-led public inquiry in the UK.
The SBS, the Royal Navy's elite special forces regiment, is also implicated for the first time in the most serious allegations - executions of unarmed and wounded people.
A veteran who served with the SBS said some troops had a "mob mentality", describing their behaviour on operations as "barbaric".
"I saw the quietest guys switch, show serious psychopathic traits," he said.  "They were lawless. They felt untouchable."
Special Forces were deployed to Afghanistan to protect British troops from Taliban fighters and bombmakers. The conflict was a deadly one for members of the UK's armed forces – 457 lost their lives and thousands more were wounded.
Asked by the BBC about the new eyewitness testimony, the Ministry of Defence said that it was "fully committed" to supporting the ongoing public inquiry into the alleged war crimes and that it urged all veterans with relevant information to come forward. It said that it was "not appropriate for the MoD to comment on allegations" which may be in the inquiry's scope.
'Psychotic murderers' in the regiment
The eyewitness testimony offers the most detailed public account of the killings to date from former members of UK Special Forces (UKSF), the umbrella group which contains the SAS, SBS and several supporting regiments.
The testimony, from more than 30 people who served with or alongside UK Special Forces, builds on years of reporting by BBC Panorama into allegations of extrajudicial killings by the SAS.
Panorama can also reveal for the first time that then Prime Minister David Cameron was repeatedly warned during his tenure that UK Special Forces were killing civilians in Afghanistan.
Speaking on condition of anonymity because of a de facto code of silence around special forces operations, the eyewitnesses told the BBC that the laws of war were being regularly and intentionally broken by the country's most elite regiments during operations in both Iraq and Afghanistan.
Those laws state that on such operations people can be deliberately killed only when they pose a direct threat to the lives of British troops or others. But members of the SAS and SBS were making their own rules, the eyewitnesses said.
"If a target had popped up on the list two or three times before, then we'd go in with the intention of killing them, there was no attempt to capture them," said one veteran who served with the SAS, referring to people who had been previously captured, questioned and then released.
"Sometimes we'd check we'd identified the target, confirm their ID, then shoot them," he said. "Often the squadron would just go and kill all the men they found there."
One witness who served with the SAS said that killing could become "an addictive thing to do" and that some members of the elite regiment were "intoxicated by that feeling" in Afghanistan. There were "lots of psychotic murderers", he said.
Getty Images
Then Prime Minister David Cameron (r) was made aware, by the then Afghan President Hamid Karzai (l), of allegations of civilian killings, the BBC has been told
"On some operations, the troop would go into guesthouse-type buildings and kill everyone there," he said. "They'd go in and shoot everyone sleeping there, on entry. It's not justified, killing people in their sleep."
A veteran who served with the SBS told the BBC that after bringing an area under control, assault teams would sweep through the area shooting anyone on the ground, checking the bodies and killing anyone left alive. "It was expected, not hidden. Everyone knew," he said.
Intentionally killing wounded people who do not pose a threat would be a clear breach of international law. But the SBS veteran told Panorama that wounded people were routinely killed. He described one operation during which a medic was treating someone who had been shot bu

前英国特种部队成员首次公开指控同事在伊拉克和阿富汗犯下战争罪。这些老兵描述了目睹SAS成员杀害手无寸铁的平民，包括在阿富汗处决一名戴手铐的男孩。他们称，这种行为变得“ routine”（常规化），俘虏常常在被搜查、戴上手铐后遭枪杀，手铐随后被剪掉，武器被放置在尸体旁以伪造现场。皇家海军特种舟艇部队（SBS）也被首次指控参与了类似的处决行动。

这些指控涵盖超过十年的时期，远超目前英国公开调查的范围。一些老兵提到，部分士兵表现出严重的心理变态特征，行为野蛮且自认为不受惩罚。时任首相卡梅伦曾被警告有关特种部队在阿富汗杀害平民的指控。英国国防部表示全力支持正在进行的公开调查，并敦促相关老兵提供信息。

data.title: Show HN: Lumoar – Free SOC 2 tool for SaaS startups
data.author: asdxrfx
data.article_summary: Lumoar提供免费工具帮助初创公司更快达到SOC 2合规要求。其免费 tier 包括引导式控制清单、政策模板生成器、证据管理及团队协作功能，无需信用卡即可使用。未来还将推出自动化证据收集、控制监控及集成等高级功能。该平台专为初创公司设计，帮助其迅速做好审计准备，并获得早期用户和合规专家的信赖。用户可以加入等待列表以获取更新和高级功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Lumoar平台的SOC2合规服务的使用体验、技术问题、合法性以及可信度的讨论。

不同观点：
• [reynaldi] 认为平台缺乏对SOC2的入门指导和教育内容，特别是对于不了解SOC2的用户来说，不清楚具体步骤。建议提供更多教育资源。
• [Oras] 提到作为初创公司面临的安全问卷、审计要求和昂贵工具的问题，并质疑Lumoar是否符合SOC2标准。
• [edoceo] 认为即使有了合规政策，仍然需要进行审计或回答安全问卷，合规专家仍然会要求复杂的流程。
• [kristel100] 强调SOC2准备工作对小团队来说非常艰难，建议提供预检清单和集成工具，对自动化程度表示关注。
• [reconnecting] 强调在提供法律相关服务之前，应确保自身合规，指出Lumoar缺少明确的服务条款页面。
• [davsti4] 报告了注册时遇到的技术问题，浏览器控制台显示CORS政策阻止了访问。
• [throw03172019] 对“免费SOC-2”平台持怀疑态度，认为通常有隐藏的陷阱，询问Lumoar的陷阱是什么。
• [wnolens] 对其他SOC2平台的成本感到好奇，但指出Lumoar工具在加载时出现错误，无法正常使用。
• [GiorgioG] 质疑该帖是否是垃圾邮件，因为原帖者此前从未发帖。
• [java-man] 批评网站在首次使用缩写时没有解释，认为这是不合规的表现。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Lumoar平台的SOC2合规性和实际可用性。用户对平台的功能、技术实现和透明度提出质疑。
• 技术问题（如CORS政策和加载错误）影响了用户体验，进一步加剧了对平台可靠性的怀疑。
• 用户对平台的教育资源和指导步骤有需求，特别是针对不熟悉SOC2的用户，这可能是平台改进的一个方向。
• 对“免费SOC-2”概念的怀疑反映了用户对潜在隐藏费用的担忧。
• 对合法性和合规性的关注，尤其是服务条款的缺失，是用户关心的另一个重要问题。

总体而言，评论反映了用户对Lumoar平台的多方面担忧，包括技术实现、教育资源、合规性和透明度。

data.author: andreeamiclaus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕本地语音助手、Siri的局限性以及LLM（大型语言模型）在移动设备上应用的可行性展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• [支持本地语音助手] worldsayshi对构建本地语音助手表示兴趣，但指出在使用小型Whisper模型时效果不佳，可能与硬件或麦克风质量有关。
• [支持本地语音助手] kristel100认为这是正确的方向，关注在普通硬件上的性能瓶颈，期待进一步发展。
• [需求简单解决方案] catapart希望有一个可以直接下载使用的应用程序，但同时感谢指南提供了所需的信息来自己构建。
• [质疑LLM文章] rrr_oh_man质疑为何使用LLM撰写文章，对文章形式提出疑问。
• [关注模型运行效果] thedeep_mind关注模型是否能在iPhone上成功运行，提到其孩子在设备上运行其他模型的经验。
• [提到Siri的本地功能] jtr1指出Siri现在已经可以在本地处理一些命令，并提供了实验方法。
• [质疑苹果的数据处理] cadamsdotcom质疑苹果为何不根据数据硬编码常用命令的处理程序。
• [赞赏项目] mrcwinn对项目表示赞赏。
• [质疑苹果的限制] mystified5016质疑苹果是否允许用户替换Siri，并提到安卓系统上非Google助手的限制问题。
• [期待GPT手机] paul7986表达了对OpenAI和微软合作推出GPT手机的期待，对iPhone的现状感到不满。
• [呼吁社区替代方案] caust1c呼吁社区开发替代Siri的方案，表示如果iPhone权限允许或有变通方法，年底可能会看到社区替代方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Siri的功能局限性和苹果的系统限制，用户对现有语音助手的不满和对更好解决方案的期待。
• 讨论中多次提到模型在普通硬件上的性能和运行效果，特别是iPhone上的用户体验。
• 对LLM在移动设备上应用的可行性及性能的关注，以及对开源社区解决方案的期待。

data.author: cantaloupe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何为博客文章或其他内容拟定标题。作者建议将标题视为“分类器”，目标是吸引合适的受众点击，同时避免吸引不合适的受众导致负面反馈。好的标题应向目标读者传递强烈信号，确保那些会喜欢内容的人点击，而避免让不喜欢的人浪费时间。作者强调，标题不仅要反映主题，还要体现风格和语气。对于已有名气的作者，标题选择可能更灵活，但对于大多数人，模仿这种策略并不明智。此外，直接将结论放入标题可能引发误解和争议，需谨慎使用。最后，作者提到技术并未解决内容传播问题，社交媒体实际上限制了内容的传播。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：标题设计及其在不同平台上的影响

不同观点：
• [boznz] 认为点击诱饵型标题（如"所有最好的程序员都知道这个..."或"突破可能使核聚变成现实..."）无论内容如何，都会被直接忽略。他希望有办法屏蔽这些标题，因为它们往往出现在YouTube或Reddit的首页。作为作者，他也指出标题或封面图片如果与读者期望不符，可能会导致差评，进而影响算法推荐。

• [tibbar] 认为在Hacker News上，好的标题比内容更重要。一个能引发讨论的标题更容易获得关注和上前页。他指出，如果标题能引发读者联想他们想讨论的相关话题，那么即便内容不足，标题本身也能带来高参与度。

• [sam_lowry_] 基于多年管理社区网站和研究标题的经验，分享了多种标题优化技巧，包括使用预过滤机制、自动通知修改、A/B测试等。最终，他选择取消标题，直接从正文前几句话生成标题，以此强迫用户更深入地思考内容。

• [MattBearman] 提到其YouTuber使用非传统标题模式（如"隔热你的露营车，或只是看着我做"），这种标题风格独特且引人注意。

• [billyp-rva] 认为社交媒体平台通过优化参与度，故意将用户留在平台内，而不是让用户轻易访问外部内容。这种做法导致标题和链接的呈现受到限制。

• [andy99] 对"我做了一个..."这种标题前缀表示不满，认为这种标题过于自我中心，没有突出作品本身。

• [eCa] 强调制作高质量内容比迎合多数人喜好更重要，反对为了吸引点击而妥协内容质量。

• [cosmicgadget] 分享其标题创作流程：先写内容，再根据内容创建标题，并依靠简短描述提供清晰的内容预览。

• [turnsout] 认为带有"或 whatever"这种轻松语气的标题更能吸引人点击，但警告不要滥用这种技巧。

• [amw-zero] 喜欢随意命名内容，认为只要内容好，人们就会找到它，不太在意标题的精确性。

• [paulpauper] 认为负面关注不一定是坏事，有些人会因为反对内容而分享，从而带来更多流量和读者。

补充讨论：
• 不同平台对标题的依赖程度和优化策略存在差异，如YouTube、Reddit、Hacker News等。
• 标题在吸引点击和内容真实性之间的平衡是一个争议焦点，部分人认为点击诱饵标题有害，而另一些人则认为这是有效的策略。
• 自动生成标题和预过滤机制在管理标题质量中的应用和效果被提及，展示了技术在标题优化中的作用。
• 讨论中涉及SEO（搜索引擎优化）和算法推荐对内容可见性的影响，强调标题在这些系统中的重要性。

How to title your blog post or whatever
How to title your blog post or whatever
May 2025
Comments at
substack
,
lemmy
.
So you’ve made a thing. I’ll pretend it’s a blog post, though it doesn’t really matter. If people read your thing, some would like it, and some wouldn’t.
You should try to make a good thing, that many people would like. That presents certain challenges. But our subject today is only how to give your thing a
title
.
My advice is: Think of the title as “classifier”.
When people see the title, some are likely to click on it and some won’t. Abstractly speaking, the title adds a second dimension to the above figure:
A title has two goals. First, think of all the people in the world who, if they clicked on your thing, would finish it and love it. Ideally, those people would click. That is, you want there to be people in the like + click region:
Other people will hate your thing. It’s fine, some people hate everything. But if they click on your thing, they’ll be annoyed and tell everyone you are dumb and bad. You don’t want that. So you
don’t
want people in the hate + click region.
I find it helpful to think about all title-related issues from this perspective.
Everyone is deluged with content. Few people will
hate
your thing, because very few will care enough to have any feelings about it at all.
The good news is that it’s a big world and none of us are that unique. If you make a thing that
you
would love, then I guarantee you at least 0.0001% of other people would love it too. That’s still 8000 people! The problem is finding them.
That’s hard. Because—you don’t like most things, right? So you start with a strong prior that most things are bad (for you). Life is short, so you only click on things when there’s a very strong signal they’ll be good (for you).
Say you write a post about concrete. Should you call it, “My favorite concrete pozzolanic admixtures”, even though 99.9% of people have no idea what pozzolanic means? Well, think of the people who’d actually like your thing. Do
they
know? If so, use “pozzolanic”. That gives a strong signal to Concrete People: “Hey! This is for you! And you
know
I’m not lying about that, because I’ve driven away all the noobs.”
So ideally you’re aiming for something like this:
Be careful imitating famous people. If Barack Obama made a thing called “Thoughts on blockchain”, everyone would read it, because the implicit title is “Thoughts on blockchain,
by Barack Goddamn Obama
”. Most of the titles you see probably come from people who have some kind of established “brand”. If you don’t have that, you probably don’t want to choose the same kind of titles.
The title isn’t just about the subject. I called this post, “How to title your blog post
or whatever
” partly because I hope some of this applies to other things beyond blog posts. But mostly I did that because it signals that my style is breezy and informal. I think people really underrate this.
Some people choose clever punny titles. If you have a big audience that reads all your things, then your title doesn’t need to be a good classifier. I’m not in that situation, but I sometimes find a pun so amusing that I can’t resist.
“Fahren-height”
was worth it.
“Taste games”
was not.
Traditional advice says that you should put your main “message” in the title. I have mixed feelings about that. On the one hand, it provides a lot of signal. On the other hand, it seems to get people’s hackles up. The world is full of bad things that basically pick a conclusion and ignore or distort all conflicting evidence. If you’re attempting to be fair or nuanced, putting your conclusion in the title might signal that you’re going to be a typical biased/bad thing. It will
definitely
lead to lots of comments “refuting” you from people who didn’t read your thing.
Putting your conclusion in the title may also ruin your “story”. Though you should ask: Do the people who’d like your thing really care about your story?
A difficult case is things that create new “labels”. Sometimes there’s an idea floating around, and we need someone to make a canonical thing with a Name. To serve that role, the thing’s title needs to be that name. This presents a trade-off. A post titled
“The Waluigi Effect”
is great for people who want to know what that is, but terrible for everyone else.
For the best
title
ever I nominate,
“I’m worried about Chicago”
. It doesn’t look fancy, but do you see how elegantly it balances all the above issues?
You’d think that, by 2025, technology would have solved the problem of things getting to people. I think it’s the opposite. Social media is optimized to keep people engaged and does not want people leaving the walled garden. Openly prohibiting links would cause a revolt, so instead they go as close as people will tolerate. Which, it turns out, is pretty close.
Boring titles are OK. I know that no one will click on
“Lin

data.title: Show HN: The missing inbox for GitHub pull requests
data.author: pvcnt
data.article_summary: Mergeable 是一个为 GitHub 拉取请求（pull requests）提供更好管理的工具。其主要功能包括：通过灵活的搜索查询将拉取请求组织成不同部分，数据存储在浏览器本地；支持键盘快捷键快速导航；可连接多个 GitHub 实例，包括 GitHub Enterprise；突出显示需要您操作的请求。该工具无需安装任何 GitHub 应用程序，并提供公共实例供使用，同时也支持自托管。文档和源码可在其官网和 GitHub 仓库中找到，项目基于 PnPM、Turborepo 和 Vite 构建，本地运行命令为 `pnpm run dev`。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub项目管理工具及其功能完善性

不同观点：
• Jerrygoyal认为GitHub的项目功能已经解决了他遇到的问题，暗示GitHub现有工具能有效满足项目管理需求。
• Rokkamokka支持GitHub项目工具，但也提到他们在工作中自行开发了一个类似的仪表板工具，用来跟踪团队的审查状态，暗示GitHub缺乏类似的内置功能是个错失的机会。
• Dvektor对该想法表示赞同，并指出当前公共实例上存在TLS证书问题，显示出对功能实现细节的关注，同时表示会持续关注项目进展。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了自行开发工具的实践，反映出部分用户可能需要更个性化的功能，而GitHub默认功能未能完全满足这些需求。
• 存在技术问题（如TLS证书问题）也被提及，表明用户对工具的稳定性和可用性有一定期望。
• 总体上，争议焦点在于GitHub是否充分提供了用户所需的项目管理和跟踪功能，部分用户认为有改进空间。

Mergeable
Mergeable is a better inbox for GitHub pull requests.
Features
Mergeable provides the following features:
Organize pull requests into sections, defined by flexible search queries.
Data is all stored locally, in the browser storage.
Keyboard shortcuts allow to navigate quickly.
Connect to multiple GitHub instances, including GitHub Enterprise.
Attention set, highlighting pull requests for which it is your turn to act.
Does not require any GitHub app to be installed.
Public instance
You can use the public instance hosted at
https://app.usemergeable.dev
Documentation
Documentation is available at
https://www.usemergeable.dev
It includes a user guide and instructions to self-host your own instance.
Run locally
This project is built using
PnPM
,
Turborepo
and
Vite
.
It can be started locally with the following command:
pnpm run dev

主要讨论点：大龄技术人员在就业市场中面临的挑战及应对策略，特别是在AI和经济变化的背景下。

不同观点：
• **改名策略**：[hackingonempty] 建议改用更常见的名字如"Shawn Kay"来避免因名字特别而被淘汰，等到HR流程时再使用 legal name。这个建议基于名字可能带来的潜在偏见。

• **经济与社会变化**：[Havoc] 认为就业困难不仅仅是AI取代岗位的问题，而是整体经济环境变化的结果，尤其是零利率政策的结束导致很多公司不再招聘。

• **地域与行业建议**：[ecshafer] 建议专注于学习C, C++, Java，并在当地寻找工作机会，尤其是在国防行业，而非只关注web开发工作。

• **远程工作与市场竞争**：[uberman] 指出选择居住在农村地区和坚持远程工作可能增加了就业难度，建议重新发布AI相关内容以吸引关注。

• **自主创业与技能转型**：[dexterlagan] 分享个人经验，建议从为他人工作转向自主创业和实现个人想法，以应对就业市场的变化。

• **技能与市场需求匹配**：[speedbird] 强调需要调整自己以符合市场需求，包括可能接受薪资下降或工作条件的变化，并建议与业内信任的人讨论。

• **国际对比与职业选择**：[Padriac] 提到在澳大利亚，军事技术岗位待遇优厚且正在招聘，建议考虑相关职业。

• **技术过时问题**：[Arnt] 指出只会单一语言如PHP的开发人员面临过时风险，类似于多年前的Perl开发者。

补充讨论：
• **系统脆弱性与经济转型**：[RainyDayTmrw] 和 [tetris11] 讨论了当前社会和经济系统的脆弱性，以及经济转型过程中可能出现的失业问题和应对策略。

• **同理心与评论动机**：[1attice] 提醒评论者在发表意见时要保持同理心，并反思自己评论的动机和潜在的心理防御机制。

• **政策与社会支持**：[adamc] 提到当前缺乏有效的社会支持和政策解决方案，对未来感到担忧。

争议焦点：
• 就业市场变化的主要原因：是AI取代岗位还是整体经济环境的变化。
• 改名策略的有效性和伦理问题：是否应通过改名来规避偏见。
• 远程工作的可行性与市场竞争力：在当前环境下是否应坚持远程工作。

data.title: Loko Scheme, an optimizing, bare-metal Scheme compiler
data.author: sph
data.article_summary: Loko Scheme是一个优化Scheme编译器，支持R6RS和R7RS Scheme语言，基于Concurrent ML实现并发。它可以交叉编译到Linux/amd64、NetBSD/amd64和裸机环境，性能良好。提供源码下载和多种安装方式（Arch Linux AUR、GNU Guix、Docker），还提供可启动的硬盘镜像。该编译器具备一定的硬件支持，包括网络、磁盘、视频、串行端口、PS/2和USB等驱动，适用于构建并发应用、系统研究和裸机实验等。项目采用EUPL-1.2或更高版本许可，并提供开发者手册。Bug报告和支持可通过邮件或IRC获取。

43964200.article_content:
scheme.fail
Welcome to the home of Loko Scheme, an optimizing Scheme compiler!
Batteries on the side (
Akku.scm
).
Cross-compiles to Linux/amd64, NetBSD/amd64 and bare metal amd64.
Speaks R6RS Scheme natively and R7RS Scheme as a second language.
Concurrency based on Concurrent ML.
Compiled code with
reasonable performance
.
Screenshots
Download
Loko is available from git:
git clone https://scheme.fail/git/loko.git/
For automated work and for browsing the repository, please use
the mirror on GitLab.
loko-0.12.1.tar.gz
(
sig
) - 2023-09-26
All releases
Loko Scheme is also available from these package repositories:
Arch Linux AUR
GNU Guix
guix install loko-scheme
Docker
docker pull weinholt/loko
docker run --rm -it weinholt/loko
A
bootable hard drive image
is available. Give it a supported machine with ≥1GB RAM and you get a REPL.
🄯 License
Loko Scheme is licensed under the
EUPL-1.2-or-later.
This is a copyleft license with a SaaS clause, but which
works well for a compiler.
Documentation
The Loko Scheme Developer's Manual
[
PDF
].
Hype-free zone
Loko Scheme is a niche compiler. It is not trying to replace any other compiler. Some ideas for what you can do with it:
Build statically linked concurrent applications.
Work on a systems-level language just for fun.
Systems research.
Unikernel experiments.
Lock-free kernel experiments.
Bare metal Scheme experiments.
New userspace-to-kernel interfaces.
Port to other operating system kernels (FreeBSD, etc).
Fight the status quo.
Loko Scheme comes with some limited hardware support:
Networking (rtl8169, rtl8139, eepro100, virtio-net, tuntap) with TCP/IP support.
Disk (ATA, ATAPI, SCSI, IDE, AHCI) drivers with FAT file system support.
Video (VESA VBE, Bochs graphics).
Serial (8250 UART).
PS/2 keyboard and mouse support.
USB stack with UHCI, HID & mass storage support.
Loko Scheme works on real hardware, but it currently needs a legacy PIC, so the most modern machines will likely not be able to run it yet.
The drivers are used in the bootable disk image.
Bugs
Please report bugs by email. Bring any questions you may have to comp.lang.scheme or
#loko on irc.libera.chat
.
Gwen Weinholt <git () weinholt.se>

data.title: Air Traffic Control
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了空中交通管制的历史和发展，特别关注其技术、管理和社交方面的复杂性。文章指出，空中交通管制的衰退源于数十年的投资不足、国防工业体系的掌控、联邦航空管理局的管理不善以及里根镇压PATCO罢工的长期影响。文章回顾了早期航空时代，由于飞机数量少且技术有限，空中交通管制需求不高，主要通过旗帜和信号灯指挥飞机降落。第一次世界大战推动了航空无线电的发展，使得地面控制成为可能。战后，民用航空迅速发展，商业航空公司开始使用无线电进行调度和天气咨询，邮政部门的航空邮件服务也为现代民航奠定了基础。邮政合同不仅资助了航空业，还促成了多家大型航空公司的成长。

>>> 2025-05-11 air traffic control (
PDF
)
Air traffic control has been in the news lately, on account of my country's
declining ability to do it. Well, that's a long-term trend, resulting from
decades of under-investment, severe capture by our increasingly incompetent
defense-industrial complex, no small degree of management incompetence in the
FAA, and long-lasting effects of Reagan crushing the PATCO strike. But that's
just my opinion, you know, maybe airplanes got too woke. In any case, it's an
interesting time to consider how
weird
parts of air traffic control are. The
technical, administrative, and social aspects of ATC all seem two notches more
complicated than you would expect. ATC is heavily influenced by its peculiar
and often accidental development, a product of necessity that perpetually
trails behind the need, and a beneficiary of hand-me-down military practices
and technology.
Aviation Radio
In the early days of aviation, there was little need for ATC---there just
weren't many planes, and technology didn't allow ground-based controllers to do
much of value. There was some use of flags and signal lights to clear aircraft
to land, but for the most part ATC had to wait for the development of aviation
radio. The impetus for that work came mostly from the First World War.
Here we have to note that the history of aviation is very closely intertwined
with the history of warfare. Aviation technology has always rapidly advanced
during major conflicts, and as we will see, ATC is no exception.
By 1913, the US Army Signal Corps was experimenting with the use of radio to
communicate with aircraft. This was pretty early in radio technology, and the
aircraft radios were huge and awkward to operate, but it was also early in
aviation and "huge and awkward to operate" could be similarly applied to the
aircraft of the day. Even so, radio had obvious potential in aviation. The
first military application for aircraft  was reconnaissance. Pilots could fly
past the front to find artillery positions and otherwise provide useful
information, and then return with maps. Well, even better than returning with a
map was providing the information in real-time, and by the end of the war
medium-frequency AM radios were well developed for aircraft.
Radios in aircraft lead naturally to another wartime innovation: ground
control. Military personnel on the ground used radio to coordinate the
schedules and routes of reconnaissance planes, and later to inform on the
positions of fighters and other enemy assets. Without any real way to know
where the planes were, this was all pretty primitive, but it set the basic
pattern that people on the ground could keep track of aircraft and provide
useful information.
Post-war, civil aviation rapidly advanced. The early 1920s saw numerous
commercial airlines adopting radio, mostly for business purposes like schedule
coordination. Once you were in contact with someone on the ground, though, it
was only logical to ask about weather and conditions. Many of our modern
practices like weather briefings, flight plans, and route clearances originated
as more or less formal practices within individual airlines.
Air Mail
The government was not left out of the action. The Post Office operated what
may have been the largest commercial aviation operation in the world during the
early 1920s, in the form of Air Mail. The Post Office itself did not have any
aircraft; all of the flying was contracted out---initially to the Army Air
Service, and later to a long list of regional airlines. Air Mail was considered
a high priority by the Post Office and proved very popular with the public.
When the transcontinental route began proper operation in 1920, it became
possible to get a letter from New York City to San Francisco in just 33 hours
by transferring it between airplanes in a nearly non-stop relay race.
The Post Office's largesse in contracting the service to private operators
provided not only the funding but the very motivation for much of our modern
aviation industry. Air travel was not very popular at the time, being loud and
uncomfortable, but the mail didn't complain. The many contract mail carriers of
the 1920s grew and consolidated into what are now some of the United States'
largest companies. For around a decade, the Post Office almost singlehandedly
bankrolled civil aviation, and passengers were a side hustle [1].
Air mail ambition was not only of economic benefit. Air mail routes were often
longer and more challenging than commercial passenger routes. Transcontinental
service required regular flights through sparsely populated parts of the
interior, challenging the navigation technology of the time and making rescue
of downed pilots a major concern. Notably, air mail operators did far more
nighttime flying than any other commercial aviation in the 1920s. The post
office became the government's de facto technical leader in civil aviation.

data.title: Understanding LucasArts' iMUSE System
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章（或页面）内容简短，提到与"meshula"和"LabMidi"相关的项目。页面显示项目是公开的，但需要登录才能更改通知设置。当前项目有4次被 fork，并获得了54个星标（Star）。文章主要是关于一个代码库或项目的简要状态信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iMUSE系统的特点、应用及其在游戏音乐中的影响

不同观点：
• [kjander79] 认为iMUSE系统的无缝音乐过渡非常出色，比如在《X-Wing》中，当帝国战舰出现时，音乐会自然切换到《帝国进行曲》。然而，他也指出基于CD音频的游戏在音乐切换时显得生硬，并质疑这是否是系统本身的局限性。他还提出，现代技术可以通过虚拟MIDI系统实现类似效果。

• [gmueckl] 强调了创造适用于iMUSE系统的内容的工具和过程的重要性，认为技术系统对创意人员的友好性是一个重大挑战。他表示，LucasArts在这方面做得很好，并对创作过程表示好奇。

• [riotnrrd] 分享了与iMUSE开发者Nick共事的个人经历，称赞其为人与专业能力，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• [jesusgm] 通过对比《Monkey Island》两代游戏的音乐体验，突出了iMUSE系统在游戏沉浸感方面的提升，强调实际体验的重要性。

• [Dwedit] 提到《Banjo-Kazooie》使用了简单的动态音乐实现方法，通过额外音轨的淡入淡出实现动态音乐，指出这种方法虽然简单但常用。

• [i_v] 探讨了音乐制作作为游戏引擎一部分的长期兴趣，提到了《Elder Scrolls Online》和AI生成音乐的例子，思考这种技术在游戏叙事和互动中的未来潜力。

补充讨论：
• [Lightkey] 提到了ScummVM与iMUSE相关的法律问题，指出iMUSE曾拥有专利，ScummVM团队需小心处理。同时，对开发者Nick认可非官方实现表示赞赏。

争议焦点：
• iMUSE系统在CD音频游戏中的局限性及其是否为技术限制所致，是[kjander79]提出的主要争议点。
• 动态音乐实现的复杂性与简单方法之间的对比，是[Dwedit]和[kjander79]讨论的一个潜在争议点。

data.title: Wtfis: Passive hostname, domain and IP lookup tool for non-robots
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
"wtfis" 是一个被动的主机名、域名和IP查询工具，专为人类易读而设计。它通过多个OSINT服务收集信息，并尽量减少API调用以避免达到免费 tier 的限额。主要功能包括：

1. 使用 Virustotal 作为主要信息源，获取主机名、IP的最新分析数据、信誉评分、流行度排名和分类等。
2. 可选使用 IP2Whois 获取更高质量的 whois 数据。
3. 使用 IPWhois 获取IP的地理位置和ASN信息。
4. 通过 Shodan 获取开放端口、操作系统和标签等信息。
5. 使用 Greynoise 判断IP是否为常规扫描或商业应用。
6. 通过 URLhaus 和 AbuseIPDB 查询是否为恶意URL或IP。

安装通过 `pip install wtfis` 或 `brew install wtfis`，配置需要设置多个API密钥。使用命令 `wtfis [选项] 实体` 查询信息。
data.comments_summary:

• DavideNL指出该工具需要Virustotal API密钥，因此可能存在隐私问题，暗示这并不完全符合隐私友好的标准。

wtfis
Passive hostname, domain and IP lookup tool for non-robots
WTF is it?
wtfis
is a commandline tool that gathers information about a domain, FQDN or IP address using various OSINT services. Unlike other tools of its kind, it's built specifically for human consumption, providing results that are pretty (YMMV) and easy to read and understand.
This tool assumes that you are using free tier / community level accounts, and so makes as few API calls as possible to minimize hitting quotas and rate limits.
The project name is a play on "whois".
Data Sources
Service
Used in lookup
Required
Free Tier
Virustotal
All
Yes
Yes
IP2Whois
Domain/FQDN
No
Yes
IPWhois
IP address
No
Yes (no signup)
Shodan
IP address
No
No
Greynoise
IP address
No
Yes
URLhaus
All
No
Yes (no signup)
AbuseIPDB
IP address
No
Yes
Virustotal
The primary source of information. Retrieves:
Hostname (FQDN), domain or IP
Latest analysis stats with vendor detail
Reputation score (based on VT community votes)
Popularity ranks (Alexa, Cisco Umbrella, etc.) (FQDN and domain only)
Categories (assigned by different vendors)
Resolutions
(FQDN and domain only)
Last n IP addresses (default: 3, max: 10)
Latest analysis stats of each IP above
Whois
Fallback only: if IP2Whois creds are not available
Various whois data about the domain itself
IP2Whois
Optionally used if creds are provided. Retrieves:
Whois
Various whois data about the domain itself
IP2Whois is recommended over Virustotal for whois data for a couple of reasons:
VT whois data format is less consistent
IP2Whois whois data tends to be of better quality than VT. Also, VT's registrant data is apparently
anonymized
.
You can save one VT API call by offloading to IP2Whois.
IPWhois
Default Geolocation and ASN lookup source for IP addresses. Retrieves:
ASN, Org, ISP and Geolocation
IPWhois should not be confused with IP2Whois, which provides domain Whois data.
Shodan
GETs data from the
/shodan/host/{ip}
endpoint (see
doc
). For each IP, retrieves:
List of open ports and services
Operating system (if available)
Tags (assigned by Shodan)
Greynoise
Using Greynoise's
community API
, wtfis will show whether an IP is in one of Greynoise's datasets:
Noise
: IP has been seen regularly scanning the Internet
RIOT
: IP belongs to a common business application (e.g. Microsoft O365, Google Workspace, Slack)
More information about the datasets
here
.
In addition, the API also returns Greynoise's
classification
of an IP (if available). Possible values are
benign
,
malicious
, and
unknown
.
URLhaus
URLhaus
is a crowd-sourced database of reported malicious URLs. This enrichment provides insight on whether the queried hostname or IP is being or was used for malware distribution via HTTP or HTTPS. Data that is provided include:
Count of currently online and total malware URLs
Whether the hostname or IP is currently in the
DNSBL
and
SURBL
public blocklists
All tags that have been assigned to the URL throughout its history in the URLhaus database
AbuseIPDB
AbuseIPDB
is a crowd-sourced database of reported malicious IP addresses. Through its API wtfis shows:
Abuse confidence score (0-100)
Number of reports
Install
$ pip install wtfis
To install via
conda
(from conda-forge), see
wtfis-feedstock
.
To install via
brew
:
brew install wtfis
Setup
wtfis uses these environment variables:
VT_API_KEY
(required) - Virustotal API key
IP2WHOIS_API_KEY
(optional) - IP2WHOIS API key
SHODAN_API_KEY
(optional) - Shodan API key
GREYNOISE_API_KEY
(optional) - Greynoise API key
ABUSEIPDB_API_KEY
(optional) - AbuseIPDB API key
WTFIS_DEFAULTS
(optional) - Default arguments
Set these using your own method.
Alternatively, create a file in your home directory
~/.env.wtfis
with the above declarations. See
.env.wtfis.example
for a template.
NOTE: Don't forget to
chmod 400
the file!
Usage
usage: wtfis [-h] [-m N] [-s] [-g] [-a] [-u] [-n] [-1] [-V] entity
positional arguments:
entity                Hostname, domain or IP
optional arguments:
-h, --help            show this help message and exit
-m N, --max-resolutions N
Maximum number of resolutions to show (default: 3)
-s, --use-shodan      Use Shodan to enrich IPs
-g, --use-greynoise   Enable Greynoise for IPs
-a, --use-abuseipdb   Enable AbuseIPDB for IPs
-u, -

data.title: The Beam
data.author: Alupis
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了Elixir编程语言的基础——Erlang虚拟机（BEAM）。文章解释了Erlang语言的历史、特点及其生态系统，包括其并发处理、容错机制和高效的资源利用。Erlang由Joe Armstrong等人在1980年代中期创建，最初用于电信系统，现已成为一种通用的开源语言。其虚拟机BEAM负责执行Erlang代码，管理并发进程，并通过异步消息传递实现进程间通信，确保系统的高可用性和可扩展性。Elixir作为基于BEAM的编程语言，继承了这些优点，并能使用Erlang的库和OTP框架。文章还提供了进一步了解Erlang和Elixir资源的链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Erlang与BEAM虚拟机的优点及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• schultzer认为Erlang的模式匹配非常适合用于编写词法分析器、解析器和编译器，并提到Elixir的宏和符号可以嵌入其他语言如SQL和Zig，提供了很大的灵活性。
• idahoduncan分享了一个关于Erlang运行时历史的小知识，指出早期版本的Erlang运行时是在Strand中实现的，这在Erlang历史讨论中不常被提及。
• kristel100对BEAM的持久生命力和其在现代异步编程中的相关性表示赞赏，认为其并发模型独特且有效。

补充讨论：
• xelxebar表示研究BEAM在其任务列表中，对BEAM的任务并行性非常感兴趣，并希望了解选择细粒度任务并行性与数据并行性架构的影响。
• troupo认为关于BEAM的文章往往缺乏对其优点的深入分析，建议提供更多具体原因来说明为什么BEAM是好的，并提供了一个参考链接。
• monkfish328表示喜欢BEAM，但希望Elixir能内置静态类型。

Sign up for our quarterly newsletter
Keep up to date with the latest news, best practice ideas and exclusive offers. Don’t miss out. Sign up here.
Welcome to the first chapter of the “Elixir, 7 Steps to Start Your Journey” series. In my previous post, I
discussed my journey
with the programming language.
In this chapter, we will discuss the Erlang Virtual Machine, the BEAM.
To understand why
the Elixir programming language is so powerful and reliable, we must understand its foundations,
which means talking about Erlang.
Elixir runs on the
Erlang Virtual Machine
and inherits many of its virtues. In this post, you will learn a little about the history of Erlang, the objective with which it was initially created, and why it is fundamental for Elixir.
What is Erlang?
Erlang as a programming language
Erlang
is a programming language created in the mid-1980s by Joe Armstrong, Robert Virding, and Mike Williams at the Ericsson Computer Science Laboratory. Initially designed for telecommunications, it is now a general-purpose language. It was influenced by other programming languages, such as ML and Prolog, and was released as open-source in 1998.
Erlang was designed with distributed, fault-tolerant, massively concurrent, and soft real-time systems in mind, making it an excellent choice for today’s systems. Most are looking for these features, in addition to having confidence in Erlang’s history in productive systems.
Some of the characteristics of this programming language are:
It is a declarative language, which means it is based on the principle of describing
what
should be calculated instead of
how
.
Pattern matching
is possible at a high level and also on bit sequences.
Functions
in Erlang are first-class data.
Erlang as the development ecosystem
Up to this point, we have referred to Erlang as the programming language; however, it should be noted that Erlang can also refer to an entire development ecosystem that is made up of:
The Erlang programming language
The framework OTP
A series of tools and
The virtual machine, BEAM
Erlang, as an ecosystem, was explicitly created to support highly available systems, which provide service even when errors or unexpected circumstances occur, and this is due to many of the characteristics of its virtual machine (VM).
So, although Erlang as a programming language is pretty cool on its own, the real magic happens when all the ecosystem elements are combined: the programming language, libraries, OTP, and the virtual machine.
If you want to know more about the history of Erlang, the list of resources below will be very helpful.
Resources
Keynote: History of philosophy of Erlang with its creators | Code BEAM V America 2021
100 Years of Erlang | Quinn Wilton | Code BEAM America 2021
Robert Virding – Hitchhiker’s Tour of the BEAM
A brief introduction to BEAM
Erlang Virtual Machine, BEAM
The Erlang Virtual Machine, known as the
BEAM
, runs as an operating system process and is responsible for executing the Erlang code. It is also responsible for creating, scheduling, and managing Erlang processes, which are the fundamental basis of concurrency.
Thanks to the BEAM schedulers, these processes can be executed in the most efficient way possible, allowing the system to be highly
scalable
. The processes do not share memory; they communicate through asynchronous message passing. This mechanism is the foundation for a system’s
fault tolerance
. As they are entirely isolated, the other system processes will not be affected if an error occurs in one of them.
The BEAM is also responsible for parallelizing your concurrent Erlang programs, making the most of a machine’s resources. Initially, the virtual machine model was a single-run queue. However, it evolved into a run queue for each available processor, ensuring no bottlenecks and that Erlang programs work correctly on any system, regardless of the number of machine cores.
Another characteristic is that storage management is automated. Garbage collection is implemented per process, which allows a system’s response time to always remain in the order of milliseconds without performance degradation.
And lastly, one of my favourite features is error detection. The virtual machine provides all the elements necessary for efficient error detection and handling, thus promoting an always-available system regardless of failures.
In summary, the BEAM is responsible for the scalability, distribution, and responsiveness of a system:
Manages the concurrency of it.
It has a mechanism for error detection and handling.
Make the most of the computer’s resources.
If you’d like to learn more about the duo that is Erlang and Elixir, check out the
“What is Elixir”
post.
Elixir in the BEAM
Like Erlang, Elixir was also influenced by other programming languages, including Erlang itself. Its code runs on the Erlang Virtual Machine, which means it takes advantage of all its features and can use all the Erlang libraries and the
OTP framework
.

主要讨论点：对现代电子设备、软件和经济模式的看法

不同观点：
• [Animats] 认为电子设备的巅峰时期已经过去，特别是1990年代的电子玩具时代，因为现在一切都集成到了智能手机中。当时的电子设备缺乏标准化，如电压、电流、极性和插头尺寸等。
• [haxton] 提出“一次性软件”的概念，认为与其寻找他人生成的平庸LLM软件，不如自己生成适合自己的软件，且成本和便捷性相近。

• [Zak] 强调电池应可由用户自行更换，大多数应采用标准化的电池类型，尽管某些设备因外形限制难以实现。
• [Havoc] 认为AI模型也像是一时的潮流，每个新模型都会在一周内成为热门，直到新的东西出现。
• [slt2021] 提到“javascript框架”的快速更替现象，并认为LLM会加速这种趋势。
• [eikenberry] 认为这与“vibe coding”非常相似。
• [tropicalfruit] 提出“scroll based memory”概念，描述人们在滑动过去后容易忘记某些信息的现象。
• [roughly] 认为当前的电子垃圾和污染问题源于我们未认识到地球是一个有限、封闭的系统，误以为垃圾和污染会流向“其他地方”。
• [nahhypedit] 认为当前经济模式类似于“pump n dump”，即成为先行者，预测高峰并套现，这种经济模式已有几十年历史，只是未被明确命名。

• 对于电子设备和软件的生命周期存在争议。一方面认为现代设备和软件趋于短期化和快速更替，另一方面则关注标准化和用户自主权的问题。
• 对AI和软件开发趋势的看法不一，有人认为这是短期潮流，有人则认为这是技术进步的必然结果。

data.title: How to avoid P hacking
data.author: benocodes
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了科学研究中的“P值操纵”（P hacking）问题，即通过调整分析或数据以获得统计显著结果的不当行为。这种做法可能源于研究者过早查看数据、重复实验直到获得显著结果、选择性报告有利数据等。文章列举了五种常见的P值操纵形式，包括过早结束实验、重复实验直到获得显著结果、挑选有利数据、调整数据以获得显著性等。P值操纵会导致科学结果的不可重复性和不可复制性，破坏科学研究的可靠性。文章建议研究者应事先确定样本量和数据处理规则，并如实报告所有实验结果，以维护科学诚信。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：P-hacking问题及其在科学研究中的表现和影响

不同观点：
• parpfish认为，P-hacking有时并非出于恶意，而是由于对新统计方法的探索和旧数据集的再分析引发的。他们提到，研究人员可能因为使用新方法从旧数据中找到“显著效果”而受到鼓励去发表结果，而不是进行验证性实验。
• gwerbret指出，在临床试验中，提前停止实验并不一定是P-hacking，特别是在早期证据显示明显效果或无效时。他们认为，这种做法可以节省时间和资源，并举了关于 circumcision 和HIV感染的临床试验为例。
• neilv用赌徒的比喻说明，反复进行实验可能最终会得到偶然的显著结果，强调需要在实验结束后再进行结果分析。
• cypherpunks01引用了一句改编的谚语，暗示研究人员的职业发展可能依赖于P-hacking，因此很难停止这种行为。
• zipy124强调了Bonferroni修正的重要性，指出许多论文没有对多重比较进行校正，导致结果不可靠。
• p4ul支持透明度，并建议改变 tenure 和 promotion 的激励机制，使可重复性成为评估的重要因素。
• dimal认为，停止P-hacking可能会在短期内影响职业发展，因为发表负面结果可能不利于职业生涯，但长期风险可以通过发表不重要的研究来减轻。
• eviks指出文章的讽刺性，认为遵循文章的建议可能不利于职业发展。
• andrewla提到预注册（preregistration）是解决P-hacking问题的一部分，并建议这种做法需要有“牙齿”，即如果研究被撤回，应该影响研究者的声誉。
• pizlonator提到软件优化中类似P-hacking的行为，认为需要通过良好的性能置信区间（perf CI）来防御，但承认统计学上的自我欺骗是难以完全避免的。
• gregwebs认为文章揭示了科学界对再现性问题的无知，感到非常不安。
• smallmancontrov指出“狗屎null假设”是常见的P-hacking策略，这种假设容易被拒绝，且常常在同行评审中被忽视。
• WhitneyLand对文章需要解释基本伦理和常识感到尴尬，认为这是科学界自我伤害的一部分，导致公众对科学的信任丧失。

补充讨论：
• spinf97提问如何决定实验的重复次数，这涉及到实验设计和统计功效的考虑，是解决P-hacking问题的一个实际操作问题。

争议焦点：
• P-hacking的定义和其合理性的边界。例如，gwerbret和parpfish认为在某些情况下，提前停止实验或使用新方法分析数据不一定是P-hacking，而其他评论者如neilv和cypherpunks01则强调这种做法的潜在危害和道德问题。
• 科学界的激励机制是否助长了P-hacking。p4ul和dimal提到职业发展和发表压力对P-hacking的影响，而andrewla建议通过预注册和声誉风险来改变这种现状。

It can happen so easily. You’re excited about an experiment, so you sneak an early peek at the data to see if the
P
value — a measure of statistical significance — has dipped below the threshold of 0.05. Or maybe you’ve tried analysing your results in several different ways, hoping one will give you that significant finding. These temptations are common, especially in the cut-throat world of publish-or-perish academia. But giving in to them can lead to what scientists call
P
hacking.
P
hacking is the practice of tweaking the analysis or data to get a statistically significant result. In other words, you’re fishing for a desirable outcome and reporting only the catches, while ignoring all the times you came up empty. It might get you a publication in the short term, but
P
hacking contributes to the reproducibility and replicability crisis in science by filling the literature with dubious or unfounded conclusions.
Most researchers don’t set out to cheat, but they could unknowingly make choices that push them towards a significant result. Here are five ways
P
hacking can slip into your research.
Ending the experiment too early
You might plan to gather 30 samples but find yourself running a quick analysis halfway through, just to see where things stand. If you notice a statistically significant difference after 15 samples, you might be inclined to stop the experiment early — after all, you’ve found what you were looking for.
It’s time to talk about ditching statistical significance
But stopping an experiment once you find a significant effect but before you reach your predetermined sample size is classic
P
hacking. It’s like declaring the winner of an election after polling just half the electorate: the result might not be representative of reality. What’s the solution? Decide on the sample size or data-collection process ahead of time and stick to it, no matter how eager you are to see the results.
Running experiments until you get a hit
Another often-unintentional form of
P
hacking is repeating the experiment or analysis until you obtain a statistically significant result. Imagine you run an experiment and the outcome is insignificant. You try again with a new batch of samples — still nothing. You repeat the study once more, and
voila
!
P
< 0.05. Success? Not quite. If you selectively report only the attempt that ‘worked’ and ignore those that didn’t, you’re engaging in
P
hacking by omission. As any gambler knows, if you roll the dice often enough, eventually you’ll get the result you want by chance alone (not that I’m a gambler). The better approach is to report all the experimental replicates, including those that didn’t work.
Cherry-picking your results
A less benign form of
P
hacking is selective reporting. Imagine you measure several outcomes or observe your effect at multiple time points — for instance, testing a therapy’s impact on recipients’ blood pressure, cholesterol, weight and blood sugar regularly over an entire month. After analysing the data, you find that only one outcome — say, blood sugar at week 3 — showed a significant improvement. You might be tempted to highlight this one promising result and downplay the rest, or even omit them from your report. This is cherry-picking: by showing only the favourable data and ignoring everything else, you create a biased narrative.
In this example, people might think the therapy worked because it lowered blood sugar at week 3, even though the overall data are not so rosy. Putting these data into the paper’s supplementary material and continuing with the experiment on the basis of this one finding is also a no-no. You should report all relevant results, not just the ones that support the hypothesis. Science progresses faster when we know what doesn’t work, as well as what does.
Tweaking your data
In data analysis, you often have to make judgements about what to include, what to exclude and how to report the data.
P
hacking can sneak in when those decisions are guided by the desire to achieve significance rather than by scientific reasoning. For example, you might notice an outlier in your data set. Including it in the analysis gives you a
P
value of 0.08, whereas excluding it brings
P
down to 0.03. Problem solved? Not quite.
In these cases, it is best practice to go back to the original data or laboratory notes to determine whether experimental conditions could explain this outlier. Perhaps you pipetted double the amount of reagent into your sample, or construction work nearby during the time you were testing that animal affected its behaviour. Researchers can often rationalize their data-filtration decisions, and most of those decisions are warranted. But if the real motive is to turn an insignificant result into a significant one, it crosses into questionable territory. The key is to decide on data-filtering rules before looking at the results. data.title: Open Hardware Ethernet Switch project, part 1
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者长期开发的开源硬件以太网交换机项目，该项目推动了其他如ngscopeclient和高速度探测器等项目的发展。文章回顾了项目的历史和进展，最早的尝试是2012年左右使用FPGA设计的“open-gig-switch”，但由于技术限制和设备不足，该设计未能成功。在随后的几年中，作者通过攻读博士学位和后续工作积累了更多经验，并购买了更先进的设备如350 MHz示波器。为了解决高速信号完整性问题，作者还设计了未完成的10 GHz采样示波器FREESAMPLE，并开发了高带宽探测器和多个协议解码器。最终，作者规划了LATENTx系列网络设备的发展蓝图，其中LATENTPINK将作为原型/技术演示平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源网络硬件项目的进展、挑战及技术选择

不同观点：
• Aurornis认为该项目非常 impressive，但担心项目范围不断扩大（scope creep）会影响实际成果的完成。他希望看到更简单、可开放迭代的设计，如4端口交换机，并对项目中的其他未兑现产品表示关注。
• Transpute提到NetFPGA项目，认为这是另一个在学术和研究环境中使用的开放网络平台，指出了其全球应用的广泛性。
• Purpleidea表示希望项目能支持switchdev，认为主流交换功能与常规Linux网络的无缝集成将带来积极影响，并强调减少专有接口的重要性。
• Bgnn从自身经验出发，讨论了以太网PHY的设计，并对是否能以较低数量购买10G或25G的PHY表示关注。
• Acyou对从不可靠来源购买网络硬件表示担忧，尤其是可能存在后门的风险，并指出开放源代码硬件在安全性方面的挑战。
• Zokier建议考虑使用Microchip的Sparx-5交换机ASIC，认为这是一个具有Linux支持且价格合理的选择，但同时也理解自定义交换引擎的吸引力。
• Westurner提供了关于OpenWRT支持的48+2端口交换机的信息，并详细讨论了与项目相关的各种开源资源和技术细节。
• Kristel100对DIY网络设备的冷却和功耗问题表示关注，认为这是此类项目成功的关键因素。

补充讨论：
• 项目范围扩大（scope creep）是讨论中的一个重要问题，Aurornis和Westurner都提到了项目复杂性和实际成果之间的平衡。
• 安全性是一个争议焦点，Acyou对从不可靠来源购买硬件的担忧引发了对开放源代码硬件安全性的讨论。
• 对具体技术选择（如PHY类型、ASIC型号）的讨论反映了参与者对技术实现细节的关注。
• 开放源代码硬件项目的实际应用和支持情况（如NetFPGA和OpenWRT）也是讨论的重要内容，提供了其他类似项目的参考。
• 项目的实际可行性和持续性（如产品可靠性和冷却问题）被认为是需要关注的重要方面。

通过这些观点，可以看出参与者们对开源网络硬件项目的热情，同时也关注其实际可行性、技术细节和潜在的安全风险。

43934869.article_content:
Switch project, part 1
2025-05-08 18:00
One of my longest-running projects has been an open hardware Ethernet switch. This has been one of the key driving forces behind many of my other projects, such as ngscopeclient and the high speed probes. It was also the project that got me into high speed digital design.
So I figured itâs time to kick off a series with a short writeup of where things are now, how we got there, and whatâs coming next. If you follow me on Mastodon youâve probably seen most of this in bits and pieces but I wanted to collect it all in one place.
Ancient history: The first switch
The first generation never had a name, it was just called âopen-gig-switchâ or something in my subversion repository (this was circa 2012 before I was primarily running on git).
I couldnât find any many-port gigabit switch ASICs that were suitable for an OSH project (i.e. purchasable in qty 1, no NDA needed for datasheet, etc). So an FPGA-based from-scratch design seemed the only option.
This board pushed a lot of limits for meâ¦ my first use of switching power supplies rather than LDOs, my biggest and most complex board to date, and I think maybe even my first use of an RGMII PHY (I had previously used the Microchip ENC424J600 which is a full 10/100 Ethernet MAC + PHY including buffer memory attached to a parallel bus or SPI interface).
And at the time my fanciest piece of test equipment was a 100 MHz Rigol DS1102D. So I had no way to do signal integrity measurements on either the Ethernet differential pairs or even the 250 MT/s RGMII lines.
This one never really got anywhere. I got three of the four PHYs up and running, PHY #4 never worked (I canât remember if it wouldnât link up, wouldnât pass data, or what). I tried resoldering a bunch of stuff but never got it functional.
I tried to bring up a basic switch with only 3 ports, but very quickly realized that 15K LUTs, <1 Mbit of BRAM, and no external CPU would make that very challenging. The XC6SLX25 was not a large FPGA and adding the Xilinx DDR controller and a softcore CPU and three MACs didnât leave much space at all for fabric. Plus I was still a relative novice to FPGA development and wasnât quite at the point of being ready to tackle the project.
So this board ended up a dead-end, but set the stage for what was coming.
The interim years
The first switch fiasco showed me I needed more skills, better test equipment, better debug tools, and more.
I was still in grad school with little budget for equipment, but over the course of my Ph.D I became a much more experienced RTL engineer. I built a couple of boards with Ethernet that mostly worked.
But since I couldnât afford a better scope and had no way to validate SI on faster stuff, I decided to table the switch project for a bit.
In 2015 I graduated and got a job that paid much more than I was making as a graduate teaching assistant. One of my first purchases was my first ârealâ oscilloscope, a 350 MHz Teledyne LeCroy WaveSurfer 3034. This was actually fast enough to do SI work on RGMII and protocol-decode 100baseTX, but I dreamed of much faster.
I knew I wanted to put 10GbE on the switch whenever I finally got back to it, and didnât expect to be able to afford a many-GHz scope any time soon, so I started looking at alternative approaches to validate SI at these speeds. This led me down another path of yak shaving in which I started designing a 10 GHz sampling oscilloscope named FREESAMPLE (which never got finished, but I do want to revisit the project one day). This, then, got put on ice when I realized a high speed scope would be useless without an equally high bandwidth probe to feed it with.
You probably already know where this story goes. My open hardware 16 GHz probe (which probably deserves a post or series of its own) is now essentially done and ramping up an initial PVT run, hopefully I can actually make them in quantity and offer to the public in the coming months.
Over the course of shaving these yaks I also bought a house, took a year or two off major projects to refurbish it, got a Sonnet EM solver seat, found a shockingly affordably 16 GHz oscilloscope on eBay (which made FREESAMPLE much less of a priority), rewrote âscopeclientâ with OpenGL acceleration as âglscopeclientâ, then rewrote it again in Vulkan as ângscopeclientâ. I also created protocol decodes for 10/100 baseTX, 1000baseX, SGMII, QSGMII, 10Gbase-R, and a few other potentially relevant protocols.
I also started dreaming up a roadmap for a whole family of networking equipment under the randomly generated umbrella name LATENTx, using colors for sub-projects (vaguely inspired by the Lockheed HAVE BLUE). The original roadmap called for LATENTRED to be a gigabit edge switch and LATENTORANGE to be a 10G core switch, but I decided that a prototyping/technology demonstrator platform was called for first. LATENTINFRARED was too long so I went with LATENTPINK as the name.
LATENTPINK
The original LATE

data.title: Policy of Transience
data.author: pekim
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在计算机使用上的一些独特习惯，这些习惯体现了一种“短暂性策略”（Policy of transience）。主要包括：关闭持久的shell历史记录、定期清理GUI桌面、频繁关闭整个网页浏览器、关闭X11会话管理，以及使用tmpfs作为临时工作空间。作者并非试图说服他人采纳这些习惯，而是分享自己的做法。他关闭shell历史记录的动机源于对隐私的担忧，尽管没有具体的安全问题，但他对系统长期保存操作记录感到不安。这种短暂性策略还涉及其他实践，如定期删除电子邮件和自动化操作系统设置。作者强调，这些做法适合个人选择，不一定适用于所有人。

不同观点：

• **spacerzasp的观点**：强调对重要数据进行自主备份，不依赖外部来源。他指出开源项目和数据可能会无预警地被移除，因此自己保存所有重要数据，即使只有少量数据被频繁使用，但这些数据非常有价值。同时，他认为只要存储成本低，就应长期保存数据。

• **dgunay的观点**：默认不删除数据，所有重要数据都会自动备份到设备外。他提到见过许多人因为无法从旧设备中恢复数据而感到困扰，因此自己的策略是确保任何时候丢失设备都不会导致数据丢失，包括使用Git时也会及时提交和推送更改。

• **hinkley的观点**：主张不在工作电脑上保存重要数据，确保数据可以在设备损坏或个人原因无法工作时被他人访问。他提到曾在一家公司工作时，因硬盘缺陷导致多人重建开发环境，因此采取了将所有重要数据保存在版本控制或公司wiki中的策略。

• **Aeolun的观点**：主张数据的永久保存，认为自己经常需要在几个月后再次访问曾经认为是临时性的数据。因此，他的策略是所有数据都会被缓存和保存，只有在缓存满了的情况下才会删除。

• **AstralStorm的观点**：认为缺乏会话管理和持久性会导致效率低下，即使是像Tails这样安全的系统也有持久性选项。他指出，真正的持久性在于将脚本和高级内容备份到适当的存档中，并加以标记，但目前缺乏一个有效的平台来减少不必要的努力。

• 数据保存的策略在不同用户之间存在较大差异，主要争议点在于数据的临时性与永久性保存之间的平衡。

• 存储成本和数据价值之间的权衡，特别是在长时间保存数据的情况下，也是讨论的一个重要方面（spacerzasp和hinkley的观点）。

Policy of transience
[Simon Tatham, 2025-05-09]
Introduction
The habits
Turn off persistent shell history
Clear my GUI desktop regularly
Close my entire web browser frequently
Turn off X11 session management
Use a tmpfs on
~/mem
as my main scratch
space
Policy of transience
Other related practices
Corporate records management: scheduled deletion of email
Automated operating system setup from a recipe
Exceptions to the policy
Conclusion
Introduction
I have several habits in my computer usage which are unusual by
many peopleâs standards (although some more so than others), and
which all kind of point in the same direction.
At the time I adopted each one, I didnât recognise this. Each
habit seemed desirable in its own context for one reason or
another, but it wasnât a lot later until I spotted the common
theme running through them all. The theme wasnât always the
reason I adopted the habit in the first place â but I think itâs
the reason Iâve
kept
all these habits, after trying
them out for some other reason.
In this article Iâll describe the habits Iâm thinking of, and
the more general idea that theyâre all instances of, which I now
think of as a âpolicy of transienceâ.
Iâm not trying to persuade anyone else that they should adopt
this general policy, or even any of the specific habits. I just
put the ideas out here in case theyâre of interest, for people
to consider, and decide
whether
theyâd find any or all
of it useful. If any of this is useful to you, great â and if
you decide itâs not for you, thatâs fine too.
The habits
Hereâs a list of the habits that I now classify under the
general heading of âpolicy of transienceâ. I
think
these are in roughly chronological order of me adopting them,
though itâs hard to be sure.
Turn off persistent shell history
I use the Linux command line, specifically
bash
.
Like many other modern Unix shells,
bash
keeps a
history of the commands youâve typed, so that you can recall
them and run them again, or modify a previous one slightly to do
a new thing.
This can be used in the immediate short term: type a command,
it doesnât quite work, recall it and edit one typo, try again.
But it can also be useful over the long term: recall a command
you ran last week, or last year, or that thing you do about once
a month. To support the long-term uses of this
feature,
bash
saves your shell history to a file
when you exit the shell (by
default
~/.bash_history
), and reloads that file
when it starts up. So you can still recall a command even if
youâve logged out or rebooted the whole machine since running
it.
Many people find this persistent history feature very useful,
and go to some lengths to improve it further â you can configure
a larger number of stored commands, some shells will sync their
history constantly instead of just on exit, there are plugins to
help you search it more easily, and so on. The general view
seems to be: shell history is good, more and easier-to-use
history is even better.
But I go the opposite way. My unusual habit is:
turn
off the history file completely
, by putting the command
â
unset HISTFILE
â in my
.bashrc
. I
still get history within a single instance of the shell, so I
can edit my last command ten times until it works properly; but
history isnât shared between my terminal windows, or preserved
when I log out and log in again.
All
the shell history
I allow myself is localised and short-term.
I started doing this very early in my Linux-using career, very
soon after I found out the history file existed in the first
place. I think my initial motivation was an extremely vague
privacy concern: it just felt
creepy
that my shell
would be remembering that much detail about stuff Iâd done in
the past.
There are certainly valid
specific
privacy concerns
about shell history. Sometimes you write an actual secret, such
as a password, on a command line by mistake. (Oops, had focus in
the wrong window.) And sometimes you just have to hold your nose
and put a secret on a command line on purpose, because some
badly designed tool wonât let you pass it in any other way.
(Thatâs already a danger, of course, because other users of the
system can see it in
ps
â but itâs one thing to
take that risk very briefly while the command is actually
running, and quite another to have a copy of the secret
preserved in
~/.bash_history
for months or years.)
But I donât think I had anything that specific in mind to begin
with: I just felt generically uneasy with the idea.
(Of course, if you
know
youâve just written a secret
on a command line, you can delete the command from that shellâs
history on purpose, before it gets saved to the file. But if you
did it by accident, you might not realise you need to; and if
you had to recall the command and retry it a few times, you
might not manage to clean up every instance of it.)
But after I adopted this policy, and put â
unset
HISTFILE
â in the standard snippet of
.bas

data.title: TransMLA: Multi-head latent attention is all you need
data.author: ocean_moist
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA)的方法，用于解决大型语言模型在硬件上的通信瓶颈问题。MLA通过在键值层使用低秩矩阵来压缩缓存的 latent 状态，减少缓存大小，从而加快推理速度。同时，MLA利用上投影矩阵增加表达能力，以少量计算换取通信开销的降低。文章证明了Group Query Attention (GQA)可以被MLA表示，但反之不成立，并提出了转换方法TransMLA，将GQA预训练模型转为MLA模型，转换后可进一步训练以增强表达能力而不增加缓存大小。此外，文章计划开发MLA特定的推理加速技术，以保持低延迟并更高效地提取Deepseek R1模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Transformer模型中的注意力机制优化，尤其是关于多头注意力（MHA）和多查询注意力（MQA）的改进以及内存优化

不同观点：
• jbellis认为，这种新方法通过仅存储中间潜在表示来大幅减少KV缓存的大小，对于内存受限的环境（如本地推理）是一个很大的优势。具体而言，传统的多头注意力需要缓存大小为T x (nh · dh)的键和值矩阵，而新方法通过低维中间表示大大减少了存储需求。

• karmakaze分享了一个视频资源，解释了MHA、MQA、GQA和MLA，并指出DeepSeek的MLA效率提高了57倍，为讨论提供了额外的背景信息和可视化解释。

• killerstorm提到了一篇相关的论文，该论文讨论了将注意力蒸馏到类似RWKV模型的更激进方法，提供了另一种优化思路。

• octocop对标题表示不满，认为不应夸大宣传，指出之前的类似方法并未达到预期。

• olq_plo对新模型在Hugging Face（HF）上的发布表示期待。

• wiz21c询问了mamba模型的进展，并自行找到了相关讨论链接，展示了社区内的其他讨论资源。

• magicalhippo从旁观者的角度分析了新模型的优势，特别提到了新模型在增加表达能力的同时仅增加了约10%的内存使用，并可以通过微调将现有GQA模型转换为新模型。此外，还详细解释了低秩近似（low-rank approximation）的原理及其在内存节省和表达能力提升方面的作用。

• kavalg给出了一个简化的总结，认为TransMLA是一种压缩已训练GQA模型的方法，并可进一步微调以加速推理。
