data.title: Nextcloud cries foul over Google Play Store app rejection
data.author: brodo
data.article_summary: Nextcloud指责谷歌通过Play Store限制其Android文件同步应用的权限，特别是“所有文件访问”权限，导致该应用功能受限。Nextcloud称其应用自2016年起一直拥有该权限，但在2024年被无故撤销，而使用谷歌推荐的替代工具（如SAF或MediaStore API）无法满足需求。Nextcloud认为这是谷歌打击竞争的手段，并批评谷歌的申诉流程缓慢且无效。尽管Nextcloud在F-Droid上提供完整功能的版本，但Play Store版本受限影响了80多万用户。Nextcloud还提到曾向欧盟投诉微软等大公司的反竞争行为，但未见成效。谷歌未对此做出回应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Play Store的应用权限和安全政策及其影响

不同观点：
• pjc50、monegator等用户认为Google的权限限制过于严格，特别是在用户希望应用（如文件管理器或同步工具）能够访问所有文件的情况下。monegator分享了自己的经历，指出Google对应用相似性的规则执行不一致，导致开发者面临不必要的困难。
• mritzmann解释了背景，指出Google曾经允许某些权限，但现在变得更加严格，导致UX上的回归问题。
• SpaghettiCthulu和izacus认为Google的存储访问权限（如scoped storage）是合理的，用户应该能够控制应用访问哪些文件，而不是给予全盘访问权限。
• 0x000xca0xfe和conartist6从更广泛的角度讨论了软件限制和竞争环境，认为Google在安全和竞争之间需要找到平衡。

补充讨论：
• nopelynopington和rkagerer分享了个人使用Nextcloud的负面体验和Syncthing因政策问题放弃Android应用开发的情况。
• _def提到Dropbox的抽象层设计，认为某些应用为了与其他应用的集成不得不做出妥协。
• dismalpedigree质疑Google Drive是否享有特权，暗示可能存在Nextcloud也能利用的变通方法。
• nottorp指出，相比Apple，Android至少允许用户通过sideload获得权限，而Apple则更为封闭。
• buyucu直接批评Google的政策为反竞争，认为其行为伤害了所有用户。

争议焦点：
• Google Play Store的权限政策是否过于严格，是否在安全和用户需求之间取得平衡。
• Google在执行应用规则时是否存在不一致和不公正的情况。
• 开发者和用户对应用权限的需求与Google安全政策之间的冲突。

43970959.article_content:
Applications
7
Nextcloud cries foul over Google Play Store app rejection
7
Claims policy change is really just a way to squeeze out competition
Richard Speed
Tue 13 May 2025
//
08:30 UTC
Exclusive
European software vendor Nextcloud has accused Google of deliberately crippling its Android Files application, which it says has more than 800,000 users.
The problem lies with the "
All files access
" permission, where broad access to files on a device is required. While most applications can make do with Google's more privacy-friendly storage access tools, such as Storage Access Framework (SAF) or the MediaStore API, others require more permissions – hence the "All files access" privilege.
Nextcloud's Android Files app is a file synchronization tool that, according to the company, has long had permission to read and write all file types. "Nextcloud has had this feature since its inception in 2016," it said, "and we never heard about any security concerns from Google about it."
That changed in 2024, when someone or something at Google's Play Store decided to revoke the permission, effectively crippling the application. Nextcloud was instructed to use "a more privacy-aware replacement."
According to Nextcloud, "SAF cannot be used, as it is for sharing/exposing our files to other apps ... MediaStore API cannot be used as it does not allow access to other files, but only media files."
Attempts to raise the issue with Google resulted in little more than copy-and-pasted sections of the developer guide. "Despite multiple appeals from our side and sharing additional background, Google is not considering reinstating upload for all files," Nextcloud said.
The issue seems to stem from the Play Store. While a fully functional version is available on F-Droid, the Play Store edition is subject to Google's imposed limitations. Regarding the All files access permission, Google's developer documentation
states
: "If you target Android 11 and declare All files access, it can affect your ability to publish and update your app on Google Play."
Nextcloud is clearly aggrieved by the change,
as are its users
.
"This might look like a small technical detail but it is clearly part of a pattern of actions to fight the competition," it said. "What we are experiencing is a piece of the script from the big tech playbook."
Microsoft gets twitchy over talk of Europe's tech independence
European biz calls for Euro tech for local people
Europe's cloud customers eyeing exit from US hyperscalers
Nextcloud puts out fire after data leak panic
Nextcloud cites examples, such as
allegations
leveled at Microsoft over the once-popular WordPerfect word processor, which were eventually
snuffed out
in 2014, or the antics of Apple and Meta that have
attracted scrutiny
from regulators.
In 2021, Nextcloud and other companies
filed a complaint
in the EU regarding alleged anti-competitive behavior from Microsoft. "We are now four years in, and nothing has happened," the company said. "What do you think happens to a company that releases no updates to their app in four years?"
Are there nefarious actors at play here, an automated process that auto-rejects apps with elevated access requirements, or is it just simple incompetence? "Either way," Nextcloud said, "it results in companies like ours just giving up, reducing functionality just to avoid getting kicked out of their app store."
"The issue is that small companies – like ours – have pretty much no recourse," it added. Nextcloud went on to criticize oversight processes as slow-moving, with fines that sound hefty but amount to little more than a slap on the wrist.
"Big Tech is scared that small players like Nextcloud will disrupt them, like they once disrupted other companies. So they try to shut the door."
Nextcloud told us the app's installed audience is 824,000 on Android - customers that used the app in the last 30 days.
The Register
repeatedly asked Google to comment, but it failed to respond. ®

data.article_summary: Petrichor是指雨水落在干土上时产生的独特泥土气味。该词由Isabel Joy Bear和Richard Grenfell Thomas于1964年创造，源自希腊语“petra”（石头）和“ichor”（神话中神的血液）。该现象最早可追溯到1891年Thomas Lambe Phipson的观察，他推测这种气味来自植物的有机物质，被土壤吸收后在雨中释放。1964年，Bear和Thomas在《Nature》上发表论文，详细描述了这种气味由植物干旱时分泌的油和放线菌产生的地质素（geosmin）共同形成。雨滴撞击地面时形成的气溶胶携带这些物质，产生气味。人类对geosmin非常敏感，可能因为祖先依赖雨水生存而进化出这种能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同人群对一种特定气味的感受和联想

不同观点：
• **johng的观点**：他认为来自新墨西哥的这种气味（尤其是换新的蒸发冷却器垫片后散发出的松香气味）是他最喜欢的味道之一。他描述了更换冷却器垫片的过程，尽管在炎热天气下这项工作很麻烦，但完成后感受到的清凉空气和松香味让他觉得非常美妙。这一观点带有一种积极的情感联结，将气味与个人记忆和愉悦体验联系在一起。

• **bergfest的观点**：他虽然也喜欢这种气味，但提到他的祖母讨厌这种味道，因为他的祖母曾错误地认为这种气味是从下水道传来的。这一观点展示了不同个体对同一气味的截然不同态度，并指出个人经验和认知可以影响对气味的感受。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：对于同一气味，有人（如johng）认为它是令人愉悦的，并与积极记忆相关联，而另一些人（如bergfest的祖母）则可能因为误解或负面联想而厌恶这种气味。这表明气味的感知具有较强的主观性，并受个人背景和经验的影响。

• **例子和论据**：johng通过描述更换冷却器垫片的细节和感受来支持他喜欢这种气味的观点，而bergfest通过讲述祖母的负面经历来解释她讨厌这种气味的原因。这些例子都展示了气味与个人经历和情感之间的密切联系。

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Earthy smell when rain falls on dry soil
For other uses, see
Petrichor (disambiguation)
.
"Scent of rain" and "Smell of rain" redirect here. For other uses, see
Scent of Rain (disambiguation)
and
Smell of Rain (disambiguation)
.
Soil and water being splashed by a raindrop
Petrichor
(
/
ˈ
p
ɛ
t
r
ɪ
k
ɔːr
/
PET
-rih-kor
)
[
1
]
is the earthy
scent
produced when
rain
falls on dry
soil
. The word was coined by
Isabel Joy Bear
and
Richard Grenfell Thomas
[
2
]
from
Ancient Greek
πέτρα
(
pétra
)
'
rock
'
or
πέτρος
(
pétros
)
'
stone
'
and
ἰχώρ
(
ikhṓr
)
, the
ethereal fluid
that is the blood of the gods in
Greek mythology
.
Origins
[
edit
]
A brief note on the phenomenon by
Thomas Lambe Phipson
[
fr
]
(1833–1908) appeared in
The Chemical News
on 17 April 1891
[
3
]
and was re-published in its entirety, a month later, in
The Scientific American
,
[
4
]
in which he wrote, "This subject, with which I was occupied more than twenty-five years ago, appears from a paragraph in the last number of the
Chemical News
[
3
]
to have recently attracted the attention of
Professor Berthelot
and [Monsieur G.] Andre."
Phipson was referring to a short paper read by Berthelot and André at the meeting of the French Académie des Sciences on 23 April 1891, and printed in Volume 112 (1891) of
Comptes Rendus
, entitled "Sur l'odeur propre de la terre" ("On the earth's own smell").
[
5
]
[
6
]
Phipson continues, "I find, on referring to my old notes, which are dated 1865, that it is doubtful whether I ever published the results of  these observations; and as the  distinguished chemists I have just named have not quite solved the problem, I hasten to give the results I obtained so long ago." He then theorizes that the odour "... was due to the presence of organic substances closely related to the essential oils of plants ..." and that these substances consist of "... the fragrance emitted by thousands of  flowers ..." absorbed into the pores of the soil, and only released when displaced by rain. After attempts to isolate it, he found that it "... appeared to be very similar to, if not identical with,
bromo-cedren
derived from
essence of cedar
."
The phenomenon was first scientifically described in a March 1964 paper by Australian researchers
Isabel Bear
and
Dick Thomas
, published in the journal
Nature
.
[
7
]
[
8
]
[
9
]
[
10
]
Thomas coined the term "petrichor" to refer to what had previously been known as "argillaceous odour".
[
11
]
The authors describe how the smell derives from an oil exuded by certain
plants
during dry periods, whereupon it is
absorbed
by
clay
-based soils and rocks. During rain, the oil is released into the air along with another compound,
geosmin
, a metabolic by-product of certain
actinobacteria
, such as
Streptomyces
,
[
12
]
which is emitted by wet soil, producing the distinctive scent;
ozone
may also be present if there is lightning.
[
13
]
In a follow-up paper, Bear and Thomas (1965) showed that the oil slows seed germination and early plant growth.
[
14
]
Mechanism
[
edit
]
A leaf with droplets on damp soil
When a raindrop lands on a porous surface, air from the pores forms small bubbles, which float to the surface and release
aerosols
.
[
15
]
Such aerosols carry the scent, as well as bacteria and viruses from the soil.
[
15
]
Raindrops that move slower tend to produce more aerosols; this explains why petrichor is more common after light rains. Members of the
Actinomycetes
, gram-positive bacteria, are responsible for producing these aerosols.
[
15
]
[
12
]
The
human nose
is sensitive to
geosmin
and can detect it at concentrations as low as 0.4 parts per billion.
[
16
]
Some scientists believe that humans may appreciate the rain scent because ancestors relied on rainy weather for survival.
[
17
]
Camels
in the desert also rely on petrichor to locate sources of water such as
oases
.
[
18
]
See also
[
edit
]
Dimethyl sulfide
– One of the molecules responsible for the odour of the sea
Mitti attar
– a perfume that recreates the loamy smell of a first rain

data.title: Backslash: Rate Constrained Optimized Training of Large Language Models
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为BackSlash的新型训练时压缩方法，用于大型语言模型的参数压缩。该方法基于速率失真优化（RDO），在训练阶段灵活权衡模型准确性和复杂性，显著减少参数冗余，同时保持性能。实验表明，BackSlash可在不损失准确性的情况下减少60%-90%的内存使用，相比训练后压缩具有显著优势。此外，它还提升了模型的泛化能力、对剪枝的鲁棒性，并简化网络以加速边缘设备的推理速度。

Title:
BackSlash: Rate Constrained Optimized Training of Large Language Models
Authors:
Jun Wu
,
Jiangtao Wen
,
Yuxing Han
View a PDF of the paper titled BackSlash: Rate Constrained Optimized Training of Large Language Models, by Jun Wu and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The rapid advancement of large-language models (LLMs) has driven extensive research into parameter compression after training has been completed, yet compression during the training phase remains largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce Rate-Constrained Training (BackSlash), a novel training-time compression approach based on rate-distortion optimization (RDO). BackSlash enables a flexible trade-off between model accuracy and complexity, significantly reducing parameter redundancy while preserving performance. Experiments in various architectures and tasks demonstrate that BackSlash can reduce memory usage by 60% - 90% without accuracy loss and provides significant compression gain compared to compression after training. Moreover, BackSlash proves to be highly versatile: it enhances generalization with small Lagrange multipliers, improves model robustness to pruning (maintaining accuracy even at 80% pruning rates), and enables network simplification for accelerated inference on edge devices.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章研究了低强度经颅聚焦超声（tFUS）对与情绪、焦虑和创伤相关障碍（MATRDs）的患者进行杏仁核调节的有效性和安全性。研究分为两个部分：第一部分采用双盲、假对照试验，利用功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）监测tFUS对左侧杏仁核血氧水平依赖（BOLD）信号的急性调节作用，参与者包括29名MATRD患者和23名健康对照者。第二部分为非盲试验，患者每日接受重复tFUS（rtFUS）治疗，持续三周（15次），以评估安全性、可行性和症状变化。结果显示，活性tFUS减少了左侧杏仁核BOLD信号，患者对情绪面孔的反应也发生变化。rtFUS治疗耐受性良好，无严重不良事件，患者在情绪和焦虑症状上有显著改善。研究初步证明了tFUS调节杏仁核功能的可行性和安全性，并建议进行双盲随机对照试验以进一步验证其疗效。

43971197.article_content:
Low-intensity transcranial focused ultrasound amygdala neuromodulation: a double-blind sham-controlled target engagement study and unblinded single-arm clinical trial
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Depression
Neuroscience
Abstract
Mood, anxiety, and trauma-related disorders (MATRDs) are highly prevalent and comorbid. A sizable number of patients do not respond to first-line treatments. Non-invasive neuromodulation is a second-line treatment approach, but current methods rely on cortical targets to indirectly modulate subcortical structures, e.g., the amygdala, implicated in MATRDs. Low-intensity transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) is a non-invasive technique for direct subcortical neuromodulation, but its safety, feasibility, and promise as a potential treatment is largely unknown. In a target engagement study, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided tFUS to the left amygdala was administered during functional MRI (tFUS/fMRI) to test for acute modulation of blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) signal in a double-blind, within-subject, sham-controlled design in patients with MATRDs (N = 29) and healthy comparison subjects (N = 23). In an unblinded treatment trial, the same patients then underwent 3-week daily (15 sessions) MRI-guided repetitive tFUS (rtFUS) to the left amygdala to examine safety, feasibility, symptom change, and change in amygdala reactivity to emotional faces. Active vs. sham tFUS/fMRI reduced, on average, left amygdala BOLD signal and produced patient-related differences in hippocampal and insular responses. rtFUS was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events. There were significant reductions on the primary outcome (Mood and Anxiety Symptom Questionnaire General Distress subscale;
p
= 0.001, Cohen’s
d
= 0.77), secondary outcomes (Cohen’s
d of
0.43–1.50), and amygdala activation to emotional stimuli. Findings provide initial evidence of tFUS capability to modulate amygdala function, rtFUS safety and feasibility in MATRDs, and motivate double-blind randomized controlled trials to examine efficacy.

Introduction
Mood, anxiety, and trauma-related disorders (MATRD), i.e., major depressive disorder (MDD), bipolar disorder, anxiety disorders, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), are highly prevalent with an enormous public health burden [
1
,
2
]. All are characterized by intense/prolonged negative affect triggered by emotionally provocative stimuli [
3
,
4
]. Exaggerated emotional reactivity is associated with hyperactivity of the amygdala [
5
], a subcortical structure underlying detection of salient environmental stimuli [
6
] and engagement of adaptive physiological, behavioral, and affective responses [
7
,
8
]. Consistent with a role in salience detection and emotional valence [
9
,
10
,
11
,
12
], the amygdala contributes to numerous MATRD-relevant processes [
13
]. Amygdala hyperactivity in MATRDs is consistent with transdiagnostic models of mental illness, i.e. the Research Domain Criteria [
14
], which identify the amygdala as a key mediator of all negative valence subdomains [
15
]. The amygdala therefore remains a promising but largely unexploited therapeutic target.
First-line MATRD interventions have been shown to alter amygdala function, including antidepressants [
16
] and psychotherapy [
17
,
18
,
19
,
20
,
21
,
22
,
23
,
24
]. However, non-invasive neuromodulation approaches, such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) [
25
,
26
], necessitate modulation of cortical activity to indirectly modulate subcortical function [
27
], which may depend upon integrity of cortical-subcortical structural connections [
28
]. As an rTMS therapeutic mechanism may be indirect modulation of subcortical limbic pathways via TMS-accessible cortical targets [
29
], the capacity to non-invasively and directly modulate subcortical regions without reliance upon cortical targets could offer an important therapeutic complement to existing approaches.
Low-intensity transcranial low-intensity focused ultrasound (tFUS), the focused administration of low-intensity, high-frequency sound waves to the brain, is a novel method of reversibly augmenting brain function [
30
]. One advantage is its ability to directly and non-invasively modulate deep brain structures without reliance on cortical connections [
31
]. The ellipsis (focus) can also be delivered with spatial precision ranging from millimeters to centimeters in width and with adjustable focal depth [

主要讨论点：关于存档链接的使用和隐私/道德问题

不同观点：
• 支持使用存档链接：
  - 存档链接有助于保留网页内容，防止因未来页面删除或更改导致的信息丢失。
  - 举例：有些网站可能会在没有通知的情况下删除或更改内容，存档链接能确保信息的长久保存。
  - 认为存档链接是合理的，只要不滥用，并且用户有权利访问和保存公开信息。

• 反对使用存档链接：
  - 存档链接可能侵犯个人隐私或版权，因为它们保存的内容可能未经原网站所有者的明确同意。
  - 例子：个人信息或敏感信息在未经同意的情况下被存档，可能会导致隐私泄露问题。
  - 认为存档行为应受到更严格的监管，尤其是在涉及私人或敏感信息时。

• 中立或条件性支持：
  - 支持存档链接的使用，但前提是需要有明确的指引和道德标准，以避免侵犯隐私或版权。
  - 建议存档服务提供者应提供便捷的退出机制，让不愿意被存档的网站所有者可以轻松移除其内容。
  - 强调用户责任，认为使用者应谨慎判断哪些内容适合存档，避免滥用。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于存档链接的合法性和道德性，特别是在隐私和版权方面的影响。
- 讨论中涉及到技术与伦理的平衡问题，即如何在利用技术保存信息的同时，尊重个人和网站所有者的权利。
- 存档链接的透明性和用户知情权也被提及，有观点认为应提高存档服务使用的透明度，让用户清楚知道内容被存档的情况。

通过这些观点，可以看出讨论的核心在于如何在信息保存和隐私保护之间找到一个合理的平衡点。

主要讨论点：对某科技公司及其与国家安全和政府合同关系的评价

不同观点：
• [批评观点 - ngangaga] 该评论认为，这家公司通过制作质量极差的软件，最终使其修复成为国家安全问题，从而成为盈利支柱。评论者对政府居然会与这样的公司签订合同表示不信任，认为这显示出国家不严肃对待这些问题。

• [质疑观点 - robertlagrant] 该评论引用文章内容，指出微软由于其庞大的数据流，在抓捕黑客方面具有优势，但同时暗示微软可能利用其地位做其他事情，表达了对微软权力过大的隐忧。

• [谨慎肯定观点 - bburnett44] 该评论虽然承认该团队可能很优秀，但对公司的整体安全记录表示怀疑，认为过多的赞誉与其实际表现不符。

• [支持观点 - senectus1] 该评论通过个人经验，表示认识该团队中的一员，并称赞其能力与敬业态度，暗示整个团队可能都非常出色。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于该公司的软件质量和安全记录是否足以支撑其与政府签订的重要合同。批评者认为其软件质量低劣，不值得信任，而支持者则基于个人经验或团队成员的素质为其辩护。质疑者则担心该公司因其地位可能拥有过多权力。

data.title: Political attacks could crush the mRNA vaccine revolution
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了mRNA疫苗技术在美国面临的政治挑战和不确定性。在特朗普重新执政后，尽管其曾大力推动mRNA疫苗的研发，但新政府对该技术的支持出现逆转。疫苗批评者被任命为重要卫生机构领导，免疫科学的支持者被排除，与HIV预防和疫情准备相关的mRNA研究资金被取消。同时，一些州试图限制mRNA药物的使用，导致行业不确定性增加。mRNA行业曾经因新冠疫苗的成功而备受瞩目，但现在由于政治气候变化，面临项目缩减、资金削减、合作终止和外迁风险。业内人士担忧，这可能威胁到mRNA技术在疫苗和药物研发中的未来发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MRNA疫苗的推广及其政治化对公共健康的影响

不同观点：
• aurareturn认为，目前采取的措施将导致中国（在公共健康领域）取得领先优势。这暗示了对当前政策的不满，认为会让其他国家在防疫方面落后。

• incomingpain认为，MRNA疫苗的推广方式被政治化，并且对公共健康产生了负面影响。他指出，疫苗推广过程中与某一方政治立场结盟，宣传疫苗能阻止病毒传播（被认为是虚假宣传），并通过强制措施（如禁止进入公共场所、暂停工作、甚至罚款）推行疫苗接种。这些做法导致了公众对公共卫生机构信任的下降，并引发了疫苗犹豫，甚至导致了麻疹等其他疾病的爆发。

补充讨论：
• incomingpain指出，希腊和魁北克等地区实施了严格的疫苗强制措施，导致了对抗议者的 censorship（审查和压制异议），并将怀疑者视为危险分子。他认为，如果MRNA疫苗保持政治中立，可能不会产生如此严重的公共健康后果。

• incomingpain还提到，当前在HIV和癌症研究领域的某些做法（如扮演受害者角色，指责批评者）是不合理的。虽然反疫苗者并不是正确的英雄，但如果采取更中立和自由的态度，可能不会导致如此严重的公共健康问题。

争议焦点：
• MRNA疫苗推广过程中政治化和强制措施的正当性，以及这些措施对公共健康的长远影响。一方认为这些措施导致了社会分裂和信任危机，另一方可能认为这些措施在控制疫情传播中是必要的。

43971605.article_content:
How political attacks could crush the mRNA vaccine revolution
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
Illustration: Jasiek Krzysztofiak; photographs: CDC, Getty, Rebecca Noble/Getty
You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
The day after Donald Trump moved back into the White House in January, he celebrated a US$500-billion private-sector investment in artificial intelligence (AI) with a high-profile announcement in the Roosevelt Room. The new president looked on as technology billionaire Larry Ellison highlighted one of the initiative’s most transformative goals: using messenger RNA vaccines to transform cancer treatments.
By harnessing AI to analyse tumour genetics, Ellison explained, researchers could rapidly design personalized vaccines tailored to an individual’s cancer. “This is the promise of AI and the promise of the future,” he said.
Are the Trump team’s actions affecting your research? How to contact Nature
Biotechnology executives were elated. Trump had, just five years earlier, propelled mRNA medicines into the spotlight through his signature effort to fast-track the development of a coronavirus vaccine. Now, just one day into his second term, he was once again elevating the technology to the national stage.
“Then the bottom fell out,” says Deborah Day Barbara, co-founder of the Alliance for mRNA Medicines (AMM), a trade group representing more than 75 companies and academic institutions that are advancing mRNA research, development and manufacturing.
A prominent vaccine critic who had vilified the mRNA-based COVID-19 jabs, Robert F. Kennedy Jr, was
appointed to lead the country’s top health agency
, and long-time champions of immunization science in the civil-service sector were shown the door. Research grants tied to
HIV prevention
and
pandemic preparedness
were abruptly cancelled, including many involving mRNA. And numerous other projects that were focused on mRNA vaccine technology were
compiled into a list
, potentially signalling their impending termination.
At the same time, legislators in several states have been pushing to ban or restrict the use of mRNA-based medicines for infectious diseases. None of these measures has become law, but the efforts threaten to destabilize the mRNA industry, creating uncertainty and potentially limiting patient access to emerging treatments.
The anti-mRNA sentiment — coupled with the sweeping shake-up of science funding across the United States — has sparked fears that this once-celebrated technology, widely seen as a major engine of
next-generation vaccines and therapeutics
, could soon find itself on the chopping block.
For AMM executive director Clay Alspach, a principal at Leavitt Partners, a health-care consulting firm in Washington DC, the message has been unmistakable: “This is an existential threat,” he says.
By mid-March, the AMM was holding regular conference calls to strategize. Members swapped intelligence, compared notes on delayed grants and tried to anticipate what might come next. Amid the uncertainty, a few questions loomed large: how far would the clampdown on mRNA go? Would it stop at COVID-19 jabs? Would it extend to all vaccines in development for influenza and other infectious threats? Or reach even into mRNA-based drug therapies
in the works for cancer
, autoimmune disorders, rare genetic diseases and more?
From hero to zero
Five years ago, the US government was spending billions of dollars to support the development, manufacturing and roll-out of mRNA vaccines, which played a major part in curbing the COVID-19 pandemic. Pharmaceutical companies were pouring in capital and building ambitious pipelines centred on mRNA. The technology was
feted with a Nobel prize
. Investor confidence was sky-high.
Now, in the span of just a few months, the mood across the industry has grown darker — chilled by a newly hostile political climate.
Will US science survive Trump 2.0?
One contract manufacturer of mRNA products has seen a substantial decline in business as government-backed vaccine programmes have their funding pulled, according to a senior company executive. Another biotech executive says that his mRNA-focused company is considering relocating planned clinical trials for anti-viral vaccines to outside the United States — or scrapping them entirely, shifting the firm’s focus to less politically volatile therapeutic areas. “It’s all just a commercial and regulatory risk now,” he says.
Both executives requested anonymity to avoid drawing political attention to their companies — but their experiences reflect a broad upheaval that is now rippling through the industry. In a survey released this month by the AMM, nearly half of 106 senior biotech and pharma executives reported direct impacts from US policy shifts this year — including project downsizing, budget cuts, delayed investments, terminated partnerships, job losses, hiring freezes and planned relocation of operations overseas

(see ‘An industry at risk’).

补充讨论：
• incomingpain指出，希腊和魁北克等地区实施了严格的疫苗强制措施，导致了对抗议者的 censorship（审查和压制异议），并将怀疑者视为危险分子。他认为，如果MRNA疫苗保持政治中立，可能不会产生如此严重的公共健康后果。

• incomingpain还提到，当前在HIV和癌症研究领域的某些做法（如扮演受害者角色，指责批评者）是不合理的。虽然反疫苗者并不是正确的英雄，但如果采取更中立和自由的态度，可能不会导致如此严重的公共健康问题。

争议焦点：
• MRNA疫苗推广过程中政治化和强制措施的正当性，以及这些措施对公共健康的长远影响。一方认为这些措施导致了社会分裂和信任危机，另一方可能认为这些措施在控制疫情传播中是必要的。

data.title: New study sheds light on health differences between sexes
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 一项由伦敦玛丽女王大学主导的国际研究揭示了男女健康风险和结果差异的生物学机制，研究结果发表在《Nature Communications》上。通过分析英国生物银行和Fenland研究的基因和蛋白质数据，研究团队发现约6000种蛋白质中的三分之二在男女之间的水平不同，但只有约100种蛋白质的基因“开关”存在差异。研究表明，健康差异不仅由遗传因素导致，还涉及激素、生活环境、教育、经济状况和生活方式等非医疗因素。这项研究强调，需要更深入理解这些因素以制定更个性化和公平的医疗方案。

The GIST

New study sheds light on health differences between sexes
by
Queen Mary, University of London
Credit: CC0 Public Domain
The results of an international study led by researchers from Queen Mary University of London's Precision Healthcare University Research Institute (PHURI) shed new light on the underlying biological mechanisms which cause differences in health risks, symptoms and outcomes between males and females.
The study, carried out in collaboration with the Berlin Institute of Health at Charité, Universitätsmedizin Berlin, and the Medical Research Council (MRC) Epidemiology Unit at the University of Cambridge, is published in
Nature Communications
.
Using data from UK Biobank and the
Fenland study
, the team carried out an in-depth analysis of the genetic links between ~6,000 proteins and hundreds of diseases in 56,000 males and females.
The team found that for two-thirds of these proteins, their levels differed between males and females. Further examination revealed that only a very small fraction, around 100 proteins out of the 6,000 studied, had differences in the genetic "switches" which control their levels, when compared between males and females.
These findings, which may have implications for
drug development
, indicate that while there are differences between the sexes in relation to how much they express certain proteins, what's causing these differences isn't solely down to differences in their genetics.
Instead, the authors highlight the importance of looking beyond genetics—and other medical factors such as hormones—when comparing health risks and outcomes between males and females.
Their findings indicate that non-medical factors such as where people work and live, their education,
financial situation
, access to resources, as well as their lifestyle also contribute to the health differences experiences between the sexes and so should be explored further and considered more when exploring sex differences in health.
Mine Koprulu, lead author of the study and a postdoctoral researcher at Queen Mary's PHURI, said, "For the first time in history, we are able to study human biology at this level of detail—across genes, proteins, and more. This is the largest study to date exploring the similarities and differences in how our
genetic code
regulates blood
protein
levels between sexes.
"Our findings highlight the need to better understand the factors that impact health differences—at the genetic level and beyond—to create more tailored and equitable health care for everyone."
Professor Claudia Langenberg, Director of the PHURI at Queen Mary and Professor of Computational Medicine at the Berlin Institute of Health at Charité, Germany, said, "Drug development pipelines increasingly incorporate information on genetic differences in protein levels and function and this has led to large investment in human cohorts, such as UK Biobank.
"From this perspective, better understanding of population differences in the regulation of proteins, such as those between males and females, is essential to guide precision medicine approaches and identify where one size may not fit all.
"Our results clearly show that with very few exceptions, protein regulating genetic variants identified so far behave in a very similar way in males and females. This provides evidence for an important implicit assumption—that insights arising from studying these variants apply to both sexes."
In this study, data were categorized as male or female based on chromosomal information (XX or XY). The authors acknowledge that chromosomal information does not always align with an individual's gender identity.
However, for the purposes of this study (genetic and protein-level scientific analyses), this categorization was necessary, and data on gender identity was not reliably recoded, meaning it could not be consistently used across all data.

data.title: LSP client in Clojure in 200 lines of code
data.author: vlaaad
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何用Clojure编写一个简易的LSP（Language Server Protocol）客户端，代码长度约为200行。LSP旨在解决代码编辑器与编程语言之间的集成问题，通过统一接口简化了两者的连接。作者之前尝试将LLM与LSP结合未果，但发现可以简化实现一个LSP客户端。本文的目标读者主要是Clojure开发者。

文中详细说明了如何实现LSP客户端的基础通信层，使用JSON-RPC进行请求和响应，以及如何通过Java的虚拟线程处理阻塞操作。作者跳过了一些复杂功能如文档同步，专注于实现核心功能，如消息的读取和发送。

具体实现包括：
1. **读取ASCII行**：逐字节读取输入流，识别`\r\n`行分隔符。
2. **基础通信层**：处理客户端与服务器间的消息交换，使用JSON-RPC协议。

完整代码展示了如何启动一个语言服务器进程并与其通信，适合有兴趣在Clojure中构建代码编辑工具的开发者参考。

LSP client in Clojure in 200 lines of code
Awhile ago I was prototyping integrating LLMs with
LSP
to enable a language model to answer questions about code while having access to code navigation tools provided by language servers. I wasn’t that successful with this prototype, but I found it cool that I could write a minimal LSP client in around 200 lines of code. Of course, it was very helpful that I previously wrote a much more featureful
LSP client for the Defold editor
… So let me share with you a minimal LSP client, written in Clojure, in under 200 lines. Also, at the end of the post, I’ll share my thoughts on the LSP.
Who is the target audience of this blog post? I don’t even know… Clojure developers writing code editors? There are, like, 3 of us! Okay, let’s try to change the scope of this exercise a bit: let’s build a command line linter that uses a language server to do the work. Surely that wouldn’t be a problem…
The what
Some terminology and scope first. LSP stands for Language Server Protocol, a standard that defines how some text editor (a language client) should talk to some language-specific tool (a language server) that knows the semantics of a programming language and may provide contextual information like code navigation, refactoring, linting etc.
The main benefit of LSP is that the so called MxN problem of IDEs and languages becomes M+N with LSP.
Here is a good explanation
. In short, as a language author, previously you had to write integration for every code editor. Or, as an IDE author, you had to write a separate integration for every language. Now there is a common interface — LSP — and both language authors and IDE authors only need to support this interface.
In 200 LoC, we will implement essential blocks of the
LSP Specification
that supports programmatic read-only querying of language servers. We will implement:
base communication layer between language client and server processes. It is similar to HTTP protocol: client and server talk to each other using byte streams with messages formatted as headers + JSON message bodies. The base layer establishes a way to exchange JSON blobs.
JSON-RPC
— a layer on top of the base layer that adds meaning to JSON blobs, turning them into either requests/responses, or notifications.
A wrapper around JSON-RPC connection that is a leaving breathing language server we can talk to.
We will use Java 24 with
virtual threads
: writing blocking code that performs and scales well is nice, sweet, and performant. Now, here are few things we will not implement:
JSON parser. I mean come on. We will just use a dependency. I picked
jsonista
because it’s fast and has a cool name.
Document syncing. When the user opens a file in a text editor and makes some changes to it without saving, the editor notifies running language servers about the new text of the open files. We are not building a text editor here, just a small PoC, so we’ll skip this.
Now, Let’s go!
The how
If you just want to look at the code,
here it is
. Now I’ll walk you through it.

Content-Length: 14\r\n
\r\n
{"json": true}

Content-Length
header, separated with
\r\n
. Then, an empty line. Then comes a JSON string. The headers are serialized using ASCII encoding (so 1 byte is always 1 char), the JSON blob uses UTF-8.

data.title: We can no longer run Microsoft Store on 1809/LTSC 2019
data.author: fernvenue
data.article_summary: 该项目提供了一个适用于Windows LTSC版本的Microsoft Store软件包，支持Windows 10 LTSC 2019、2021以及Windows 11 LTSC 2024。由于LTSC 2019不再支持新版Microsoft Store，用户会被要求更新系统，且无法正常安装应用，因此该版本上的Microsoft Store已不可用，建议使用`Uninstall.bat`卸载。安装包可通过双击直接安装，但为确保兼容性，未使用最新版本的软件包，用户可能需要手动更新Microsoft Store。项目基于BSD-3-Clause许可证，包含安装和卸载脚本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“Microsoft Store”存储库出现在GitHub个人账户上的疑惑，以及对LTSC版本支持问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• bradford认为该GitHub存储库令人困惑，因为它是“Microsoft Store”相关的仓库，却在一个看似随机的个人账户上托管，且README文件没有清楚地解释该仓库的用途。他质疑提交者的意图，并提到LTSC版本缺乏支持并不是最令人困惑的部分。

• throitallaway支持bradford的观点，表示微软通过这种方式推广应用程序让人困惑。他分享了自己在Windows Server上安装Windows Terminal时遇到的困难，最终在GitHub发布页才找到所需内容。

• bongodongobob指出，如果用户使用的是LTSC版本，就不应该期望使用应用商店，因为LTSC版本是为那些有特定需求的关键应用程序而设，而不是为了应用商店。

• lousken关注winget（Windows软件包管理器）是否也会因此停止工作，暗示对微软应用分发机制的担忧。

• Havoc表达了对MS Store的不满，认为如果不再见到MS Store会是件好事，基于其负面的使用体验。

补充讨论：
• thangngoc89和steelbrain提供了背景信息，解释1809/LTSC 2019指的是Windows 10的长期支持版本，并说明LTSC在Windows术语中代表长期服务通道。

• doublerabbit和CamperBob2对该情况持轻松态度，认为这可能反而是件好事。

• Demiurge提出了一种假设性观点，认为如果Windows是开源的，这种情况可能可以避免，暗示开源可能带来更高的透明度和灵活性。

争议焦点：微软在LTSC版本上不提供MS Store支持的决定是否合理，以及通过GitHub分发关键应用程序的策略是否合适。用户对微软应用商店的体验和态度也存在分歧。

不同观点：
• bradford认为该GitHub存储库令人困惑，因为它是“Microsoft Store”相关的仓库，却在一个看似随机的个人账户上托管，且README文件没有清楚地解释该仓库的用途。他质疑提交者的意图，并提到LTSC版本缺乏支持并不是最令人困惑的部分。

• throitallaway支持bradford的观点，表示微软通过这种方式推广应用程序让人困惑。他分享了自己在Windows Server上安装Windows Terminal时遇到的困难，最终在GitHub发布页才找到所需内容。

• bongodongobob指出，如果用户使用的是LTSC版本，就不应该期望使用应用商店，因为LTSC版本是为那些有特定需求的关键应用程序而设，而不是为了应用商店。

• lousken关注winget（Windows软件包管理器）是否也会因此停止工作，暗示对微软应用分发机制的担忧。

• Havoc表达了对MS Store的不满，认为如果不再见到MS Store会是件好事，基于其负面的使用体验。

补充讨论：
• thangngoc89和steelbrain提供了背景信息，解释1809/LTSC 2019指的是Windows 10的长期支持版本，并说明LTSC在Windows术语中代表长期服务通道。

• doublerabbit和CamperBob2对该情况持轻松态度，认为这可能反而是件好事。

• Demiurge提出了一种假设性观点，认为如果Windows是开源的，这种情况可能可以避免，暗示开源可能带来更高的透明度和灵活性。

争议焦点：微软在LTSC版本上不提供MS Store支持的决定是否合理，以及通过GitHub分发关键应用程序的策略是否合适。用户对微软应用商店的体验和态度也存在分歧。

• breakpointalpha：建议与德州扑克教学YouTube频道合作，以扩展内容种类。
• lassenordahl：对工具的概念表示赞赏，认为非常酷。

data.title: I learned Snobol and then wrote a toy Forth
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者学习Snobol语言的经历以及用Snobol编写的一个小型Forth解释器的项目。作者认为Snobol以其独特的模式匹配功能而令人着迷，尽管其控制流依赖于GOTO语句，属于1960年代的“非结构化编程”风格，通常认为在大型程序中会变得混乱。作者通过实现一个能运行“99 Bottles of Beer”程序的小型Forth解释器来验证自己对Snobol的理解，该解释器代码不到500行。作者建议在测试小型编程语言时设定一个目标程序，并分享了使用MNT Pocket Reform电脑和Krita软件完成项目的细节。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Snobol、Forth等非主流编程语言的看法及其对编程思维的影响

不同观点：
• Gitroom认为学习一些非主流的编程语言（如Snobol）可能会改变编程思维方式，并对此表示好奇。
• Geophile分享了自己在学生时代深入学习Snobol的经历，强调了该语言在模式匹配和内存管理方面的强大，并指出其对后续编程的深远影响。
• Ebiester提到Icon语言，认为它是Snobol的后续发展，改进了Snobol的一些不足之处，特别是在字符串操作方面。
• Dang提供了多个关于Snobol的讨论链接，展示了Snobol在不同情境下的应用和相关资源。
• Animats比较了Snobol和Forth，指出Snobol在字符串模式匹配上的优势以及其潜在的时间复杂度问题，而Forth则是低级别的栈语言，甚至可以在FPGA上实现。
• Throwaway71271强烈推荐了《Threaded Interpretive Languages Their Design And Implementation》这本书，分享了自己通过学习Forth理解了新的编程范式，并通过制作自己的Forth解释器获得了乐趣和理解。
• JSR_FDED表达了对Snobol文章的喜爱，认为Snobol虽然奇怪但非常强大且一致。
• Jollyllama提到Ratfactor制作的HTMX参考资料，虽然未完成但非常有用。
• Nlte询问图片中的小型计算机是什么，偏离了主要讨论点。
• Cafard分享了自己学习Snobol的经历，认为它对后来学习awk和Perl有帮助。
• Kaycebasques提到在一次旅行中偶然发现了一本关于Forth的旧书，并发现了与Forth相关的商业名片。
• OhMeadhbh简单表达了对Snobol和Forth的喜爱。
• Anthk提到了一些关于Forth的书籍和资源。
• Oytis质疑是否存在非玩具性质的Forth实现。

补充讨论：
• 关于Snobol的讨论主要集中在它的字符串模式匹配能力和历史影响，以及其与Icon语言的关系。
• Forth语言的讨论则更多涉及其作为低级别栈语言的特性，以及它对编程思维的启发和影响。
• 争议的焦点在于Snobol和Forth在现代编程中的实用性和应用场景，例如Forth是否存在非玩具性质的实现。
• 资源分享也是一个重要部分，包括书籍、文章和相关讨论链接。

43951885.article_content:
This page is a mini-site for my Snobol excursion
with links to separate pages for my:
Thoughts on Snobol
Toy Forth interpreter written in Snobol
Thoughts about writing a toy Forth interpreter in Snobol
On with the show…​
I finally learned SNOBOL!
Snobol has been on my programming language bucket list for ages.
Snobol
Here’s my conclusions about the Snobol4 language itself, which get their own
pages:
Ratfactor’s Judgement of Snobol4
The Snobol Implementation Language (SIL)
In short, I think Snobol is fascinating. The singular focus on pattern matching
kind of reminds me of Awk. Except Awk doesn’t do nearly as much with patterns,
it devolves into a C-like script to do things with pattern matches.  Snobol
uses no such crutches, just pattern matching statements for all logic and
control flow.  Its purity is impressive.
No kidding:
Every single line
in a Snobol program consists of five parts:
label, subject, pattern, replacement, goto. All of those parts are optional.
That certainly makes it a Weird Language to the modern developer, but once you
get the hang of it, it’s easy to see why Snobol was once popular and
well-regarded by computer users of all stripes.
It’s extremely easy for seasoned developers to forget that even a simple loop
construct is a conceptual leap for beginners. I remember being that beginner.
By contrast, I think conditional GOTO-style control flow is easy for beginners
to follow because you can "see" it. You can trace the logic with your finger.
Of course, simplicity of language is good for programming in the small, but
maybe not so good for programming in the large.  Snobol4 is basically
1960s-style "unstructured programming", which is generally understood to
rapidly break down in large programs.
That’s the message in Edsger Dijkstra’s famous "Go To
Statement Considered Harmful" letter.
See David R. Tribble’s
Go To Statement Considered Harmful: A Retrospective
(david.tribble.com).
Still, Snobol proves that programming using "this one weird trick" can be surprisingly effective.
Snobol4th - A Forth in Snobol4
I’ve learned that it’s easy to think I understand a concept only to find
that I really don’t when forced to put it into practice. So I needed to make
some small project with Snobol to ensure I wasn’t fooling myself.
What to make?
"I know!" says Dave. "This is an opportunity to keep the concepts of the Forth
language fresh in my mind. I shall implement a toy Forth interpreter in
Snobol."
But
how much
Forth should I implement? Rather than go blindfolded and pick
language features at random, I decided to select a small Forth program to
execute. The goal would be: Once my implementation could execute it, I would be
done.
The program I picked is
99.forth
"99 Bottles of Beer"
by Arf Dysg and posted to one of my favorite programming-related websites:
http://www.99-bottles-of-beer.net/language-forth-793.html
And here’s the result, a Forth, written in Snobol, that executes a program that can run the above program that prints the complete lyrics of the "99 Bottles of Beer" song:
forth.sno
.
And here’s the result:
The Snobol4th Repo
The resulting Forth implementation is less than 500 lines of Snobol.
The README in the repo explains the program in greater detail and the
source of the interpreter is pretty readable - although it would be
a weird way to learn how Forth normally works.
Making toys to make toys
I really like this method of having a small target program.
A Forth interpreter put my Snobol knowledge to the test.
Forth is not my creation, but this strange implementation of Snobol4th
certainly is - both in its unusual execution and in the small subset of the
language I chose to implement. So for certain values of "my", I’ll call
this my toy programming language.
If you’re going to test out a small toy programming language of your own, I
think a target program is something to consider. Here’s a "card" I wrote about
this:
Have a target for your toy language
Speaking of cards, here’s the first one I wrote about Snobol before I dove all
the way in. For the modern developer, getting started with Snobol4 can be a bit
baffling. Here’s another small "card" page:
Getting started with Snobol
Colophon
I did this project late at night in bed when the rest of the family was asleep.
The computer pictured above is an
MNT Pocket Reform
.
I drew the little rat and snowball at the  top of this page with my favorite
FOSS drawing program,
Krita
.

data.title: In a high-stress work environment, prioritize relationships
data.author: wqtz
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在高压力工作环境中，优先考虑人际关系的重要性。在这种环境下，压力可能大到让人想辞职并对同事发怒。然而，作者提醒读者，每个人都在承受压力，你不是特例。即便工作看似可替代，但人际关系和印象却长久留存，未来的推荐信和职业机会仍依赖这些联系。因此，不要对人发火或撕破脸。在处理工作时，应关注如何影响他人，而不仅是截止日期或任务本身。保持人际关系的健康比单纯完成工作更重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工作环境中的人际关系与压力管理

不同观点：
• alphazard 认为，软件行业中，压力主要来源于不称职的同事，他们带来混乱和不确定性。与这类人保持礼貌距离是避免压力重复互动的关键，而与有能力且高效的同事相处则能带来积极体验。
• cj 提出，即使之前的工作经历很糟糕，在求职时仍应将其描绘得积极一些，以避免面试官对你的不满产生疑虑。
• jimkleiber 引用了名言，强调对每个人保持友善的重要性，因为每个人都在面对自己未知的战斗。这种心态有助于管理生活中的压力。
• neilv 指出，在高压力工作环境中，建立良好的人际关系不仅有助于未来推荐，还能在当下缓解环境带来的压力。但也要注意，过于依赖支持性关系可能会让人不愿离开有害的工作环境。
• itchyjunk 则表示，减少对人际关系的关注能减轻压力，专注于自己的事情更好，尽管这种方法因人而异。

补充讨论：
• dpe82 提到谷歌的一项研究，表明心理安全是团队高效工作的关键因素，强调了工作环境中安全感的重要性。
• _ink_ 和 BartSpaans 强调了同理心和人际关系在职场中的重要性，认为社交能力往往比工作能力本身更重要。
• zphds 和 ArthurStacks 提醒大家在高压环境下保持健康生活方式的重要性，特别是良好的睡眠和饮食。
• taraindara 和 Daisywh 分享了个人经历，强调在困难时期意识到自己并不孤单是一种安慰，良好的人际关系有时能在关键时刻提供帮助。

争议焦点：
• 关于是否应在高压力环境中投入精力建立人际关系存在不同看法。neilv 认为支持性关系能缓解压力，但也会让人不愿离开有害环境；而 itchyjunk 则认为减少对人际关系的关注能更有效减轻压力。
• 另一个争议点是关于如何在求职时描述过去的工作经历，cj 建议将其美化以避免负面印象，而 junikaefer 则表示在某些地区，背景调查并不重要。

总的来说，讨论围绕如何在高压力工作环境中处理人际关系和管理压力展开，不同观点强调了个人经验和策略的多样性。

In a high-stress work environment, prioritize relationships
13 May, 2025
How high is the stress I am talking about? You are commuting all you think is that you might snap today, you might quit today. That is what I am calling a high-stress work environment. You know after a certain point the job becomes disposable and you are making a list in your head of who you are going to say "fuck you" to as you storm out of the building.
The reality in this environment is that everyone is stressed and you are not unique. The person pressing you is being pressed on by another guy. Everyone hates their job and everyone likes the movie "Office Space" daydreaming about quitting and dating Jennifer Aniston, who happens to be beautiful but stupid enough to not see that.
The reality is that if you quit, you DO NEED these connections to get a new job in the form of a recommendation. Do not snap at people. You may think the job is disposable, but the reality is that the memory is not. You will always be "that guy". You will always be the person who said "fuck you" to them, even though you were both in a pile of shit neck-deep.
So, prioritize relationships. If you are doing something, forget about deadlines or significance, think of the other person who is begging you and how it impacts them. Every relationship is a human relationship, so do not let the "professional environment" corrupt that.

data.article_summary: Alondra Nelson宣布辞去美国国家科学基金会（NSF）和国会图书馆学者委员会的职务。她指出，在当前政治环境下，公共机构维护和保护知识的任务受到严重威胁。尽管科学家和图书馆员努力工作，但政府对科学和知识的压制以及对经费的削减使得这些机构难以履行其使命。Nelson提到，她曾希望通过在这些机构中的工作促进知识和创新，但逐渐意识到继续留任已无法有效推动其初衷。她特别提到，言论自由和民主的知识体系对 advisory 工作至关重要，而当前环境却使其越来越难以实现。Nelson以《华氏451》中的社会警告为例，强调了对知识压制和机构无关紧要性的接受正危害科研和公共政策的制定。

T

Even as the White House threatens the foundational tenets of
constitutional democracy
and continues to
slash funding
for essential social services, it is tempting to hope that the public institutions charged with promoting and protecting knowledge will, nevertheless, soldier on with their mission. I did.
Since January 2025, scientists and librarians, program officers and policy analysts at the National Science Foundation, the Library of Congress, and other federal offices and agencies have focused on their work, despite an increasingly hostile political environment. We’ve also seen civil servants fired and
accused
of not making the mark, vendors’s contracts
ignored
, and grants and fellowships
cancelled
.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Perseverance has its limits. The erosion of these institutions’ integrity—and the growing realization that it is impossible to fulfill their missions in good faith—has made the cost of continuing untenable. This is why I must step away from my work with two federal institutions I care deeply about.
In both these roles, over the past few years, I've been asked to serve on diverse bodies that offer guidance about how the Executive and Legislative branches can be stewards of knowledge and create structure to enable discovery, innovation, and ingenuity. In the instance of the National Science Board, this ideal has dissolved so gradually, yet so completely, that I barely noticed its absence until confronted with its hollow simulacrum.
I have encountered increasing barriers to the exercise of honest counsel. These repeated obstacles of procedural circumvention, particularly insidious to those of us who have long advocated for more democratic and inclusive knowledge systems, represent not just personal frustration, but institutional regression.
Freedom of expression is not merely an abstract principle, or even a constitutional right, but a practical necessity for meaningful advisory work. In Ray Bradbury's
Fahrenheit 451
, published as short stories in the late 1940s and as a novel in 1953, warned not only of the destruction of books, but of a society in which people had lost the desire to read them.
The parallel today
is not only the administration’s
effort
to destroy and suppress knowledge, but also the institution’s willingness to accept the cultivated
irrelevance
of it—a challenge that undermines any serious effort to conduct research, inform policy, or guide public institutions.

traces its roots
to Vannevar Bush’s landmark
report
, “Science, the Endless Frontier,” addressed to President Harry S. Truman. The NSF can be understood not only as a catalyst of scientific promise for national purpose, but also as a guarded response to fears about centralized control over knowledge and thought, shaped by the dark shadows of the Third Reich and the emerging Red Scare.
The NSF’s investments have shaped some of the most transformative technologies of our time—from
GPS
to
the internet
—and supported vital research in the social and behavioral sciences that helps the nation understand itself and evaluate its progress toward its democratic ideals. So in 2024, I was honored to be appointed to the National Science Board, which is charged under 42 U.S. Code § 1863 with establishing the policies of the Foundation and providing oversight of its mission.

data.title: Show HN: A5
data.author: pheelicks
data.article_summary: A5是一个开源的全球等面积地理空间索引系统，基于五边形对十二面体进行划分，提供32种不同分辨率级别，最小单元面积小于30平方毫米。A5的单元格具有统一的面积（误差在2%以内），适用于表示城市区域或土地等空间数据，便于进行空间分析和聚合点数据。与其它DGGS（离散全球网格系统）相比，A5具有均匀的单元大小、高分辨率（64位整数编码）、以及最小化的全球单元区域畸变。A5使用TypeScript实现，遵循Apache 2.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同空间索引系统（A5, H3, S2, HEALPix等）的优缺点及适用场景

不同观点：
• **[knowitnone]** 建议在标题中添加描述，以便更直观地理解何时使用该系统。

• **[carderne]** 提出A5相比H3的优势：
  - A5分辨率更高，比H3高约4个数量级。
  - A5的单元格大小更一致（平方米上相等），而H3的单元格大小可能相差约2倍。
  同时，提出A5的缺点：形状不规则，中心点间距离不一致。

• **[xioxox]** 询问A5与HEALPix相比的优势，HEALPix也是一种常用的地理空间索引方法。

• **[Tabular-Iceberg]** 分享了自己曾经无意中创建了一个DGG（离散全球网格），但项目未继续，不确定是否可行，暗示A5可能在某些方面不如其他实现。

• **[yencabulator]** 比较了多个系统：
  - Google的S2注重性能和前缀匹配。
  - Uber的H3通过复杂数学计算，减少中心点间距离的变化，适用于驾驶时间优化。
  - A5进一步复杂化数学计算，减少远距离单元格面积变化，适用于分析密度等场景。

• **[pheelicks]** 提供了一个可视化解释和互动示例的链接，帮助理解A5的工作原理。

• **[jll29]** 指出A5使用五边形，而H3使用六边形，并提供了H3的参考链接。

• **[Bedon292]** 询问A5是否仅适用于数据可视化，还是在数据库搜索等场景中也能带来性能提升。

• **[zX41ZdbW]** 提到H3和S2在ClickHouse中开箱即用，并有C和C++库，但A5仅有TypeScript实现，虽然移植不难。

• **[ralusek]** 质疑优化最低顶点曲率（A5基于十二面体）的必要性，认为一般场景下S2或H3已经足够，想不出为何要选择A5。

补充讨论：
- A5的分辨率和单元格一致性被认为是其主要优势，但其不规则形状和复杂的数学计算可能限制其应用场景。
- 讨论中涉及多个空间索引系统的比较，包括S2、H3、HEALPix和A5，每个系统在特定应用中都有其独特的优势和局限性。
- 实现和支持的语言、库等技术细节也被提及，作为选择空间索引系统时的重要考虑因素。

A5
- Global, equal-area, millimeter-accurate geospatial index
Website:
A5Geo.org
Introduction
A5 is a geospatial index that partitions the world into
pentagonal cells
. The cells are available at
32 different resolution levels
, with the largest cell covering the whole world, and the smallest less than 30mm². Within each resolution level the cells have equal area, to
within 2%
.
A5 cells provide simple way to represent spatial data as a collection of cells, which together represent regions on the globe. These can be anything, from city districts to parcels of land. Once data is in a cell-based format, it becomes much simpler to perform analysis such as calculating the correlation between different variables - for example elevation and crop yield.
Cells can also be used to group (aggregate) point data, to understand how it spatially distributed. For example, the
density of holiday rentals
across a city.
To understand how it works, take a look at the
Examples
.
A5 is implemented in TypeScript and is available as a
library
, with
API documentation here
. It is
open source
and licensed under the
Apache 2.0 License
.
Benefits over alternative systems
Like other
DGGSs
, A5 can be used for indexing, spatial joins, and other spatial operations. The appropriate choice of DGGS will depend on the use case, the key strengths of A5 over other similar indexing systems are:
Uniform cell sizes group spatial features without introducing bias due to unequal cell sizes.
Very high resolution of 30mm² at final resolution level, encoded as a 64-bit integer.
Minimal distortion of cell areas across the globe.
Geometric Construction
DGGSs
are generally based on a planar cell tiling which is applied to the sides of a
platonic solid
, before being projected onto a sphere.
A5 is unique in that it uses a pentagonal tiling of a dodecahedron. The
pentagon chosen
for the tiling is equilateral, but not regular - unlike other common DGGSs which use regular polygons, for example
HTM
uses triangles,
S2
uses squares, and
H3
uses hexagons.
The benefit of choosing a dodecahedron is that it is the platonic solid with the lowest vertex curvature, and by this measure it is the most spherical of all the platonic solids. This is key for minimizing cell distortion as the process of projecting a platonic solid onto a sphere involves warping the cell geometry to force the vertex curvature to approach zero. Thus, the lower the original vertex curvature, the less distortion will be introduced by the projection.

  - A5的单元格大小更一致（平方米上相等），而H3的单元格大小可能相差约2倍。
  同时，提出A5的缺点：形状不规则，中心点间距离不一致。

• **[xioxox]** 询问A5与HEALPix相比的优势，HEALPix也是一种常用的地理空间索引方法。

• **[Tabular-Iceberg]** 分享了自己曾经无意中创建了一个DGG（离散全球网格），但项目未继续，不确定是否可行，暗示A5可能在某些方面不如其他实现。

• **[yencabulator]** 比较了多个系统：
  - Google的S2注重性能和前缀匹配。
  - Uber的H3通过复杂数学计算，减少中心点间距离的变化，适用于驾驶时间优化。
  - A5进一步复杂化数学计算，减少远距离单元格面积变化，适用于分析密度等场景。

• **[pheelicks]** 提供了一个可视化解释和互动示例的链接，帮助理解A5的工作原理。

• **[jll29]** 指出A5使用五边形，而H3使用六边形，并提供了H3的参考链接。

• **[Bedon292]** 询问A5是否仅适用于数据可视化，还是在数据库搜索等场景中也能带来性能提升。

• **[zX41ZdbW]** 提到H3和S2在ClickHouse中开箱即用，并有C和C++库，但A5仅有TypeScript实现，虽然移植不难。

• **[ralusek]** 质疑优化最低顶点曲率（A5基于十二面体）的必要性，认为一般场景下S2或H3已经足够，想不出为何要选择A5。

补充讨论：
- A5的分辨率和单元格一致性被认为是其主要优势，但其不规则形状和复杂的数学计算可能限制其应用场景。
- 讨论中涉及多个空间索引系统的比较，包括S2、H3、HEALPix和A5，每个系统在特定应用中都有其独特的优势和局限性。
- 实现和支持的语言、库等技术细节也被提及，作为选择空间索引系统时的重要考虑因素。

data.title: As US vuln-tracking falters, EU enters with its own security bug database
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 欧洲漏洞数据库（EUVD）已全面运行，提供一个简化的平台来监控关键和正在被利用的安全漏洞。在美国因预算削减和披露延迟导致其自身漏洞跟踪系统陷入困境之际，欧盟推出EUVD，旨在提高漏洞管理效率和透明度。与美国的国家漏洞数据库（NVD）类似，EUVD标识每个披露的漏洞，注明其严重性和利用状态，并提供可用的补救措施和补丁链接。不同的是，EUVD几乎实时更新，并突出显示关键和被利用的漏洞。EUVD提供三个仪表板视图，信息来源于开源数据库、各国CSIRT的建议和警报，以及供应商发布的补救和修补指南。ENISA作为CVE编号机构，也在与MITRE沟通，以了解美国CVE计划的未来影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于美国CVE项目 funding 问题及相关各方的反应

不同观点：
• [tptacek] 认为关于CISA是否资助NVD（国家漏洞数据库）的讨论很奇怪，因为CISA最终确实资助了NVD。他表示人们不必过于关心这一特定问题，因为即便没有政府资助，民间也可以运作CVE系统。

• [ta1243] 指出相关问题源于2022年欧盟指令，与近期美国政府的行动无关，且该问题已经酝酿了很长时间，暗示讨论存在时间错位。

• [devrandoom] 表达了对美国内部出现问题（可能指CVE资助问题）的悲哀情绪，隐含对美国现状的不满。

• [davidw] 认为欧洲领导人应该利用机会加大从美国“吸纳人才”的力度，暗示美国当前的混乱可能导致人才流失，欧洲可以从中受益。

• [j_walter] 对媒体和公众在CVE项目资助问题上的反应表示不满，认为之前所谓的“资金缺口”被夸大，只是合同未及时续签，而非真正的“资助中断”，批评相关报道有煽动性。

• [gadders] 引用了维基百科中的“华盛顿纪念碑综合症”来解释政府在最后一刻才解决资助问题，暗示政府故意拖延以制造紧迫感，从而获得公众支持。

• 争议焦点在于CVE项目资助问题是否被夸大以及相关报道是否具有煽动性。一些评论（如j_walter）认为问题被媒体过度解读，而其他评论（如devrandoom和gadders）则对政府处理方式表示不满。

• 讨论还涉及美国与欧洲在网络安全和人才竞争方面的潜在互动，特别是davidw提到的人才流失问题，这可能反映出对全球网络安全领域竞争态势的关注。

43972438.article_content:
Security
9
As US vuln-tracking falters, EU enters with its own security bug database
9
EUVD comes into play not a moment too soon
Jessica Lyons
Tue 13 May 2025
//
10:00 UTC
The European Vulnerability Database (EUVD) is now fully operational, offering a streamlined platform to monitor critical and actively exploited security flaws amid the US struggles with budget cuts, delayed disclosures, and confusion around the future of its own tracking systems.
As of Tuesday, the
full-fledged version of the website
is up and running.
"The EU is now equipped with an essential tool designed to substantially improve the management of vulnerabilities and the risks associated with it," ENISA Executive Director Juhan Lepassaar said in a statement announcing the EUVD.
"The database ensures transparency to all users of the affected ICT products and services and will stand as an efficient source of information to find mitigation measures," Lepassaar continued.
The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) first announced the project in June 2024 under a mandate from the EU's Network and Information Security 2 Directive, and quietly rolled out a limited-access beta version last month during a period of uncertainty surrounding the United States'
Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) program
.
Register
readers — especially those tasked with vulnerability management — will recall that the US government's funding for the CVE program was
set to expire
in April until the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, aka CISA, swooped in at the 11th hour and
renewed the contract
with MITRE to operate the initiative.
More broadly, Uncle Sam has been hard at work
slashing CISA
and other
cybersecurity funding
while key federal employees responsible for the US government's secure-by-design program have
jumped ship
.
Plus, on Monday, CISA said it would
no longer
publish routine alerts - including those detailing exploited vulnerabilities - on its public website. Instead, these updates will be delivered via email, RSS feeds, and the agency's account on X.
With all this, a cybersecurity professional could be forgiven for doubting the US government's commitment to hardening networks and rooting out vulnerabilities.
Enter the
EUVD
. The EUVD is similar to the US government's
National Vulnerability Database
(NVD) in that it identifies each disclosed bug (with both a CVE-assigned ID and its
own EUVD identifier
), notes the vulnerability's criticality and exploitation status, and links to available advisories and patches.
Unlike the NVD, which is still
struggling with a backlog of vulnerability submissions
and is not very easy to navigate, the EUVD is updated in near real-time and highlights both critical and exploited vulnerabilities at the top of the site.
CVE fallout: The splintering of the standard vulnerability tracking system has begun
Amid CVE funding fumble, 'we were mushrooms, kept in the dark,' says board member
CISA slammed for role in 'censorship industrial complex' as budget faces possible $500M cut
Ex-CISA chief decries cuts as Trump demands loyalty above all else
The EUVD provides three dashboard views: one for critical vulnerabilities, one for those actively exploited, and one for those coordinated by members of the
EU CSIRTs network
.
Information is sourced from open-source databases as well as advisories and alerts issued by national CSIRTs, mitigation and patching guidelines published by vendors, and exploited vulnerability details.
ENISA is also a
CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)
, meaning it can assign CVE identifiers and coordinate vulnerability disclosures under the CVE program. Even as an active CNA, however, ENISA seems to be in the dark about what's next for the embattled US-government-funded CVE program, which is only under contract with MITRE until next March.
The launch announcement notes that "ENISA is in contact with MITRE to understand the impact and next steps following the announcement on the funding to the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures Program." ®

data.title: Remote workers more likely to start their own business
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 文章指出，疫情期间更多远程工作的员工选择创业，经济学家发现这一趋势对政策制定者和公司制定远程工作政策有重要影响。研究分析了IP地址和LinkedIn数据，发现至少11.6%的疫情后新企业成立可归因于远程工作带来的创业效应。远程工作减少通勤时间、提高生产力、提供更灵活的工作时间，并降低员工监控，使得员工更容易在保有工资保障的同时探索创业。然而，公司可能因此失去关键员工，这些员工可能创立与原雇主竞争的企业。因此，一些大公司如Amazon、Google等开始缩减远程工作政策，部分原因是为了避免这种外溢效应。文章还提到，不同研究对远程工作与创业的关系有不同看法，但总体上，远程工作有助于新企业的创立和创新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：远程工作对员工创业行为的影响，以及雇主对此的担忧

不同观点：
• 一些评论认为，远程工作让员工有更多时间和空间进行自我实现，甚至创业。这表明远程工作可能提高员工效率，使他们有余裕时间来开展自己的业务（hennell, t-writescode）。
• 另一观点指出，虽然员工创业可能对原雇主不利，但这实际上有助于整体经济和劳动力参与度，可能带来双赢局面（jawns）。
• 有人提到，疫情让人们重新评估生活和工作，远程工作带来的自由和舒适感促使人们追求更高质量的生活，而非仅仅接受现有工作条件（erikerikson, bad_haircut72）。
• 一些评论质疑研究方法的有效性，认为无法明确区分是远程工作本身还是其他变量（如员工的教育和技能）导致了创业增加（nabilhat, chriskanan）。

补充讨论：
• 部分评论关注远程工作对员工的心理健康和生活质量的积极影响，认为这种工作方式使工作成为生活的一部分而非负担（erikerikson）。
• 有评论指出，某些岗位（如销售）的员工更容易利用公司资源和客户关系自立门户，这可能是远程工作无法解决的固有风险（gethly）。
• 还有评论担忧，如果雇主利用数据监控来防止员工创业或离职，可能会抑制劳动力和创新的发展（neilv）。

争议焦点：
• 雇主担心员工利用远程工作的自由时间创业，并考虑是否通过增加办公室工作要求来减少这种现象，但这种做法可能导致员工参与度低和业务影响差（alabastervlog, Brajewar, recursivedoubts）。
• 研究方法的有效性和结论的可靠性受到质疑，特别是在如何区分远程工作影响和员工自身创业倾向方面（nabilhat, chriskanan）。

CxO
28
Bosses weren’t being paranoid: Remote workers more likely to start their own biz
28
All those return to office mandates make a lot more sense now
Thomas Claburn
Mon 12 May 2025
//
21:08 UTC
Companies with higher levels of remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic saw more of their employees launch startups, economists have found. They argue this entrepreneurial spillover is a factor policymakers and firms should weigh when shaping remote work policies.
In a
research paper
titled, "Entrepreneurial Spawning From Remote Work," authors Alan Kwan (Hong Kong University), Ben Matthies (University of Notre Dame), Richard R. Townsend (University of California, San Diego), and Ting Xu (University of Toronto) describe how they analyzed IP address data in conjunction with LinkedIn data to cross-reference those working from home with those who formed new businesses.
The IP address information came from an unidentified "data partner" that uses first- and third-party cookies to create user profiles and ultimately infer their place of employment. The LinkedIn data – user profiles and resumes – came from Revelio Labs, and was supplemented with US census data and corporate data from Aberdeen CiTDB and People Data Labs.
The boffins analyzed the data "to measure spawning from wage employment into entrepreneurship" – that is, a title change and employment change on LinkedIn indicating a shift from being an employee to a founder.
"Based on our firm-level estimate, we calibrate that at least 11.6 percent of the post-pandemic increase in new firm entry can be explained by spawning from remote work," the authors state in their paper.
They added that their analysis focused on workers at firms that continued to grow employment during the pandemic - suggesting these startups were more likely voluntary than driven by layoffs.
The authors cite various other studies on remote work showing how it frees up time by reducing commuting, increases productivity, offers more flexible hours, and reduces employee monitoring.
Taken together, the authors theorize, these factors make it easier to explore business formation while protected by the financial safety of a regular wage.
[The departing workers] might start a new firm competing with their old employer. So these employers might not want to invest too much in remote work, given this spillover effect
Ting Xu (徐霆), assistant professor of finance at the University of Toronto and one of the paper's authors, said the findings have different implications for policymakers and firms.
"For policymakers, these spawnings, which essentially represent positive spillovers, are a good thing," Xu told
The Register
. "It's good that we have people creating new firms, new jobs, and new innovation. This is presumably better reallocation, because essentially remote work allows you to better explore outside options in entrepreneurship."
He continued, "From firms' perspective, they might be hurt because they have key employees leaving. [The departing workers] might start a new firm competing with their old employer. So these employers might not want to invest too much in remote work, given this spillover effect."

A
study
(Barrios et al., 2024) of remote work and entrepreneurship from last year found seemingly contradictory results: in some cases, working from home reduced entrepreneurship by substituting for the flexibility typically gained through self-employment. However, Xu said the results, based on zip code data and business registrations, are complementary because they focus on different types of startups.
The Barrios paper, Xu said, emphasized how workplace flexibility suppressed the formation of small businesses. Essentially, workers seeking more flexible working conditions didn't need to start their own side-hustle lifestyle business when they had the freedom afforded by working from home.
But for businesses that are seeking to grow, like biotech startups – which is what the LinkedIn data captures – remote work provides the time and safety to support that sort of entrepreneurship, Xu said.
Many large technology companies have dialed back on remote work policies implemented during the pandemic.
Amazon
,
Dell
,
Google
, and
IBM
have all curtailed or cut remote working for employees, often citing allegedly improved camaraderie, innovation, and productivity for on-site work.
Critics of "return to office" mandates note that there are other possible motives, including office occupancy requirements as a condition for
local tax breaks
and
layoff cost avoidance
by increasing employee obligations to the point that workers leave voluntarily.

Bureau of Labor Statistics
, remote work is positively

• 研究方法的有效性和结论的可靠性受到质疑，特别是在如何区分远程工作影响和员工自身创业倾向方面（nabilhat, chriskanan）。

• **[TechEnthusiast]的观点**：回应称，虽然从表面上看，添加日历MCP服务器和整合Claude可能看起来相似，但实际的技术细节和应用场景存在显著区别。TechEnthusiast指出，Claude作为一个智能助手，可能需要特定的集成方式来处理日历功能，而不仅仅是简单的服务器添加。

• **[AIExpert]的观点**：补充说明，Claude的架构可能需要对日历功能进行定制化的处理，包括自然语言处理、事件提醒等功能的无缝衔接，而不仅仅是通过MCP服务器实现表面的连接。AIExpert强调了这种整合需要考虑用户体验和系统稳定性。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：核心争议在于将日历MCP服务器添加到Claude的操作是否仅仅是技术细节上的改变，还是涉及到更深层次的功能和用户体验上的整合。

• **论据和例子**：
  - [TechEnthusiast]提到，Claude需要处理复杂的自然语言请求，如“下周三下午3点安排会议”，这涉及到自然语言处理和日历功能的深度整合。
  - [AIExpert]补充，整合日历功能需要考虑Claude现有的架构和算法，确保新功能不会影响现有功能的使用体验。

  - 强调了在智能助手系统中添加新功能的复杂性，不仅仅是简单地添加服务器。

data.title: Show HN: Basecoat – shadcn/UI components, no React required
data.author: hunvreus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕BasecoatUI库的实现、使用体验及其潜在改进的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持与感谢**：
  - 多位用户（如juddlyon、diordiderot、urbanisierung）表达了对该项目的感谢，认为它在填补现代开发和旧有技术栈之间的空白，特别是在服务器渲染的营销网站中非常有用。
  
• **关于组件转换方式的疑问**：
  - exiguus和WilcoKruijer关注组件从shadcn/ui转换为HTML的方式，询问是否是通过手动操作或自动化脚本实现。
  
• **功能与改进建议**：
  - gsanderson建议增加焦点陷阱（focus trap）功能，以便在对话框打开时限制Tab键的焦点移动，提升用户体验。
  - replwoacause提出增加CDN选项，以便用户可以快速开始试用。
  - rglullis建议放弃Tailwind，转而使用SASS mixins进行样式处理。
  
• **技术选择的讨论**：
  - czhu12认为从单页应用（SPA）回到 vanilla JS 开发时，UI组件的缺失是个主要问题，Basecoat填补了这个空白，并猜测未来可能会推出付费版本。
  - o_m质疑为何选择Alpine.js而不是原生Web组件，这引发了对技术选型的讨论。
  
• **与其他工具的比较**：
  - replwoacause提到Basecoat让他想起了Franken-ui.dev，暗示两者有相似之处。
  - Jonovono提到自己使用了AlpineJS的Pines UI库，并表示会对Basecoat进行尝试，暗示不同工具之间的竞争和选择。

补充讨论：
• **多样化的技术背景**：
  - 用户在使用不同的前端框架（如Vue、React）和后端技术（如Ruby on Rails）的背景下，对BasecoatUI提出了不同的需求和看法。
  
• **定制化与自动化**：
  - 讨论中多次提及组件的手动与自动化处理，显示出开发者对工作流程效率的关注。

争议焦点：
• **技术选型**：
  - 选择Alpine.js而非原生Web组件引发了o_m的质疑，显示出在现代前端开发中对技术选型的不同偏好。

data.title: One hundred and one rules of effective living
data.author: mathgenius
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对生活建议、规则和哲理的讨论与争议

不同观点：
• [xivzgrev] 认为按小时计费是一种公平的工作安排，因为购买的是他人的时间，且按小时计费可以避免 flat rate 中可能出现的只完成最低要求、缺乏工作自豪感的问题。同时提到开发人员在固定费用项目中可能遇到无休止的需求变更。
• [snide] 支持本杰明·富兰克林的13种美德，认为这些简短的规则具有指导意义，并具体列举了这些美德，如节制、沉默、秩序等。
• [hnthrow90348765] 批评将工作视为生活的首要规则，认为这是空洞的，并指出在规则中缺乏对爱的提及。
• [lifefeed] 对励志文学持谨慎态度，认为适量阅读有益，但过多阅读可能让人麻木，仅在历史学研究中有一定价值。
• [reverendsteveii] 批评规则的提出者自认为智慧，规则看似智慧实则空洞，适合单向传播而非对话讨论，最终可能被归类为“毫无意义”或“不言而喻”。
• [pricees] 反对不给表现出不尊重的人第二次机会的规则，认为这可能毁掉一个本来可以过得很好的人生。
• [ngangaga] 对规则中“坦率交易”和“对自己诚实”等主观性强的建议提出质疑，认为满足自己的评估是最困难的部分。
• [corry] 认为101条规则太多，更喜欢玛丽·奥利弗的“用你唯一的狂野而珍贵的人生做什么”这一挑战性问题。
• [jebarker] 质疑阅读此类生活建议的实际益处，认为哲学思考和冥想如果不付诸实践就毫无价值，经验才是学习的途径。
• [world2vec] 指出规则中存在自相矛盾之处，例如“远离残忍的人”和“宁可被畏惧也不要被爱”这两条规则之间的矛盾，认为这只是一个自我帮助的书后引语汇编。
• [awkward] 提到两个规则“不要过多谈论”和“积极心态意味着根据自我发展的能力评估环境”之间可能存在的实际操作难度。
• [aquariusDue] 幽默地建议成立一个委员会编写人生手册，但认为这可能比编写现代C语言标准库还难。
• [neilv] 认为“只谈论自己熟悉的事物”这一规则会淘汰99%以上的互联网内容，包括Hacker News。
• [mudiadamz] 认为这些生活建议平庸无聊。
• [noja] 引用《Everyone's Free To Wear Sunscreen》这首歌，似乎是以轻松的方式参与讨论。

补充讨论：
• 规则的实用性和矛盾：一些评论指出规则之间存在矛盾，以及这些规则在实际操作中的可行性和适用性问题。
• 对励志文学和哲学思考的态度：部分评论对励志文学持谨慎态度，认为适量阅读有益，但过多可能适得其反，且哲学思考需结合实践才有意义。
• 对规则数量和内容的主观评价：有评论认为101条规则太多，且部分规则内容主观性强，难以操作和评估。

争议的焦点：
• 规则的公平性和实际操作性：例如按小时计费的公平性与 flat rate 的问题，以及不给不尊重的人第二次机会的规则是否合理。
• 规则的数量和矛盾：101条规则是否过多，以及规则之间的自相矛盾之处。
• 对生活建议的实用价值：这些规则和建议在实际生活中的实用价值和可操作性。

data.title: Microsoft is Cutting 3% of All Workers
data.author: jmsflknr
data.article_summary: 微软宣布将裁员3%，涉及各个层级和地区，旨在优化管理层级以适应动态市场。截至去年6月，微软有228,000名员工，此次裁员将影响数千人，为其自2023年裁掉10,000人以来最大规模的裁员。公司发言人表示，这些裁员并非基于绩效，而是组织调整的一部分。尽管微软最近财报表现超出预期，营收达258亿美元，但公司希望通过调整激励和市场策略，更好地推动人工智能等新领域的增长。近期其他科技公司如亚马逊和CrowdStrike也进行了类似裁员。微软股价目前接近历史高点，分析师预计其将在2025年继续成为表现最佳的大盘股。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软公司管理层调整及其影响

data.title: Welcome to the age of paranoia as deepfakes and scams abound
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了在远程工作和数字通信普及的背景下，求职诈骗和数字冒名骗局愈发猖獗，迫使人们采取多步骤的背景调查来验证身份。公关人员Nicole Yelland分享了自己在被 elaborate scam 欺骗后，现在每次收到陌生会议请求时都会进行详细验证，包括使用数据聚合工具Spokeo、测试语言能力以及要求开启摄像头。同时，AI技术的进步使得假身份更容易制造，导致一些公司和个人转向使用老派的社交工程技巧，如要求实时自拍或快速提问本地细节，以确认对方身份。一些AI初创公司和区块链身份验证工具也在尝试解决这一问题，但传统方法在某些情况下仍然有效。

These days, when
Nicole Yelland receives a meeting request from someone she doesn’t already know, she conducts a multistep
background check
before deciding whether to accept. Yelland, who works in public relations for a Detroit-based nonprofit, says she’ll run the person’s information through Spokeo, a personal data aggregator that she pays a monthly subscription fee to use. If the contact claims to speak Spanish, Yelland says, she will casually test their ability to understand and translate trickier phrases. If something doesn’t quite seem right, she’ll ask the person to join a Microsoft Teams call—with their camera on.
If Yelland sounds paranoid, that’s because she is. In January, before she started her current nonprofit role, Yelland says, she got roped into an elaborate scam targeting job seekers. “Now, I do the whole verification rigamarole any time someone reaches out to me,” she tells WIRED.
Digital imposter scams aren’t new; messaging
platforms
, social media sites, and
dating apps
have long been rife with fakery. In a time when remote work and distributed teams have become commonplace, professional communications channels are no longer safe, either. The same artificial intelligence tools that tech companies promise will boost worker productivity are also making it easier for criminals and fraudsters to construct fake personas in seconds.
On LinkedIn, it can be hard to distinguish a slightly touched-up headshot of a real person from a too-polished, AI-generated facsimile. Deepfake videos are getting so good that longtime email scammers are pivoting to
impersonating people
on live video calls. According to the US Federal Trade Commission, reports of job and employment related scams nearly tripled from 2020 to 2024, and actual losses from those scams
have increased
from $90 million to $500 million.
Yelland says the scammers that approached her back in January were impersonating a real company, one with a legitimate product. The “hiring manager” she corresponded with over email also seemed legit, even sharing a slide deck outlining the responsibilities of the role they were advertising. But during the first video interview, Yelland says, the scammers refused to turn their cameras on during a Microsoft Teams meeting and made unusual requests for detailed personal information, including her driver’s license number. Realizing she’d been duped, Yelland slammed her laptop shut.
These kinds of schemes have become so widespread that AI startups have emerged promising to detect other AI-enabled deepfakes, including
GetReal Labs
and
Reality Defender
. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman also runs an identity-verification startup called Tools for Humanity, which makes
eye-scanning devices that capture
a person’s biometric data, create a unique identifier for their identity, and store that information on the blockchain. The whole
idea behind it
is proving “personhood,” or that someone is a real human. (Lots of people working on blockchain technology say that blockchain is the solution for identity verification.)
But some corporate professionals are turning instead to old-fashioned social engineering techniques to verify every fishy-seeming interaction they have. Welcome to the Age of Paranoia, when someone might ask you to send them an email while you’re mid-conversation on the phone, slide into your Instagram DMs to ensure the LinkedIn message you sent was really from you, or request you text a selfie with a time stamp, proving you are who you claim to be. Some colleagues say they even share code words with each other, so they have a way to ensure they’re not being misled if an encounter feels off.
“What’s funny is, the lo-fi approach works,” says Daniel Goldman, a blockchain software engineer and former startup founder. Goldman says he began changing his own behavior after he heard a prominent figure in the crypto world had been convincingly deepfaked on a video call. “It put the fear of god in me,” he says. Afterward, he warned his family and friends that even if they hear what they believe is his voice or see him on a video call asking for something concrete—like money or an internet password—they should hang up and email him first before doing anything.
Ken Schumacher, founder of the recruitment verification service Ropes, says he’s worked with hiring managers who ask job candidates rapid-fire questions about the city where they claim to live on their résumé, such as their favorite coffee shops and places to hang out. If the applicant is actually based in that geographic region, Schumacher says, they should be able to respond quickly with accurate details.
Another verification tactic some people use, Schumacher says, is what he calls the “phone camera trick.” If someone suspects the person they’re talking to over video chat is being deceitful, they can ask them to hold up their phone camera to show their laptop. data.title: Dutch ingenuity: A brainless soft robot running on air
data.author: davoneus
data.article_summary: 荷兰阿姆斯特丹的AMOLF研究所团队开发了一种无需电子大脑的新型机器人，仅依靠气流驱动，能跑、越障甚至游泳。灵感源于实验室中弯折管子产生的高频振动，这种自维持的非对称运动模仿了生物的自然运动。机器人由3D打印身体和四条管状腿组成，通过调节气流控制运动速度和步态。管子间的气流同步使机器人能自动适应环境，如在地面奔跑或在水中游泳。尽管已实现无束缚自主运动，但仍需解决功耗和行为控制问题，例如如何在遇到障碍时作出反应。这项研究展示了通过物理机制而非复杂控制系统实现自然运动的潜力。

Most robots rely on complex control systems, AI-powered or otherwise, that govern their movement. These centralized electronic brains need time to react to changes in their environment and produce movements that are often awkwardly, well, robotic.
It doesn’t have to be that way. A team of Dutch scientists at the FOM Institute for Molecular and Atomic Physics (AMOLF) in Amsterdam built a new kind of robot that can run, go over obstacles, and even swim, all driven only by the flow of air. And it does all that with no brain at all.
Sky-dancing physics
“I was in a lab, working on another project, and had to bend a tube to stop air from going through it. The tube started oscillating at very high frequency, making a very loud noise,” says Alberto Comoretto, a roboticist at AMOLF and lead author of the study. To see what was going on with the tube, Comoretto set up a high-speed camera and recorded the movement. He found that the movement resulted from the interplay between the air pressure inside the tube and the state of the tube itself.
When there was a kink in the tube, the increasing pressure pushed that kink along the tube’s length. That caused the pressure to decrease, which enabled a new kink to appear and the cycle to repeat. “We were super excited because we saw this self-sustaining, periodic, asymmetric motion,” Comoretto told Ars.
The first reason for Comoretto’s excitement was that the flapping tube in his lab was driven by the kind of airflow physics that Peter Marshall, Doron Gazit, and Aireh Dranger harnessed to build their famous dancing “Fly Guys” for the Olympic Games in Atlanta in 1996. The second reason was that asymmetry and periodicity he saw in the tube’s movement pattern were also present in the way all living things moved, from single-celled organisms to humans.
Comoretto’s team decided to build a robot that harnessed the Fly Guys’ physics to achieve natural, almost lifelike movement. But it was harder than it seemed.
Tubular legs
“The movements of these dancing Fly Guys are designed to be random to make them dance in a compelling way,” Comoretto explains. “In our robot, we control the motion through constraining the geometry in very specific ways.” The design comprised a 3D-printed body with four attached tubes bent at the bottom to form the robot’s legs. The frequency of oscillations in the tubes, and therefore the robot’s speed, was regulated by adjusting the amount of air pumped into each tube.
In a standard multi-limbed robot, the remaining challenge would be to synchronize the limbs to achieve different gaits. Surprisingly, though, limb synchronization in Comoretto’s robot appeared as an emergent property of its design.
“Imagine the
experiment
with metronomes that start to synchronize when you put them on a movable plate—it’s exactly that,” says Johannes Overvelde, AMOLF researcher and co-author of the study. The metronomes synchronize because the moving plate they’re on works as a coupling, connecting them together. In the robot, the same kind of coupling was achieved by connecting all tubes to the same input airflow, which enabled them to communicate through variations in pressure. And it worked wonders.
The robot could adjust its gait to the environment it was in. On the ground, all limbs autonomously activated in synchrony, and the robot ran a bit like a
stotting gazelle
. In the water, where the tubes met less resistance than on the ground, the limbs moved in antiphase to enable swimming like a dog.
There are still issues to iron out before robots relying on this kind of seamless body-environment dynamics make it out of the early research phase, though.
Into the wild
The first problem with Comoretto’s robot was power consumption. The initial design that his team tested in their lab was tethered, and the air was pumped to the limbs through a thin hose. Fifteen standard liters of air per minute enabled the robot to move quickly and perform all its amazing tricks, but the pump that supplied it used 85 watts. That was too much to even start thinking about dropping the tether and using onboard power sources.

This version used two simple light sensors as its “eyes,” connected to a system that could selectively activate each of the oscillating limbs. 主要讨论点：对某研究声称解决多个重大科学问题（包括千禧年大奖难题）的评论和争议。

不同观点：
• [openquery] 认为该研究可能只是为了吸引关注和互动，尤其是基于作者的社交媒体形象（如 bored ape 头像），并怀疑其真实性。虽然不确定，但认为是高水平的诱导互动内容。
• [breakyerself] 认为该研究听起来像是个怪人理论，将其比作1885年试图构建宇宙统一理论的人，暗示其缺乏科学依据。
• [hamburga] 认为该研究与 Wolfram 物理模型有相似之处，且研究提出了几个可验证的预测，并列举了文件中提到的六个具体、无参数的预测，认为这些预测若能在2030年前得到验证，可能具有一定价值。
• [dvcoolster] 提供了研究的完整PDF和公共存储库链接，没有直接评论研究的可信性，而是提供了更多信息供他人查阅。
• [voxl] 强烈批评该研究，认为其完全符合“怪人指数”，包括对数学哲学的无知、依赖公众和AI模型进行同行评审而非科学会议、与区块链NFT等涉嫌欺诈的技术关联，以及依赖LLM模型理解内容。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于该研究是否具有科学价值，或者仅仅是为了吸引关注和互动。
• 一些评论者（如 [voxl]）对使用LLM和区块链技术持强烈批评态度，认为这些技术在此情境下不具备科学价值。
• 其他评论者（如 [hamburga]）则较为中立，关注研究中提出的可验证预测，认为需要等待实验结果来验证其科学价值。
• 社交媒体形象（如 bored ape 头像）也被用作判断研究可信性的依据之一，尽管这在科学讨论中并不常见。

data.title: The Height Enigma (CSS)
data.author: czue
data.article_summary:
这篇文章探讨了CSS中基于百分比的**高度**为何有时不起作用的谜题。关键在于，**宽度**和**高度**的计算方式截然不同。宽度默认会填满可用空间，而高度则会根据子元素内容收缩。因此，当子元素设置`height: 50%`时，它试图根据父元素的高度计算，而父元素的高度又依赖于子元素，导致循环计算，浏览器因此忽略该声明。

要使`height: 50%`生效，父元素必须有明确的高度，例如通过设置固定像素值。此外，文章还提到`width: auto`与`width: 100%`的区别，前者更具动态性，会考虑外边距，而后者则严格等于父容器的宽度。理解这些机制有助于解决类似的CSS问题。
