data.title: FCC threatens EchoStar licenses for spectrum that SpaceX wants to use
data.author: unsnap_biceps
data.article_summary: 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）主席布兰登·卡尔威胁撤销EchoStar的频谱许可证，因其被指未充分利用频谱资源，特别是2 GHz频段，该频段被SpaceX等公司觊觎。卡尔要求审查EchoStar是否按规定提供5G服务。EchoStar主席查尔斯·厄尔根为公司辩护，但承认无法预测FCC程序的结果。SpaceX此前向FCC提交的数据显示，EchoStar几乎未使用该频段提供5G服务，并建议重新分配频谱。EchoStar反驳称，SpaceX的指控是企图获取更多免费频谱。此外，VTel Wireless也 petition 要求FCC重新考虑延长EchoStar建设期限的决定。FCC现正征求公众意见，以评估EchoStar对2 GHz频段的使用情况及其合规性。此事引发EchoStar股价下跌8%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FCC威胁撤销EchoStar的频谱许可证，因其被指未充分利用频谱资源，而其他公司如SpaceX则希望获得这些频谱资源。

不同观点：
• [jjtheblunt] 认为标题有故意引发愤怒的嫌疑，因为看起来像是在挑起争端。他指出，FCC威胁撤销EchoStar的许可证，因为EchoStar被指未充分利用其频谱资源，而这一频谱正是其他公司（如SpaceX）所渴望获得的。

• [Neywiny] 同意"用它或失去它"的原则，但对频谱的具体大小提出质疑。他认为，虽然EchoStar拥有40MHz的总频谱，但在2GHz频段上，这样的带宽实际上相对较窄，可能不足以实现重大应用或效益。

• [vorpalhex] 强烈支持"用它或失去它"的原则，特别是在频谱分配上。他认为，如果一个公司拥有巨大的频谱分配但未能有效利用或提供实际的益处，那么收回频谱是公平的。他隐含支持像SpaceX这样的公司获得更多频谱资源，因为它们可能更有效地利用这些资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于EchoStar是否在浪费频谱资源，以及是否应该根据"用它或失去它"的原则收回其许可证。
• 对频谱的实际可用性和其对社会或行业的效益有不同的看法，部分评论者认为40MHz在某些频段上可能已经足够大，而其他人则认为如果未能充分利用，就应重新分配。
• 讨论还涉及到标题是否具有煽动性，表明在信息传播中如何呈现问题可能影响公众和利益相关者的反应。

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr has threatened to revoke EchoStar licenses for radio frequency bands coveted by rival firms including SpaceX, which alleges that EchoStar is underutilizing the spectrum.
"I have directed agency staff to begin a review of EchoStar's compliance with its federal obligations to provide 5G service throughout the United States per the terms of its federal spectrum licenses," Carr wrote in a May 9 letter to EchoStar Chairman Charles Ergen. EchoStar and its affiliates "hold a large number of FCC spectrum licenses that cover a significant amount of spectrum," the letter said.
Ergen defended his company's wireless deployment but informed investors that EchoStar "cannot predict with any degree of certainty the outcome" of the FCC proceedings. The letter from Carr and Ergen's statement is included in a Securities and Exchange Commission
filing
submitted by EchoStar today. EchoStar's stock price was down about 8 percent in trading today.
EchoStar bought Dish Network in December 2023 and offers wireless service under the Boost Mobile brand. As The Wall Street Journal
notes
, the firm "has spent years wiring thousands of cellphone towers to help Boost become a wireless operator that could rival AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, but the project has been slow-going. Boost's subscriber base has shrunk in the five years since Ergen bought the brand from Sprint."
SpaceX did some measurements
Last month, Starlink operator SpaceX
told the FCC
that "new data confirms what most people already suspected—Dish Network barely uses the AWS-4 [2 GHz] band, if it is used at all, to provide 5G or any other service to American consumers." SpaceX said one of its satellites "measured the power spectral density (PSD) levels in those bands and found that DISH's use of the band is
de minimis
at best."
SpaceX urged the FCC to reallocate the spectrum, saying "the 2 GHz band remains ripe for sharing among next-generation satellite systems that seek to finally make productive use of the spectrum for consumers and first responders." EchoStar
countered
that SpaceX's filing is "intended to cloak another land grab for even more free spectrum," and that its "methodology is completely nonsensical, given that EchoStar's terrestrial deployment is subject to population-based milestones that EchoStar has repeatedly demonstrated in status reports."
"If SpaceX had done a basic search of public filings, it would know that EchoStar extensively utilizes the 2 GHz band and that the Commission itself has confirmed the coverage, utilization, and methodology for assessing the quality of EchoStar's 5G network based on independent drive-tests," EchoStar told the FCC. "EchoStar's deployment already reaches over 80 percent of the United States population with over 23,000 5G sites deployed."
There is also a pending
petition
filed by Vermont-based VTel Wireless, which asked the FCC to reconsider a 2024 decision to extend EchoStar construction deadlines for several spectrum bands. VTel was outbid by Dish in auctions for licenses to use
AWS H Block
and
AWS-3
bands.
"In this case, teetering on the verge of bankruptcy, EchoStar found itself unable to meet the commitments previously made to the Commission in connection with its approval of T-Mobile's merger with Sprint—an approval predicated on EchoStar constructing a fourth nationwide 5G broadband network by June 14, 2025," VTel wrote in its October 2024 petition. "But with no notice to or input from the public, WTB [the FCC's Wireless Telecommunications Bureau] apparently cut a deal with EchoStar to give it yet more time to complete that network and finally put its wireless licenses to use."
FCC seeks public input
Carr's letter said he asked FCC staff to investigate EchoStar's compliance with construction deadlines and "to issue a public notice seeking comment on the scope and scale of MSS [mobile satellite service] utilization in the 2 GHz band that is currently licensed to EchoStar or its affiliates." The AWS-4 band (2000-2020 MHz and 2180-2200 MHz) was originally designated for satellite service. The FCC
decided
to also allow terrestrial use of the frequencies in 2012 to expand mobile broadband access.
The FCC Space Bureau announced yesterday that it is
seeking comment
on EchoStar's use of the 2GHz spectrum, and the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau is
seeking comment
on VTel's petition for reconsideration.
"In 2019, EchoStar's predecessor, Dish, agreed to meet specific buildout obligations in connection with a number of spectrum licenses across several different bands," Carr wrote. "In particular, the FCC agreed to relax some of EchoStar's then-existing buildout obligations in exchange for EchoStar's commitment to put its licensed spectrum to work deploying a nationwide 5G broadband network. EchoStar promised—among other things—that

data.title: Mason: A declarative build tool on top of Dagger
data.author: gk1
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者开发的一个声明式构建工具Mason，它基于Dagger构建系统。作者喜欢Dagger的强大功能，但发现其在大规模部署时存在一些问题，如对项目的显著影响、使用复杂（需要手动处理环境变量和文件系统）、多次调用才能完成任务等。为解决这些问题，Mason提供了一个简单的CLI用户体验，采用声明式配置文件，支持项目间共享模块，并具有可扩展性。Mason采用两阶段设计（计划/应用），通过配置文件生成Dagger脚本并执行。它简化了模块调用和变量传递，定义了不同构建阶段（测试、打包、发布等），统一了UX。Mason让Dagger使用更简便，尤其在企业环境中，能快速集成现有Dagger模块，并保持一致的开发体验。不过，对于单一项目可能显得多余。未来计划包括增加报告功能等。

Mason: a declarative build tool on top of Dagger
I wrote something. A build tool.
A declarative build tool on top of Dagger
.
Why?
Because I really like
Dagger
, but as I tried to spread its usage at
work
, I found that in its current form, it was difficult to scale its deployment.
My main concerns are:
It has a
significant impact on the projects
where you use it. If you create a specific module for the project, even if you reuse other modules for most of the work, you'll still need to write a lot of boilerplate code to make it work.
Its
usage is non-trivial
, meaning that if you were used to running
make build
, you won't be able to replace it with just
dagger run build
. You'll need to give it a few more arguments, because it won't automatically read your environment variables or host filesystem. And even worse, you'll need multiple calls if you want to export files, such as test results, and exit with an error code in case of failure.
What I'd like is:
a
simple CLI UX, common across all projects
.
Maven
got it right years ago: you see a
pom.xml
file, you know that running
mvn package
will produce the artifacts.
a
declarative and easy way to configure projects
that are mostly similar, and could share the same Dagger module, but with different parameters.
GoReleaser
is a good example of this: a single configuration file to configure how to produce artifacts, where to publish them, etc.
Kubernetes
is another good example: a generic envelope common to all kinds of resources, but a specific spec, making it easy to filter resources and implement custom logic for each of them.
an
extensible system
, making it easy to implement custom logic in any language.
Dagger
is a great tool for this, with its powerful modules.
I had this idea in my mind for a while, thinking about how to "orchestrate" Dagger modules in a nice and declarative way. And when the Dagger team released the
Interactive Shell
, with the ability to run Dagger scripts, I quickly saw how it could solve some of my concerns. I just needed something to generate the "right" script based on a configuration file.
We can solve any problem by introducing an extra level of indirection.
What about
using Dagger to generate the Dagger script
? A 2 phases plan/apply design, where the first phase generates the script, and the second phase runs it. The configuration file would be split into multiple independent resources, each with a kind/group... or rather, kind/module. This way, we have an easy way to call any module, to process its own resources, and generate a script.
Our build tool can now be very simple: a coordinator that calls Dagger twice, and in the middle merges the scripts to produce a single one. Need to use the output of one module in another? Just define a variable in the first module and use it in the second one.
We just need to define a few conventions, such as
phases
-
test
,
lint
,
package
,
publish
- to handle the UX topic. Running the
test
phase will filter the scripts to only include the relevant ones. No need to guess which module to run or which arguments to pass.
Writing a build tool on top of Dagger really highlights the power of Dagger:
Caching? Don't care, Dagger handles it.
plugin system? Dagger modules.
sandboxed execution? Dagger handles it.
Nice TUI? Of course.
Replacing Dagger with
Mason
What does that change? Everything and not that much ;-)
Everything
, because:
I need to replace all the "local" Dagger modules with YAML configuration files
I need to replace the multiple Dagger calls from my CI config with a single call to Mason
I need to write new Dagger modules to process the new configuration files
And
not that much
, because:
I can still re-use my existing Dagger modules as-is, if I write new modules to "only" generate the scripts
Or I can extend my existing Dagger modules to also generate a script, in addition to their original purpose
Under the hood, it's still Dagger, so same UIs: TUI, Web UI, etc.
Is it worth it?
In a corporate environment, where you might have specific ways to connect to systems, publish artifacts, etc, chances are that you already have custom Dagger modules. Some kind of private Daggerverse. With support for Go projects, Python projects, etc.
In this case, "daggerizing" a new project by just adding a few YAML files is simple, fast, and easy to maintain. On top of that, the ability for the developers to switch between projects and still have the same UX is a big plus.
But if you have a single project, it might seem overkill to add this extra layer...
Next steps
This is only the beginning.
Release early, release often
.
There are still a lot of things to do, such as some kind of "reporting" feature, to allow any module to analyse the result. A pluggable sys

data.author: winwang

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPU加速的大数据处理工具，尤其是与现有Spark加速器（如Spark RAPIDS、Gluten + Velox、DataFusion Comet）的比较与协作可能性，以及数据处理中的兼容性、性能和数据本地化问题。

不同观点：
• andygrove：对项目是否会与现有的开源Spark加速器（如Spark RAPIDS、Gluten + Velox、DataFusion Comet）进行合作或扩展提出疑问。他认为这些项目已经有多年发展且有专门团队支持，特别是Spark RAPIDS和Gluten + Velox已经在利用GPU。他还指出Spark兼容性非常困难，特别是在处理不同硬件架构和语言时。最后，他关心项目在性能与兼容性之间的权衡。

• sitkack：提到与CUDA相关的其他项目，如Bend和HVM，引入了更多关于GPU计算的背景信息。

• dogman123：表达了对项目的潜在应用兴趣，特别是针对大规模数据混洗问题，提到当前使用Glue成本过高。

• wenbin：将项目与Heavy.ai（前身为MapD）进行比较，暗示项目在市场上的定位可能与其他类似工具重叠。

• s2radhak：关注数据本地化问题，尤其是与S3/GCS/blobstore集成的解决方案。

• jelder：询问项目与PG-Strom项目之间的关系。

• random17：对GPU加速在哪些工作负载下有显著影响以及哪些工作负载仍面临挑战表示好奇，特别是对于需要大规模混洗的查询。

• threeseed：提到NVIDIA的RAPIDS和Spark-RAPIDS项目，并指出这些工具已经在AWS上得到支持，暗示市场上已有成熟的解决方案。

• mritchie712：引用了一篇关于BigQuery用户不需要处理大规模数据的文章，讨论了大数据处理的实际需求，并推荐了duckdb和MotherDuck。

• debarshri：回忆Hadoop时代的数据本地化处理概念，并询问当数据存储在bucket中时是否会产生传输成本。

• Boxxed：对数据来自GCS时GPU的优势表示怀疑，认为CPU仍然需要处理所有数据，询问是否有机制保持数据在GPU中活跃。

• achennupati：询问项目与AWS EMR上使用GPU实例的Spark-RAPIDS有何不同，项目是基于Spark-RAPIDS构建还是一个更定制化的解决方案。

• _zoltan_：提到VeloxCon会议中关于GPU处理和Velox与cuDF集成的讨论，提供了相关的技术背景。

• billy1kaplan：表示对项目的长期关注，并对项目的进展表示赞赏。

• latchkey：表示愿意提供免费的AMD MI300x VM用于构建/测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是项目与现有Spark加速器的关系及区别，特别是兼容性与性能的平衡。
• 数据本地化问题在使用云存储（如S3/GCS）时显得尤为重要，如何优化数据传输和处理成本是讨论的一个重点。
• 项目在GPU加速大数据处理中的独特性和创新性也受到关注，特别是在已有类似解决方案的情况下。

• dogman123：表达了对项目的潜在应用兴趣，特别是针对大规模数据混洗问题，提到当前使用Glue成本过高。

• wenbin：将项目与Heavy.ai（前身为MapD）进行比较，暗示项目在市场上的定位可能与其他类似工具重叠。

• s2radhak：关注数据本地化问题，尤其是与S3/GCS/blobstore集成的解决方案。

• jelder：询问项目与PG-Strom项目之间的关系。

• random17：对GPU加速在哪些工作负载下有显著影响以及哪些工作负载仍面临挑战表示好奇，特别是对于需要大规模混洗的查询。

• threeseed：提到NVIDIA的RAPIDS和Spark-RAPIDS项目，并指出这些工具已经在AWS上得到支持，暗示市场上已有成熟的解决方案。

• mritchie712：引用了一篇关于BigQuery用户不需要处理大规模数据的文章，讨论了大数据处理的实际需求，并推荐了duckdb和MotherDuck。

• debarshri：回忆Hadoop时代的数据本地化处理概念，并询问当数据存储在bucket中时是否会产生传输成本。

• Boxxed：对数据来自GCS时GPU的优势表示怀疑，认为CPU仍然需要处理所有数据，询问是否有机制保持数据在GPU中活跃。

• achennupati：询问项目与AWS EMR上使用GPU实例的Spark-RAPIDS有何不同，项目是基于Spark-RAPIDS构建还是一个更定制化的解决方案。

• _zoltan_：提到VeloxCon会议中关于GPU处理和Velox与cuDF集成的讨论，提供了相关的技术背景。

• billy1kaplan：表示对项目的长期关注，并对项目的进展表示赞赏。

• latchkey：表示愿意提供免费的AMD MI300x VM用于构建/测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是项目与现有Spark加速器的关系及区别，特别是兼容性与性能的平衡。
• 数据本地化问题在使用云存储（如S3/GCS）时显得尤为重要，如何优化数据传输和处理成本是讨论的一个重点。
• 项目在GPU加速大数据处理中的独特性和创新性也受到关注，特别是在已有类似解决方案的情况下。

data.title: Republicans Try to Cram Ban on AI Regulation into Budget Reconciliation Bill
data.author: spenvo
data.article_summary: 共和党人试图通过预算调解法案禁止各州在未来10年内对人工智能（AI）进行任何监管。根据肯塔基州众议员Brett Guthrie提出的法案内容，各州及地方政府将被禁止执行任何针对AI模型、系统或自动化决策系统的法律或法规。该法案若通过，将影响诸如加州和纽约等州已实施的关于AI透明的法律，例如要求医疗提供者披露使用生成式AI和进行偏见审查等规定。这一举措被视为特朗普政府与AI行业密切关系的延续，旨在阻止各州自行制定AI监管措施。法案将在5月13日由众议院审议。

News
Republicans Try to Cram Ban on AI Regulation Into Budget Reconciliation Bill
Emanuel Maiberg
·
May 12, 2025
at 10:09 AM
Republicans try to use the Budget Reconciliation bill to stop states from regulating AI entirely for 10 years.
Photo by
Darren Halstead
/
Unsplash
Late last night, House Republicans introduced new language to the Budget Reconciliation bill that will immiserate the lives of millions of Americans by cutting their access to Medicaid, and making life much more difficult for millions more by making them pay higher fees when they seek medical care. While a lot of attention will be justifiably given to these cuts, the bill has also crammed in new language that attempts to entirely stop states from enacting any regulation against artificial intelligence.
“...no State or political subdivision thereof may enforce any law or regulation regulating artificial intelligence models, artificial intelligence systems, or automated decision systems during the 10 year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act,”
says the text of the bill
introduced Sunday night by Congressman Brett Guthrie of Kentucky, Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. The text of the bill will be considered by the House at the budget reconciliation markup on May 13.
That language of the bill, how it goes on to define AI and other “automated systems,” and what it considers “regulation,” is broad enough to cover relatively new generative AI tools and technology that has existed for much longer. In theory, that language will make it impossible to enforce many existing and proposed state laws that aim to protect people from and inform them about AI systems.
For example, last year California passed a
law
that requires health care providers to disclose when they have used generative AI to communicate clinical information to patients. In 2021, New York passed the first
law
in the United States requiring employers to conduct bias audits of AI tools used for employment decisions. California also passed a
law
that will go into effect in 2026 which requires developers of generative AI models to share detailed documentation on its websites about the data it used to develop these models, an extremely consequential law as AI companies are currently hiding their exploitation of copyrighted materials in order to create these models, as we have
shown
repeatedly
.
In theory none of these states will be able to enforce these laws if Republicans manage to pass the Budget Reconciliation bill with this current language.
The AI industry has been sucking up to Trump since before he got into office, and his administration is intertwined with AI executives, be it Elon Musk at DOGE, David Sacks as an AI czar, or Marc Andreessen as an advisor. Trump has returned the favor by undoing Biden era executive orders aimed at mitigating AI risk. Preventing states from charting their own paths on this issue and trying to protect people from these systems will be one of the most radical positions Republicans have taken on this issue yet.

data.title: Shingles vaccine reduces risk of heart disease by 23%, study of one million
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: 美国疾病控制与预防中心推荐50岁以上或免疫系统较弱的人群接种两剂Shingrix疫苗，以预防带状疱疹。近期一项韩国研究发现，接种带状疱疹疫苗还可能降低心血管疾病和中风的风险。研究分析了127万余名50岁以上人群的健康数据，结果显示接种者的心血管疾病风险降低了23%，尤其在男性、60岁以下人群以及生活习惯不健康的人群中效果更明显。虽然需要更多研究确认因果关系，但该研究表明疫苗不仅能预防感染，还有助于长期维持健康。目前，Shingrix疫苗已取代早期的活病毒疫苗，成为更有效的选择。

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends two doses of the Shingrix vaccine for adults who are immunocompromised or over age 50.
Getty Images
Get inspired by a weekly roundup on living well, made simple.
Sign up for CNN’s Life, But Better newsletter for information and tools designed to improve your well-being
.
CNN
—
Getting the shingles vaccine could do more than just prevent a painful red rash — it may also lower the risk of heart disease and stroke, according to a new South Korean study of more than one million people published in the
European Heart Journal.
The
highly common
herpes strain, also called varicella-zoster virus (VZV), can cause chickenpox in childhood and later develop into shingles in older or immuno-compromised adults. The shingles vaccine is already considered a top-line defense against the virus, but
recent studies
have pointed to other unexpected health benefits.
An analysis of health outcomes for 1,271,922 people age 50 and older found a 23% lower risk of cardiovascular disease among those who were vaccinated for shingles. The reduced risk was most noticeable up to eight years after vaccination among males, people under 60, and even those with “unhealthy lifestyles,” such as chronic smoking or drinking, according to the May 6 study.
Hot dog with fresh organic bread bun white wheat and black charcoal sausage ketchup mustard
Chan2545/iStockphoto/Getty Images
Related article
Parkinson’s disease prevention may ‘begin at the dinner table’
“Since shingles can cause inflammation in blood vessels and lead to blood clots, which in turn raise the risk of heart disease, preventing shingles through vaccination might also help reduce these cardiovascular risks,” explained Hayeon Lee, a coauthor and researcher from the Kyung Hee University College of Medicine in an email. It’s also possible that the nerve damage caused by shingles could disturb the heart’s rhythm, leading to irregular palpitations and even cardiac arrest, per the study.
The vaccine may be better at preventing shingles in younger patients and males because of their more robust immune systems, Lee said.
“If a vaccine helps lower the risk of both infection and serious chronic conditions, it becomes an even more valuable public health tool,” Lee said. “This study supports a broader understanding of vaccination — not just as a shield against infectious diseases, but as part of a more comprehensive approach to maintaining long-term health.”
More research is needed to determine a direct causal link between vaccination and reduced cardiovascular event risk, but this analysis is the largest and most comprehensive so far, presenting a compelling case for those on the fence about vaccination, said Dr. Sharon Curhan, a physician and epidemiologist at Brigham and Women’s Hospital, who was not involved in the study.
Since this herpes strain can lie dormant in the body for years after exposure before it reactivates into shingles, you don’t need a history of chickenpox to get the vaccine, Curhan said.
In fact, more than 99% of adults age 50 years and older worldwide have been exposed to VZV, and many may not have had, or known they had chickenpox at all, according to estimates from the
US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
.
The limitations
Patients from the study used an older variation of the shingles vaccine that is being phased out of most countries.
The live zoster vaccine, no longer available in the US
as of 2020
, contains a living but weakened form of the virus used to generate an immune response. It’s since been swapped for Shingrix, a two-shot recombinant zoster vaccine containing only part of the virus — which has shown to be more effective.
More research is needed to compare the various health benefits of these different vaccine variations, said Dr. Pascal Geldsetzer, an assistant professor of medicine at Stanford University who was not involved in the study.

data.title: Plain Vanilla Web
data.author: andrewrn
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一种不依赖构建工具或框架，仅使用编辑器、浏览器和网页标准来制作网站和网页应用的技术。主要涵盖以下主题：

1. **组件**：使用Web Components作为基础构建块，替代React或Vue等框架的组件方法。
2. **样式**：充分利用现代CSS的功能，替代CSS Modules、PostCSS或SASS。
3. **网站**：基于Web Components构建网页项目，无需使用构建工具、框架或服务器端逻辑即可部署生产。
4. **应用**：使用原生技术构建单页应用，处理路由和状态管理。

该教程面向已有HTML、CSS和JavaScript基础的开发者。文章还讨论了现代框架的优缺点，指出纯原生开发方式虽然牺牲了一些短期便利，但换来了长期的简化和几乎零维护的优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否需要使用框架以及替代方案的讨论，特别是在Web开发中的应用。

不同观点：
• bob1029认为，很多B2B SaaS场景下，可能根本不需要网站或复杂的Web应用，通过电子邮件和Excel文件等方式可能更有效。
• donohoe表示，虽然不反对框架，但其团队在没有使用框架的情况下也取得了成功，用户反馈积极，并认为纯JavaScript目前对他们很有效。
• pelagicAustral支持简化开发，主张构建一个整体的、舒适的系统，不必过于关注反应性和页面刷新问题。
• coolhand2120对框架持批评态度，认为复杂性导致了更多的问题，怀念早期简单开发的时代，但承认框架有其存在的理由。
• red_admiral指出，自定义组件开发最终可能还是会构建出一个微型框架，并认为框架在处理共享状态和异步更新时是必要的。
• dmje强调了区分Web应用和Web网站的重要性，认为它们是不同的，需要不同的技术方法。
• 90s_dev对Web组件持怀疑态度，认为现代JS动态更新方式仍然有其优势，并主张在框架外进行创新。
• NoSalt强烈反对使用框架，认为框架带来了不必要的复杂性和膨胀，倾向于使用库而不是框架。
• chrisweekly认为理解Web基础技术是必要的，并推荐使用符合Web标准的工具和技术，同时保持对取舍的 awareness。
• FjordWarden不认为Web组件能替代React或Vue等框架，指出Web组件在复杂值和反应性方面的不足。
• mmcnl同意FjordWarden的观点，认为Web组件没有解决状态管理问题，框架在这方面更有优势。
• hanlonsrazor认为框架有助于标准化和最佳实践的实施，使得开发更高效，特别对于组织来说更具成本效益。
• montag对Web组件的发展现状表示失望，指出其社区和资源的支持不足。
• neiman分享了一个不用框架的小项目经验，虽然成功实现，但过程中仍感到不确定是否应使用框架。
• braden-lk对Web组件的进步表示赞赏，但认为在状态管理和交互性方面，纯JavaScript仍然较为繁琐。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于是否需要框架来实现Web开发，特别是针对B2B应用和一般网站。
- 支持框架的观点认为其能提高效率、标准化和最佳实践；反对框架的观点则强调复杂性和不必要的膨胀。
- 对Web组件的可行性存在争议，部分开发者认为其无法替代现有框架的功能。
- 实践中，有开发者成功使用了无框架方案，并认为这是一种更简单有效的选择。

About this site
This is an overview of the major techniques used to make web sites and web applications
without making use of build tools or frameworks, with just an editor, a browser, and web standards.
Specifically, that means these topics:
Components
The use of Web Components as the basic building block for making higher-level primitives out of plain HTML, JavaScript and CSS, replacing the components approach from frameworks like React or Vue.
Styling
Fully leveraging the abilities of modern CSS to replace the conveniences of CSS Modules, PostCSS, or SASS.
Sites
Making a web project based on web components and deploying it for production without involving build tools, frameworks or server-side logic.
Applications
How to build single-page web applications with vanilla techniques, how to do routing, and how to manage state.
This tutorial is meant for those who already know their way around HTML, CSS and JavaScript. If you're just starting out learning web development and are looking for resources to get going, then this is not the site for you yet.
You can get started at
The Odin Project Foundations Course
or the
MDN Learn web development
learning path.
Wait, but why
Modern web development frameworks are powerful in their ability to develop rich well-structured web applications quickly,
and for this reason alone they are well worth your time to learn.
However, this rich functionality comes at the cost of framework and tooling complexity,
and the resulting projects often require regular maintenance to keep secure and up to date.
The plain vanilla style of web development makes a different choice,
trading off a few short term comforts for long term benefits like simplicity and being effectively zero-maintenance.
This approach is made possible by today's browser landscape, which offers excellent web standards support.
Up next
Learn about using
Web Components
as the way to compose content, style and behavior.
43954896.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一种不依赖构建工具或框架，仅使用编辑器、浏览器和网页标准来制作网站和网页应用的技术。主要涵盖以下主题：

1. **组件**：使用Web Components作为基础构建块，替代React或Vue等框架的组件方法。
2. **样式**：充分利用现代CSS的功能，替代CSS Modules、PostCSS或SASS。
3. **网站**：基于Web Components构建网页项目，无需使用构建工具、框架或服务器端逻辑即可部署生产。
4. **应用**：使用原生技术构建单页应用，处理路由和状态管理。

该教程面向已有HTML、CSS和JavaScript基础的开发者。文章还讨论了现代框架的优缺点，指出纯原生开发方式虽然牺牲了一些短期便利，但换来了长期的简化和几乎零维护的优势。

data.title: VPN firm says it didn't know customers had lifetime subscriptions, cancels them
data.author: ajdude
data.article_summary: VPNSecure的新所有者取消了终身订阅服务，引发用户不满。新 owners 声称在收购VPNSecure时并不知情这些终身订阅，并在2023年收购后发现问题。由于这些终身订阅用户不产生持续收入，导致公司资源紧张，他们决定取消这些账户。受影响用户可获得折扣订阅，但需在5月31日前购买。用户对这一突然变化表示愤怒，并在Trustpilot上留下大量差评。VPNSecure对此道歉，并解释未起诉前所有者是因为诉讼成本高于收购价格。公司强调不会再次提供终身订阅服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：消费者对“终身订阅”等优惠的信任问题及相关商业模式的可行性

不同观点：
• YaBa 表示自己是受影响客户之一，曾获得两年免费订阅，但因此对公司失去信任，尤其对“终身订阅”持怀疑态度。他还提到类似的 web hosting 服务，曾以低价吸引客户，但最终因成本问题取消服务，暗示这种低价策略不可持续。

• jqpabc123 持相似观点，认为许多看似优惠的服务（如终身订阅、无限数据计划、永久软件许可证等）往往存在隐性问题或无法兑现承诺。他强调如果某个优惠听起来过于美好，那很可能就是不真实的。

• b3ing 则从另一个角度讨论，提到实体收据会随着时间褪色，即使有终身保修也难以证明。虽然现在有了数字收据，但如果是在实体店购买的商品，收据可能会因质量问题而难以保存，并暗示这可能是商家故意为之。

• Havoc 强烈质疑“终身订阅”的可靠性，将这种订阅与诈骗行为相提并论，特别是提到曾被类似的“终身VPN”服务欺骗，最终变成每月收费1美元，表达了对这类服务的不信任。

补充讨论：
• gnabgib 提供了一个外部讨论链接，暗示有关类似话题的讨论已在其他平台上进行，提供了进一步阅读的参考。

争议焦点：
• 消费者普遍认为“终身订阅”等优惠实际上并不可靠，企业可能通过这些优惠吸引客户但最终无法兑现承诺，导致消费者对这种商业模式失去信任。
• 另一个争议点是商家是否故意通过褪色收据或不清晰的条款来逃避保修责任。

The new owners of VPN provider VPNSecure have drawn ire after canceling lifetime subscriptions. The owners told customers that they didn’t know about the lifetime subscriptions when they bought VPNSecure, and they cannot honor the purchases.
In March, complaints started appearing online about lifetime subscriptions to VPNSecure no longer working.
The first public response Ars Technica found came on April 28, when lifetime subscription holders reported receiving an email from the VPN provider saying:
To continue providing a secure and high-quality experience for all users, Lifetime Deal accounts have now been deactivated as of April 28th, 2025.
A copy of the email from “The VPN Secure Team” and
posted on Reddit
notes that VPNSecure had previously deactivated accounts with lifetime subscriptions that it said hadn’t been used in “over 6 months.” The message noted that VPNSecure was acquired in 2023, “including the technology, domain, and customer database—but not the liabilities.” The email continues:
Unfortunately, the previous owner did not disclose that thousands of Lifetime Deals (LTDs) had been sold through platforms like StackSocial.
We discovered this only months later—when a large portion of our resources were strained by these LTD accounts and high support volume from users, who through part of the database, provided no sustaining income to help us improve and maintain the service.
VPNSecure is offering affected users discounted new subscriptions for either $1.87 for a month (instead of $9.95), $19 for a year (instead of $79.92), or $55 for three years (instead of $107.64).
The deals
are available until May 31, per the email.
This week, users reported receiving a follow-up email from VPNSecure providing more details about why it made its bold and sudden move. Screenshots of the email
shared on Reddit
say that the acquisition by InfiniteQuant Ltd (which is a different company than
InfiniteQuant Capital Ltd
, an InfiniteQuant Capital rep told Ars via email) was “an asset only deal.”
A VPNSecure representative claimed on the reviews site
Trustpilot
that the current owners “did not gain access to the customer database until months” after the acquisition. According to VPNSecure’s owners, their acquisition netted them “the tech, the brand, and the infrastructure/technology—but none of the company, contracts, payments, or obligations from the previous owners.”
The current owners said they didn’t sue the seller because “a corporate lawsuit would’ve cost more than the entire purchase of the business.”
VPNSecure also apologized to any customers who felt caught offguard by the changes, noted their backlash, and thanked those who purchased new subscriptions.
The email’s authors claimed that they could have chosen to shut down VPNSecure after learning about the lifetime subscriptions but “chose the hard path.” They also emphasized they “never will” sell lifetime subscriptions.
Unaware of lifetime subscriptions
Customers have been incredulous about VPNSecure's owners not knowing about the purchased lifetime subscriptions before buying the company. The firm's email to customers this week said the current owners reviewed six to 12 months of VPNSecure’s prior “financials” before making the purchase, but the listing, profit and loss statements, and communications never mentioned lifetime deals.
The email included a link to a
VPNSecure sales listing
dated April 2023 that shows an “estimated valuation” of $282,090–$344,770 and doesn’t mention lifetime subscriptions.
Ars looked at the VPNSecure website’s history using the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine and didn’t find mention of lifetime subscriptions. Lifetime subscriptions to the service were apparently only offered through third parties, like these listings on
StackSocial
and
Wccftech
, that no longer link to purchaseable subscriptions. VPNSecure’s email this week claimed that lifetime subscriptions were sold “between 2015 and 2017”; however, Ars found ads on ZDNET pushing $40 lifetime subscriptions
in 2021
and $28 lifetime subscriptions
in 2022
.
A screenshot from a 2021 ZDNET listing.

A screenshot from a 2022 ZDNET listing.
A screenshot from a 2021 ZDNET listing.
ZDNET
A screenshot from a 2022 ZDNET listing.
Customer backlash
Since March, there have been 20 pages' worth of one-star reviews on Trustpilot complaining about lifetime subscribers losing access to their VPN. One Trustpilot user wrote on April 30:
When the service stopped working, I logged a ticket. A couple days later, I got that infamous email informing me my subscription had (already) been cancelled. The comms should have been sent earlier (before the service was interrupted), and written with more clarity and empathy.
VPNSecure is responding to the complaints on Trustpil

data.title: Reviving a modular cargo bike design from the 1930s
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 法国移动公司Cyclauto从1930年代的设计中汲取灵感，推出了一款高效灵活的模块化货运自行车。该设计由法国实业家Auguste Reymond原创，骑行者位于前轮正上方，直接驱动前轮，无需链条，减少了维护需求。内置的三速齿轮箱使起步更容易。Cyclauto的货舱部分可拆卸，能够连接各种类型的拖车，实现模块化使用，可根据需求运载货物、人员或商业设备（如食品车）。其两段式车架设计还便于拆卸运输。此外，该设计提供了更短的轴距，使自行车在城市环境中更易 maneuver。尽管在自行车展上亮相，但该公司尚未公布生产日期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型三轮货运自行车的设计与实用性

不同观点：
• ben7799：认为这种三轮车并非为竞技设计，因此对于速度和爬坡能力的担忧不成立。设计上尽量使用标准自行车组件以降低成本，并提到与Cruzbike类似的前轮驱动设计，解决了斜躺自行车常见的传动系统问题。
• btbuildem：指出三轮车在转弯时不稳定，尤其是在无负载时，且由于无法倾斜，转弯时会产生较大的扭力。对比了新旧设计，指出新设计在转弯时可能会让骑行者被甩出。
• nabilhat：对三轮车设计持较为积极的态度，分享了个人骑行体验，认为稳定性问题被夸大。强调实际骑行体验比网上讨论更有说服力。
• willemlaurentz：指出在城市中低速行驶的好处，比如可以时刻关注货物安全，特别在载有小孩时更为重要。
• asix66：分享了哥本哈根使用此类三轮车进行货物运输和年度 cargo-bike 比赛的例子，说明这种设计在实际生活中有应用场景。
• jabl：提到了一种四轮 cargo 自行车 "Velove Armadillo"，并认为这种设计在城市货物运输中更为实用。
• bgnn：认为电动版会更实用，并提供了荷兰邮政服务使用类似车辆的例子。
• CelestialMystic：质疑前置三档花鼓的设计，认为传统的变速器和链条系统更便宜且易于维护。
• analog31：指出三轮车前双轮设计在转弯时更稳定，并提到三轮全地形车下架的原因。
• gcanyon：对无拖车情况下骑行感到好奇，认为像带齿轮的单轮车。
• fitsumbelay：提到华盛顿特区有长期使用此类型车辆的快递员，并进行了改装以搭载儿童。
• dpedu：担心骑行时转向会感觉怪异，因为需要像开车一样转向，而不是像传统自行车那样反向操控。
• Brajeshwar：将此设计比作加强版的人力黄包车。
• hombre_fatal：对前部设计感到新奇，认为像汽车一样的转向系统赋予了更多创意可能性。
• HumblyTossed：提到一个关于 cargo 自行车的评测视频，提供了进一步的参考。

补充讨论：
• 设计与实用性的争议：主要集中在三轮车的稳定性、转向方式和维护成本上。
• 实际应用场景：一些评论分享了实际使用案例和文化背景，比如哥本哈根的 cargo-bike 比赛和荷兰邮政服务使用类似车辆。
• 创新与传统的对比：讨论了新型设计与传统自行车设计之间的优缺点。

争议焦点：三轮车设计的稳定性和实用性，特别是在转弯和高速情况下的表现。

43963397.article_content:
Reviving a Modular Cargo Bike Design from the 1930s
The Cyclauto is efficient and flexible
By
Rain Noe
-
May 12
in
Bikes
Your average cargo bike typically has a long frame divided into two areas: One for the cargo, and one for the rider. The rider is positioned just forward of the rear wheel, with a chain delivering power from the pedals to that rear wheel.
French mobility company
Cyclauto
has gone through the history books to revive an alternate design from the 1930s.
This design, originally by French industrialist Auguste Reymond, places the rider directly above the front wheel. They pedal this wheel directly; there's no chain, reducing maintenance needs. A three-speed gearbox in the hub makes starting easier.
The cargo-carrying part, in Cyclauto's modern rendition, is detachable, recalling a semi-trailer. This means a wide variety of trailer styles can be fitted to the drive unit, creating a modular system that can handle a wide variety of user needs. The Cyclauto can be configured to move cargo, people or even commercial fixtures (think food cart).
An additional benefit to the two-piece frame is that the bike can be broken down for transport, allowing the user "to load it into a trunk for easy transport from point A to point B."
Lastly, the company says the shorter wheelbase of their arrangement provides a tighter turning radius, making the bike easier to maneuver in urban environments.
The Cyclauto has been making the rounds at bike shows, but the company has yet to reveal production dates.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了宾汉姆顿大学副教授Guy German及其团队研究人在水中浸泡过久后手指皱纹的形成原因和模式。传统观点认为皱纹是皮肤吸水膨胀所致，但German的研究发现，实际上是皮下血管收缩导致皱纹形成。在一项发表于《Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials》的论文中，German和Rachel Laytin进一步证实，多次浸泡后，皱纹的形态模式是固定的，因为血管位置相对稳定。研究还发现，患有正中神经损伤的人不会出现这种皱纹，这为法医学和指纹识别提供了新思路。German表示，这项研究不仅解答了一个孩子的有趣提问，还可能在实际应用中发挥重要作用。

43979063.article_content:
Do your fingers wrinkle the same way every time you’re in the water too long? Research says yes
Question from a child inspires biomedical engineering paper
Because finger wrinkles after prolonged immersion are caused by blood vessels beneath the skin contracting, the patterns of wrinkles stay constant. Image Credit: Guy German.
By Chris Kocher
May 07, 2025
share via twitter
share via linkedin
share via email
Sometimes it takes a kid to ask a question no one has considered before.
Guy German is an associate professor and director of the Watson School's  Biomedical Engineering Department. He couldn't decide between astrophysics and genetics when he was applying to college, so he flipped a coin! Image Credit: Jonathan Cohen.
Guy German is an associate professor and director of the Watson School's  Biomedical Engineering Department. He couldn't decide between astrophysics and genetics when he was applying to college, so he flipped a coin! Image Credit: Jonathan Cohen.
×
A couple of years ago, Binghamton University Associate Professor
Guy German
published research about why human skin wrinkles when you stay in the water too long. Received wisdom held that the water swelled your skin and made your fingers wrinkly, but little to no research had been done to prove that.
What German and his team at the Biological Soft Matter Mechanics Laboratory found is that blood vessels beneath the skin actually contract after prolonged immersion, and that’s where the wrinkles come from.
He wrote about the research for The Conversation
— a nonprofit news organization that asks academics to share their expertise on current topics — as part of its Curious Kids feature. One of the follow-up questions stumped him, though.
“A student asked, ‘Yeah, but do the wrinkles always form in the same way?’ And I thought: I haven’t the foggiest clue!” said German, a faculty member at the
Thomas J. Watson College of Engineering and Applied Science
’s
Department of Biomedical Engineering
. “So it led to this research to find out.”
In
a paper recently published in the
Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials
, German and Rachel Laytin ’23, MS ’24, show that, yes, the topography patterns remain constant after multiple immersions.
“Blood vessels don’t change their position much — they move around a bit, but in relation to other blood vessels, they’re pretty static,” German said. “That means the wrinkles should form in the same manner, and we proved that they do.”
The research put subjects’ fingers in water for 30 minutes, taking photos and then repeating the immersion under the same conditions at least 24 hours later. By comparing the images, German and Laytin found the same patterns of raised loops and ridges after both immersions.
They also made an interesting side discovery: “We’ve heard that wrinkles don’t form in people who have median nerve damage in their fingers,” German said. “One of my students told us, ‘I’ve got median nerve damage in my fingers.’ So we tested him — no wrinkles!”
As much fun as it was to figure out something a child asked, the research also could have real-world applications in forensics, such as fingerprinting at crime scenes and identifying bodies found after prolonged water exposure. German’s father, a retired U.K. police officer, faced some of these challenges during his law enforcement career.
“Biometrics and fingerprints are built into my brain,” he said. “I always think about this sort of stuff, because it’s fascinating.”
German is eager to further explore questions about skin immersion with his students: “I feel like a kid in a candy store, because there’s so much science here that I don’t know. We thank the people at The Conversation and the wonderful question they asked us, because it does create cool new science.”

本文介绍了与古代研究相关的几个重要工具和方法：

1. **Epigrafía**（碑文学）：研究铭文的学科，帮助了解古代文字、语言和历史。
2. **Numismática**（钱币学）：通过分析古钱币，获取有关经济、政治和文化的见解。
3. **Onomástica**（专名学）：研究人名和地名，以揭示社会结构和历史背景。
4. **Mapas**（地图）：用于理解古代地理和领土变迁。
5. **Mapas Hesperia**：专门展示古希腊和古罗马世界的地图，提供历史地理参考。
6. **Instrucciones**（说明）：提供如何使用上述工具和方法的指南，以促进历史研究。

这些工具和方法共同帮助学者深入研究古代文明。

data.title: When graphic design saves lives
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了过去公共卫生宣传通过海报传递信息的方式，特别是哈佛图书馆数字化收集的3000多张关于HIV/AIDS的宣传海报。这些海报展示了不同国家在1990至2004年间的公共卫生宣传策略，强调了视觉和文字结合对信息传达的重要性。海报设计需简洁，传递单一信息和情感，并引导进一步行动，如通过二维码获取更多信息。随着时间推移，宣传活动针对不同受众变得更加多样化，并且从羞辱或警告信息转向积极肯定的信息。此外，文章提到现代预防和治疗手段（如PrEP和U=U策略）使得HIV的传播可被有效遏制，海报内容虽已过时，但提供了对未来宣传的重要启示。

43948244.article_content:
Today, much of the visual communication around public health is digital — in Instagram infographics, TikToks, or YouTube videos. But in decades past, posters, printed out and pasted up in public, were a key way to spread messaging.
“People remember information better if it’s presented both visually and with printed messages,” said
Amanda Yarnell
, chair of the
Chan Center for Health Communication
, which helps online creators spread evidence-based health messages in ways that resonate. “Seeing something and reading something at the same time improves understanding.”
Harvard Library has digitized more than 3,000 posters related to a single major public health crisis: the HIV/AIDS epidemic. The posters come from numerous countries around the world and span roughly 1990 to 2004. The
collection
tells a story, said Yarnell, of what the public health establishment has learned about what messages work, and why.
Message, feeling, action
In the small area of a poster — and the limited time in which you might hope to catch someone’s attention — designers need to craft a single simple message. Too many words and you lose people.
“A good poster is one point and a feeling: something that the messenger wants you to remember, and then the feeling helps you remember it,” said Yarnell, who is also a lecturer on social and behavioral sciences at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. “And best-case scenario, there’s a route to more. It used to be a phone number, and then it became a website, and now it’s probably a QR code.”

data.title: Type-constrained code generation with language models
data.author: tough
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提出了一种类型约束的代码生成方法，利用类型系统来指导大型语言模型（LLM）生成更准确的代码。传统方法常产生无法编译的代码，尤其是存在类型错误。为此，作者引入了一种基于前缀自动机和可居住类型搜索的解码方法，以确保生成代码的类型正确性。该方法在基础简单类型语言上形式化，并扩展至TypeScript以展示其实用性。实验结果表明，该方法显著减少了编译错误，并提高了在代码合成、翻译和修复任务中的功能正确性，适用于不同规模和类型的LLM模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程语言中的应用及优化，特别是TypeScript和其他编程语言的处理方式

不同观点：
• [energy123] 认为可以专注于让LLM在一种编程语言（尤其是小型语言或特定领域语言）上表现最佳，而不是追求构建通用的前沿模型。这种策略可以通过将所有资源集中在特定语言的RL（强化学习）管道上来实现。
• [_jayhack_] 提到MultiLSPy工具，它是一个Python包装器，围绕多个语言服务器协议（LSP）。他还引用了相关研究，这些研究使用静态分析超越类型系统，以过滤无效的变量名和控制流等。
• [kreetx] 建议将此方法扩展到Haskell，利用Curry-Howard同构，通过类型签名定义所需程序，让LLM找到实现方法。
• [ArcaneMoose] 认为TypeScript是LLM的最佳语言，因为它有大量训练数据和结构化的类型系统，这些都有助于LLM的理解和执行。
• [bmc7505] 主张使用有限模型理论来实现这一目标，但认为目前尚未达到这一阶段。
• [slt2021] 提出是否有可能训练基于抽象语法树（AST）而不是基于标记的LLM，并询问是否有相关研究。
• [koakuma-chan] 认为如果库文档易于复制粘贴到LLM中，将极大受益于这种代码社会。
• [informal007] 建议将反馈循环移到LLM训练的RL阶段，并询问是否有相关研究。
• [weiwenhao] 质疑LLM目前是否真正理解代码。

补充讨论：
• [muglug] 指出这种研究来自大学而非大型AI实验室，推测这些实验室可能仍相信更大的模型是未来的方向。

Title:
Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models
Authors:
Niels Mündler
,
Jingxuan He
,
Hao Wang
,
Koushik Sen
,
Dawn Song
,
Martin Vechev
View a PDF of the paper titled Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models, by Niels M\"undler and Jingxuan He and Hao Wang and Koushik Sen and Dawn Song and Martin Vechev
View PDF
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) have achieved notable success in code generation. However, they still frequently produce uncompilable output because their next-token inference procedure does not model formal aspects of code. Although constrained decoding is a promising approach to alleviate this issue, it has only been applied to handle either domain-specific languages or syntactic features of general-purpose programming languages. However, LLMs frequently generate code with typing errors, which are beyond the domain of syntax and generally hard to adequately constrain. To address this challenge, we introduce a type-constrained decoding approach that leverages type systems to guide code generation. For this purpose, we develop novel prefix automata and a search over inhabitable types, forming a sound approach to enforce well-typedness on LLM-generated code. We formalize our approach on a foundational simply-typed language and extend it to TypeScript to demonstrate practicality. Our evaluation on the HumanEval and MBPP datasets shows that our approach reduces compilation errors by more than half and significantly increases functional correctness in code synthesis, translation, and repair tasks across LLMs of various sizes and model families, including state-of-the-art open-weight models with more than 30B parameters. The results demonstrate the generality and effectiveness of our approach in constraining LLM code generation with formal rules of type systems.

data.title: Flattening Rust’s learning curve
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary:
本文提供了学习Rust语言的建议，旨在帮助学习者减轻挫败感并加快掌握速度。核心建议包括：

1. **接受新思维模式**：Rust需要学习所有权、生命周期和trait系统等新概念，学习效果与态度关系更大，而非仅依赖编程经验。
   
2. **借助编译器学习**：将借用检查器视为合作者，利用编译器的提示来理解问题。编译器无法推断时，反思代码设计。

3. **逐步学习**：初期不要急于求成，可以多用`String`、`clone()`和`unwrap()`，稍后重构。避免一开始就接触异步或复杂组合子。

4. **从小步骤开始**：每次学习一个新概念，写简单代码片段，逐渐增加复杂性。习惯于重写和试验代码。

5. **精确与习惯**：从一开始就启用Clippy进行代码检查，养成良好编码习惯。

通过这些策略，学习者可以更顺利地掌握Rust，减少学习曲线中的困难。

不同观点：
• **Animats** 认为Rust的所有权模型可以通过几个核心原则简化理解，如每个数据对象有且只有一个所有者、所有权可以转移、引用不能超过对象的生命周期等。他批评了许多解释过于冗长。

• **mprovost** 建议初学者先学习Rust的一个子集，比如可以暂时不学习生命周期，同时反对过度依赖`clone()`，主张一开始就学习借用机制。
• **writebetterc** 认为Rust的所有权和生命周期概念不仅适用于Rust，也适用于现代程序设计，如C++。

• **jillesvangurp** 认为Rust对新手来说非常困难，因为它的语法复杂且高度简练，很多特性需要深厚的理论基础才能理解，这使得它不适合大多数没有计算机科学硕士学位的程序员。
• **cadamsdotcom** 强调Rust的借用检查器虽然让人感到挫折，但也帮助他学会了如何编写线程安全的代码，他认为每个人都应该学习Rust。
• **baalimago** 对Rust中一些不直观的设计选择表示不满，比如为什么需要在一个已经是字符串的对象上调用`to_string()`。
• **scotty79** 认为理解Rust的值语义是关键，变量是固定大小的物理内存，值可以被移入或移出，Rust的很多设计元素都是这一概念的直接结果。
• **ants_everywhere** 指出学习曲线平坦意味着学不到新东西，Rust的学习曲线虽然陡峭，但这是学习新知识的必然过程。
• **TheChaplain** 认为Rust的语法丑陋，像Perl和C++模板元编程的孩子，无法忍受。
• **jamil7** 认为Rust的学习曲线被夸大了，不需要掌握所有细节就能开始使用并获得生产力。
• **sesm** 希望有一份简洁的文档，解释Rust设计决策背后的主要原因，特别是对C++背景的程序员。
• **Havoc** 认为Rust在入门阶段是可控的，但异步编程可能带来更高层次的困难。

补充讨论：
• Rust的所有权和借用机制是讨论的核心，一些人认为这些机制是Rust独特且强大的特性，而另一些人则认为这些概念难以理解且增加了学习的难度。
• Rust的语法美丑存在争议，一些人认为其高度简练的语法和复杂性是其强大之处，而另一些人则觉得语法丑陋且难以接受。
• 初学者是否应该先学习Rust的一个子集，以及是否需要深入理解所有概念才能有效使用Rust，也存在不同看法。一些人建议先掌握基本概念，而另一些人则认为可以先使用简单的特性。
• Rust的异步编程被认为是更高层次的挑战，特别是在入门之后。

争议焦点：
• Rust的语法复杂性和所有权模型的学习难度是主要的争议点，一些人认为这些特性使得Rust难以学习，而另一些人则认为这些特性是Rust的优势，并且可以通过学习掌握。

Published: 2025-05-05
I see people make the same mistakes over and over again when learning Rust.
Here are my thoughts (ordered by importance) on how you can ease the learning process.
My goal is to help you save time and frustration.
Let Your Guard Down
Stop resisting. That’s the most important lesson.
Accept that learning Rust requires adopting a completely different mental model than what you’re used to.
There are a ton of new concepts to learn like lifetimes, ownership, and the trait system.
And depending on your background, you’ll need to add generics, pattern matching, or macros to the list.
Your learning pace doesn’t have much to do with whether you’re smart or not or if you have a lot of programming experience.
Instead, what matters more is
your attitude toward the language
.
I have seen junior devs excel at Rust with no prior training and senior engineers struggle for weeks/months or even give up entirely. Leave your hubris at home.
Treat the borrow checker as a co-author, not an adversary. This reframes the relationship.
Let the compiler do the teaching: for example, this works great with lifetimes, because the compiler will tell you when a lifetime is ambiguous.
Then just add it but take the time to reason about
why
the compiler couldn’t figure it out itself.

longest
(
x
:
&
str
,
y
:
&
str
)
->
&
str
{
if
x
.
len
(
)
>
y
.
len
(
)
{
x
}
else
{
y
}
}
If you try to compile this, the compiler will ask you to add a lifetime parameter.
It provides this helpful suggestion:
1
|
fn
longest
<
'a
>
(
x
:
&
'a
str
,
y
:
&
'a
str
)
->
&
'a
str
{
|
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
So you don’t have to guess what the compiler wants and can follow its instructions.
But also sit down and wonder
why
the compiler couldn’t figure it out itself.
Most of the time when fighting the compiler it is actually exposing a design flaw.
Similarly, if your code gets overly verbose or looks ugly, there’s probably a better way.
Declare defeat and learn to do it the Rust way.
If you come from a dynamic language like Python, you’ll find that Rust is more verbose in general.
Most of it just comes from type annotations, though.
Some people might dismiss Rust as being “unelegant” or “ugly”, but the verbosity actually serves a good purpose and is immensely helpful for building large-scale applications:
First off, you will read the code more often than you write it,
which means type annotations will give you more local context to reason with.
Second, it helps immensely with refactoring because the compiler can check if you broke any code while you move things around.
If your code turns out to look very ugly, take a step back and ask if there’s a simpler solution.
Don’t dismiss the language right away.
Turn on all
clippy lints
on day one – even the pedantic ones.
Run the linter and follow the suggestions religiously.
Don’t skip that step once your program compiles.
Resistance is futile.
The longer you refuse to learn, the longer you will suffer;
but the moment you let your guard down is the moment you’ll start to learn.
Forget what you think you knew about programming and really start to listen to what the compiler, the standard library, and clippy are trying to tell you.
Baby Steps
I certainly tried to run before I could walk.
That alone cost me a lot of precious time.
Don’t make it too hard on yourself in the beginning.
Here are some tips:
Use
String
and
clone()
and
unwrap
generously; you can always refactor later – and refactoring is the best part about Rust!
I wrote an article on saving yourself time during that phase
here
.
Use simple if or match statements before starting to learn some of the more idiomatic
.and_then
etc. combinators
Avoid async Rust in week 1. The additional rules are a tax on people still learning the core ownership model.
Don’t introduce too many new concepts at the same time!
Instead, while you learn about a new concept, have an editor open and write out a few examples.
What helped was to just write some code in the
Rust playground
and try to get it to compile. Write super small snippets (e.g., one
main.rs
for one concept) instead of using one big “tutorial” repo.
Get into the habit of throwing most of your code away.
I still do that and test out ideas in the playground or when I brainstorm with clients.
For instance, here’s one of my favorite code snippets to explain the concept of ownership:

Can you explain it?
Ask yourself what would change if

If Rust code looks scary to you,
break it down

Write your own, simpler version, then slowly increase the complexity.
Rust is easier to write than to read.
By writing lots of Rust, you will also learn how to read it better as well.

43978435.article_summary:
本文提供了学习Rust语言的建议，旨在帮助学习者减轻挫败感并加快掌握速度。核心建议包括：

1. **接受新思维模式**：Rust需要学习所有权、生命周期和trait系统等新概念，学习效果与态度关系更大，而非仅依赖编程经验。
   
2. **借助编译器学习**：将借用检查器视为合作者，利用编译器的提示来理解问题。编译器无法推断时，反思代码设计。

3. **逐步学习**：初期不要急于求成，可以多用`String`、`clone()`和`unwrap()`，稍后重构。避免一开始就接触异步或复杂组合子。

4. **从小步骤开始**：每次学习一个新概念，写简单代码片段，逐渐增加复杂性。习惯于重写和试验代码。

5. **精确与习惯**：从一开始就启用Clippy进行代码检查，养成良好编码习惯。

通过这些策略，学习者可以更顺利地掌握Rust，减少学习曲线中的困难。

data.title: Less meat is nearly always better than sustainable meat
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了如何通过饮食选择减少碳足迹。研究表明，食物的生产过程，尤其是肉类和奶制品，是饮食中碳排放的主要来源，远超食物的运输和包装。植物性食物，如豌豆、豆腐和坚果，其碳足迹通常远低于肉类和奶制品。例如，生产100克豌豆蛋白的排放量仅为0.4千克二氧化碳当量，而同等牛肉蛋白的排放量高达35千克。即便考虑全球不同地区的差异，植物性食物的碳足迹仍普遍低于肉类，即使是低影响的肉类生产。在欧洲饮食中，肉类、奶制品和鸡蛋占据了83%的碳排放。因此，减少肉类消费，尤其是牛肉和羊肉，是降低饮食碳足迹的有效方法。转向鸡肉、猪肉或植物性食物也能显著减少碳排放。

Home
CO2 & Greenhouse Gas Emissions
What is the best way to reduce our diet's carbon footprint?
I have
shown previously
that
what
we choose to eat has the largest impact, making a bigger difference than how far our food has traveled, or how much packaging it’s wrapped in. This is because only a small fraction comes from transport and packaging, and most of our food emissions come from processes on the farm, or from
land use
change.
Regardless of whether you compare the footprint of foods in terms of their
weight
(e.g., one kilogram of cheese versus one kilogram of peas),
protein content
, or
calories
, the overall conclusion is the same: plant-based foods tend to have a lower carbon footprint than meat and dairy. In many cases, a much smaller footprint.
As an example, producing 100 grams of protein from peas
emits just
0.4 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalents (CO
2
eq). To get the same amount of protein from beef, emissions would be nearly 90 times higher, at 35 kgCO
2
eq.
1
But it comes with the caveat that comparisons are made based on global averages.
Many argue that this overlooks the large variation in the footprints of foods across the world. Using global averages might give us a misleading picture for some parts of the world or some producers. If I source my beef or lamb from low-impact producers, could they have a lower footprint than plant-based alternatives?The evidence suggests, no: plant-based foods emit fewer greenhouse gases than meat and dairy, regardless of how they are produced.
Let’s take a look at the full range of footprints for protein-rich foods.
Protein-rich foods account for the bulk of our dietary emissions. In European diets, meat, dairy and eggs account for 83%.
2
That’s why I focus on them here.
In the visualization we see the range of carbon footprints for these foods. This data is from the largest meta-analysis of global food systems to date, published in
Science
by Joseph Poore and Thomas Nemecek (2018).
3
In this study, the authors looked at data across more than 38,000 commercial farms in 119 countries.
All greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are measured in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalents per 100 grams of protein; this metric takes account of not only carbon dioxide but also the range of other greenhouse gases – this is further explained in the footnote.
4
To make reading less repetitive, I refer to it as ‘kgCO
2
eq’ below.
The visualization shows the median footprint – highlighted by a small white circle for each food product.
But since there are large differences between producers, this chart also shows the full spectrum of emissions – from the lowest to highest producers. The height at each point in the curve represents the amount of global production with that specific footprint.
Download image
The median footprint for beef is 25 kgCO
2
eq.
5
But some producers have a much higher footprint: ten percent emit more than 105 kgCO
2
eq per 100 grams. At the other end, some are much lower. Ten percent emit less than 9 kgCO
2
eq. We see from the height of the curve that most beef production lies in the range between 17 to 27 kgCO
2
eq.
How do the distributions between plant-based and meat-based sources compare?
Plant-based protein sources – tofu, beans, peas and nuts – have the lowest carbon footprint. This is certainly true when you compare average emissions. But it’s still true when you compare the extremes: there’s not much overlap in emissions between the
worst
producers of plant proteins, and the
best
producers of meat and dairy.
Let’s compare the highest-impact producers (the top ten percent) of plant-based proteins with the lowest-impact producers (the bottom ten percent) of meat and dairy.
The pea producers with the highest footprint emit just 0.8 kgCO
2
eq per 100 grams of protein.
6
For nuts it is 2.4 and for tofu, 3.5 kgCO
2
eq. All are several times less than the lowest impact lamb (12  kgCO
2
eq) and beef (9 kgCO
2
eq). Emissions are also lower than those from the best cheese and pork (4.5 kgCO
2
eq); and slightly lower or comparable to those from the lowest-footprint chicken (2.4 kgCO
2
eq).
7
If you want a lower-carbon diet, eating
less
meat is nearly always better than eating the
most sustainable
meat.
This is also true for the differences
between
meat products. Chicken, eggs, and pork nearly always have a lower footprint than beef and lamb: there is some, but not much overlap between the
worst
poultry and pork producers, and the
best
beef and lamb producers. The world’s highest impact chicken and pork have a footprint of 12 and 14 kgCO
2
eq. This is similar to, or only slightly higher than, the world’s best beef and lamb.
Regardless of where you get your beef or lamb from, substituting with chicken and pork is likely to reduce your carbon footprint.
More sustainable meat production can still make a big difference

data.title: How (memory) safe is Zig? (2021)
data.author: vortex_ape
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Zig语言在内存安全性方面与C和Rust的比较，重点关注系统性防止内存安全漏洞的能力。作者指出，Zig在消除C语言中一些明显的陷阱和提供更好的默认选项上有所改进，如使用切片类型、禁止空指针、自动边界检查、算术溢出检查等。Zig还引入了运行时分配器以捕获使用后释放和双重释放问题，并通过`defer`和`errdefer`简化资源清理，减少错误可能性。然而，Zig缺乏Rust那样的可组合编译时证明系统，无法实现Rust那样系统性的内存安全保障。Rust通过独特的编译器验证机制，能够构建高度内存安全的系统，而Zig主要通过运行时检查和更好的默认设置来提升安全性，但未达到Rust的水平。Zig仍在快速发展中，未来可能会有更多改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程语言和工具在实现内存安全性方面的机制和效果比较，主要涉及Rust、Zig、C/C++及其相关工具。

不同观点：
• **90s_dev** 认为Rust在系统性预防内存不安全方面比Zig更有效。Zig依赖大量测试和测试分配器来发现和记录错误，而不是通过语言本身的机制来确保内存安全。
• **pizlonator** 反驳关于C/C++无法实现内存安全的观点，提出Fil-C可以提供比Rust更全面的安全性，且没有“逃生舱口”（escape hatches），并与C/C++高度兼容，可以作为clang的替代目标。
• **nanolith** 提出除了编译时机制（如Rust）和测试机制（如Zig）外，还有第三种软件安全机制，即模型检查（model checking）。尽管目前没有针对Zig的模型检查工具，但构建这样一个工具并不困难。
• **BrouteMinou** 认为Zig并不追求内存安全性，而是提供控制。Zig比C更安全，但不能称之为“安全”语言。相比之下，Rust是安全的，而Zig则提供了更多的控制。

补充讨论：
• **dang** 提供了一些关于Zig安全性的历史讨论链接，显示出这个话题在社区中反复出现，且有多次深入讨论。
• **Dwedit** 讨论了在处理未初始化指针时，使用特定内存页和访问标记来提高程序崩溃的可检测性，提供了一种技术上的具体实现方法，以增强安全性。

争议焦点：
• Zig是否能够提供足够的内存安全性。一部分人认为Zig通过测试和控制提供了某种程度的安全性，但不能与Rust相提并论；另一部分人则认为Zig根本不是一种追求内存安全性的语言。
• Rust与C/C++（及Fil-C）在安全性上的比较，特别是在“逃生舱口”和全面安全性方面的优劣。

43978333.article_content:
I keep seeing discussions that equate zig's level of memory safety with c (or occasionally with rust!). Neither is particularly accurate. This is an attempt at a more detailed breakdown.
This article is limited to memory safety. See
Assorted thoughts on zig and rust
for a more general comparison.
I'm concerned mostly with security. In practice, it doesn't seem that any level of testing is sufficient to prevent vulnerabilities due to memory safety in large programs. So I'm not covering tools like AddressSanitizer that are intended for testing and are
not recommended
for production use. Instead I'll focus on tools which can systematically rule out errors (eg compiler-inserted bounds checks completely prevent out-of-bounds heap read/write).
I'm also focusing on software as it is typically shipped, ignoring eg bounds checking compilers like
tcc
or quarantining allocators like
hardened_malloc
which are rarely used because of the performance overhead.
Finally, note the 'Updated' date below the title. Zig in particular is still under rapid development and will likely change faster than this article updates. (See the
tracking issue
for safety mechanisms).
I see two major categories of safety mechanisms:
Adhoc runtime checks
. These appear in all zig and rust codebases but are very rare in idomatic c. Many of these checks are also idiomatic in modern c++ codebases but are hamstrung by backwards-compatible interfaces. These checks are easy to implement and probably sufficiently non-controversial that any new systems language will have similar features. Examples include:
Pervasive use of a slice type (pointer + length) and bounds-checking reads/writes of those slices.
Disallowing null pointers, except via an 'optional' type which cannot be derefenced without checking for null.
Builtin support for tagged unions which cannot be accessed without checking the tag.
Automatic checking of over/underflow in arithmetic and when casting between numeric types.
Using a separate type for null-terminated strings, to prevent accidentally passing a non-null-terminated string when a null-terminated string was expected (usually when interfacing with c/c++ code).
Tracking pointer alignment in the type system and checking for correct alignment when casting between pointer types.
Composable compile-time proofs
. These are unique to rust and are novel, non-trivial to implement and add a significant amount of complexity to the language. The 'composable' part is key. 'Unsafe' code allows adding new axioms to the system, and the compiler verifies that those axioms are composed in valid ways. All rust code is built out of combinations of a small number of such axioms. This is why it has been possible to write complex systems in rust with very little unsafe code and a high level of memory safety, whereas after-the-fact global static analysis has been limited to much more restrictive coding styles. This is also why I don't expect to see a post-hoc static analysis tool for zig that approaches the same level of safety and flexibility that rust achieves - the library apis have to be designed with the proof system in mind.
Zig also has some improvements over c which don't fit into either of these categories:
The standard library includes a set of allocators which catch use-after-free and double-free at runtime. It's
not yet clear
how high the runtime and memory overhead will be. Similar allocators do exist for c and are not widely used, which makes me somewhat pessimistic, but I'd be happy to be proved wrong.
The pervasive allocator api makes it easier to use arena allocation or garbage-collected pools to simplify lifetime management.
Using
defer
and
errdefer
simplifies resource cleanup inside complicated control flow, reducing the possibility of mistakes.
Support for generics almost entirely eliminates the need to cast to/from void pointers.
In zig creating an unitialized variable also requires using the
undefined
keyword which helps flag such cases for review. In debug/release-safe, assigning
undefined
to a variable or pointer also fills that memory region with
0xAA
, increasing the chance of an immediate crash on access and making debugging easier.
In c unitialized variables are often used when the variable can't easily be initialized by a single expression. In zig it's often possible to avoid uninitialized variables by using a labeled block that returns the initial value, or using an optional type and initializing it to null.
@bitcast
produces compile errors if you try to cast between two types with incompatible or undefined representations.
When compiling c code, the zig compiler has safer default options than gcc or clang (eg asan is enabled by default).
To summarize: Zig removes some of the most egregious footguns from c, has better defaults, makes some good practices more ergonomic, and benefits from a fresh start in the standard library (eg using slices everywhere). But it does not nearly approach the level of systematic prevention of memor
43978333.article_summary: 本文讨论了Zig语言在内存安全性方面与C和Rust的比较，重点关注系统性防止内存安全漏洞的能力。作者指出，Zig在消除C语言中一些明显的陷阱和提供更好的默认选项上有所改进，如使用切片类型、禁止空指针、自动边界检查、算术溢出检查等。Zig还引入了运行时分配器以捕获使用后释放和双重释放问题，并通过`defer`和`errdefer`简化资源清理，减少错误可能性。然而，Zig缺乏Rust那样的可组合编译时证明系统，无法实现Rust那样系统性的内存安全保障。Rust通过独特的编译器验证机制，能够构建高度内存安全的系统，而Zig主要通过运行时检查和更好的默认设置来提升安全性，但未达到Rust的水平。Zig仍在快速发展中，未来可能会有更多改进。

data.title: Garbage collection of object storage at scale
data.author: ko_pivot
data.article_summary: WarpStream是Apache Kafka的替代方案，构建于对象存储之上。其主要技术挑战之一是解决如何有效删除对象存储中已被逻辑删除的文件。这些文件可能由于数据过期、主题删除或压缩等原因被删除。简单使用桶策略（如设置7天自动删除）不适用于复杂系统，如WarpStream，因为不同主题的保留时间可能不同，且Kafka具有压缩主题等高级功能，无法通过简单策略实现。同步删除也存在问题，如节点崩溃可能导致文件成为孤儿文件，增加存储成本。为解决这些问题，WarpStream考虑使用延迟队列、异步协调或两者结合的方法来有效管理对象存储的清理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对存储系统的垃圾收集（GC）和删除操作的解决方案及其优缺点

不同观点：
• deathanatos认为简单的“桶策略”（bucket policy）并非万能，提出可以利用写前日志（WAL）来处理删除操作。他描述了将待删除操作记录到对象存储中，执行删除，然后再删除WAL文件的方法。如果系统崩溃并发现WAL文件，则可以重新执行删除命令。这种方法在他处理混合删除场景（例如部分删除在对象存储中，部分在SQL数据库中）时非常有效，因为对象存储被用作强一致性存储。

• telotortium对deathanatos的评论做出了回应，提到WarpStream销售一种基于对象存储的Apache Kafka替代品，暗示这种产品可能在解决该问题上有效，并以一种不突兀的方式进行了宣传。

• siscia分享了一种在成本不敏感环境下的有效方法：定期压缩文件，并设置桶策略删除超过一定时间（t+delta+buffer）的文件。同时设置一个报警机制，针对超过t+buffer的文件进行提醒。这种方法依赖于定期压缩和时间缓冲来管理文件删除。

• juancn提出了另一种大规模垃圾收集的机制，即基于概率标记-清除（mark and sweep）方法，使用布隆过滤器（bloom filters）。在标记阶段并行构建多个布隆过滤器，然后合并这些过滤器。在清除阶段，利用合并后的布隆过滤器来判断文件/对象是否存活。布隆过滤器可以确定文件不存活，或者以一定概率判断文件可能存活。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种技术方案，包括WAL、桶策略、压缩策略以及布隆过滤器，展示了不同方法在处理大规模存储系统垃圾收集问题时的多样性。
• 不同方法在处理删除操作时的效率、成本和复杂性上各有优劣。例如，deathanatos的WAL方法强调强一致性，而sisia的方法则侧重于通过时间缓冲和报警机制来确保操作的可靠性。
• juancn的布隆过滤器方法引入了一种概率性算法，可以在资源有限的情况下处理大规模数据，但其缺点是可能存在误报。

争议焦点：
• 不同方法在实际应用中的适用性及优缺点是讨论的主要争议点。例如，deathanatos的WAL方法在复杂场景下有效，但可能增加系统复杂性，而sisia的方法则较为简单直接，但依赖于精确的时间控制和报警机制。

43945423.article_content:
WarpStream Executive Summary
Sign in
start free
Get started free
HN Disclaimer:
WarpStream sells a drop-in replacement for Apache Kafka built directly on-top of object storage.
Over the last 10 years, Iâve built several distributed systems on top of object storage, with
WarpStream
being the most recent. One consistent factor across all of these systems is how much time we spent solving what seems like a relatively straightforward problem: removing files from object storage that had been logically deleted either due to data expiry or compaction.
I discussed this in more detail in
âThe Case for Shared Storageâ blog post
, but to briefly recap: every shared storage system Iâve ever built has looked something like this:
Clients interact with stateless nodes (that are perhaps split into different ârolesâ). The stateless nodes abstract over a shared storage backend (like object storage) and a strongly-consistent metadata store to create some kind of logical abstraction, in WarpStreamâs case: the Apache Kafka protocol.
There are a few ways in which a WarpStream file can end up logically deleted in the metadata store, and therefore needs to be physically deleted from the object store:
All the data in the file has expired due to the configured topic TTLs: â´
All of the data in the file is deleted due to explicit topic deletions: â´
The file was logically deleted by a compaction in which this particular file participated as an input: â´
In the rest of this post, Iâll go over a few different ways to solve this problem by using a
delayed queue
,
async reconciliation
, or
both
. But before I introduce what I think the best ways to solve this problem are, letâs first go over a few approaches that seem obvious, but donât work well in practice like
bucket policies
and
synchronous deletion
.
Why Not Just Use a Bucket Policy?
The easiest way to handle object storage cleanup would be to use a bucket policy with a configurable TTL. For example, we could configure an object storage policy that automatically deletes files that are more than 7 days old. For simple or time-series oriented systems, this is often a good solution.
However, for more complex systems like WarpStream, which has to provide the abstraction of Apache Kafka, this approach doesnât work. For example, consider a WarpStream cluster with hundreds or thousands of different topics. Some topics could be configured with retention as low as 1 hour, and others with retention as high as 90 days. If we relied on a simple bucket policy, then weâd have to configure the bucket policy to be
at least
90 days, which would incur excessive storage costs for the topics with lower retention because a WarpStream file can contain data for many different topics.
Even if we were comfortable with requiring that all topics within a single cluster share a single retention, other implementation details and features in Kafka canât be implemented with a simple object storage bucket policy. For example, Kafka has a feature called âcompacted topicsâ. In a compacted topic, records are deleted / expired not when theyâre too old, but when
theyâre overwritten by a new record with the same key
. A record may be overwritten seconds after it was first written, or several years later.
Unfortunately, bucket policies only work as a mechanism for cleaning up object storage files for the most simple use-cases. Shared storage systems that need to provide more advanced functionality will have to implement object cleanup in the system itself.
Why Not Just Use Synchronous Deletion?
Naively, it seems like whenever the metadata store decides to logically delete a file, it should be able to go and physically remove the file from the object store at the same time, keeping the two systems in sync:
// Tada.
metadataStore.DeleteFile(fileID)
objectStore.DeleteFile(fileID)
â
In traditional programming language theory, this method of garbage collection is analogous to âreference trackingâ. But distributed systems arenât programming languages, and the code above doesnât work in the real world:
if err := metadataStore.DeleteFile(fileID); err != nil {
// This is fine, we can just retry later.
}
if err := objectStore.DeleteFile(fileID); err != nil {
// Uh oh. This file will be orphaned in object storage forever.
}
â
If the file is removed from the metadata store successfully, but isnât removed from the object store (because a node crashed, we got a 500, etc.), then that file will be
orphaned
in the object store.
An orphan file is a file that is physically present in the object store, but not logically tracked in the metadata store, and therefore not part of the distributed database anymore. This is a problem because these orphaned files will accumulate over time and cost you a lot of money.
But actually, thereâs another reason this approach doesnât work even if both deletes succeeded atomically somehow: in-flight queries. The lifecycle of a query in a shared storage s

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于CARDIAC（纸板教学计算机）的历史、用途及其教学效果的讨论

不同观点：
• [manithree] 认为CARDIAC的高质量版本很重要，并且强调如果没有实际的"机器"（即物理模型），整个教学概念就没有意义。他还分享了自己在1979或1980年获得该设备的个人经历，并表示至今仍保留着它。

• [jleyank] 提出CARDIAC可能采用了两步教学法。首先，让学生通过操作纸板模型了解汇编编程、指令处理和内存等概念。接着，学生通过编写CARDIAC的电子版（虚拟机）来深化学习，并通过调试过程学习各种相关的技术。他还将CARDIAC与PDP-8等早期小型计算机的使用体验相比较。

• [andrehacker] 提到与CARDIAC相关的更早期（1959年）的PAPAC-00，这是一个2寄存器、1位、固定指令的二进制数字计算机，意在提供更多历史背景信息。

• [rootbear] 分享了个人经历，他在1970年左右由八年级的科学老师获得了一个CARDIAC设备，并表示这激发了他对计算机的兴趣，且至今仍保留着它。

• [Prunkton] 引用了一个与CARDIAC文档中的流程图相关的幽默例子（关于修理轮胎的流程图），通过性别问题引发的幽默反应，暗示了教学材料中的某些过时或不合适的表达。

• [anthk] 表达了对一种名为SUBLEQ的机械计算机的兴趣，并希望它能通过Eforth语言输出到电传打字机上，讨论了CARDIAC之外的其他可能的教学工具。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点并不明显，但不同用户对CARDIAC的具体用途和教学效果存在不同的评价角度，有的侧重个人经历和情感价值，有的则关注其教学方法和历史背景。
• 幽默元素（Prunkton的评论）提供了一个轻松的视角，但也指出了历史教学材料中可能存在的性别偏见问题。
• 对CARDIAC的历史背景和其他类似设备的提及（如PAPAC-00）丰富了讨论，提供了更广泛的视野。

• [andrehacker] 提到与CARDIAC相关的更早期（1959年）的PAPAC-00，这是一个2寄存器、1位、固定指令的二进制数字计算机，意在提供更多历史背景信息。

• [rootbear] 分享了个人经历，他在1970年左右由八年级的科学老师获得了一个CARDIAC设备，并表示这激发了他对计算机的兴趣，且至今仍保留着它。

• [Prunkton] 引用了一个与CARDIAC文档中的流程图相关的幽默例子（关于修理轮胎的流程图），通过性别问题引发的幽默反应，暗示了教学材料中的某些过时或不合适的表达。

• [anthk] 表达了对一种名为SUBLEQ的机械计算机的兴趣，并希望它能通过Eforth语言输出到电传打字机上，讨论了CARDIAC之外的其他可能的教学工具。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点并不明显，但不同用户对CARDIAC的具体用途和教学效果存在不同的评价角度，有的侧重个人经历和情感价值，有的则关注其教学方法和历史背景。
• 幽默元素（Prunkton的评论）提供了一个轻松的视角，但也指出了历史教学材料中可能存在的性别偏见问题。
• 对CARDIAC的历史背景和其他类似设备的提及（如PAPAC-00）丰富了讨论，提供了更广泛的视野。

data.title: Coffee for people who don't like coffee
data.author: ostwilkens
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者从喜欢喝Jolt Cola等碳酸饮料，到因健康原因尝试咖啡的经历。由于不喜欢传统咖啡的苦酸味道和高温，作者受到YouTube咖啡专家James Hoffmann的启发，开始探索轻度烘焙咖啡，并购买了便宜的研磨机和Clever Dripper进行冲泡。作者尝试了多种咖啡豆，偏好轻盈多汁的品种，如Kichawir和Hunkute，并邀请读者推荐其他咖啡豆。文章最后提醒读者利用搜索引擎寻找咖啡烘焙商。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：咖啡的不同制作方法、口味偏好及其文化背景

不同观点：
• nkrisc认为优质的咖啡豆不应过度烘焙，同时强调使用 whole bean 和过滤水的重要性，并分享了自己在温度和冲泡时间上的经验。
• iamthemonster介绍了澳大利亚的咖啡文化，特别是对深烘焙豆子的偏好以及其在牛奶咖啡中的应用，同时指出浅烘豆在澳洲并不常见，且更适合黑咖啡。
• podunkPDX分享了自己从手动烘豆到购买专业烘豆机的经历，强调自制烘豆的优越口感。
• yoko888表示自己不喜欢咖啡的苦味，更偏好喝水和绿茶，认为每个人都有自己适合的饮品。
• owlninja提到自己不喜欢喝热饮，即使在炎热环境下有些人仍然喜欢喝热咖啡，这让他感到不解。
• 90s_dev讲述了自己从讨厌咖啡到习惯并喜欢上黑咖啡的过程，并分享了一种简易的泡咖啡方法。
• Adambuilds认为咖啡已经从传统苦味饮品演变为适应各种口味和健康需求的饮品，并分享了自己对浅烘和果味咖啡的喜爱。
• mastazi对瑞典咖啡烘焙习惯进行了讨论，质疑了一些关于北欧烘焙习惯的常见说法。
• kmm认为速溶咖啡适合不喜欢繁琐过程的人，并表示自己对咖啡的口味要求不高，因此速溶咖啡已能满足其需求。
• Waterluvian分享了自己从讨厌咖啡到逐渐适应并最终喜欢上咖啡的经历，特别是通过加入大量热巧克力来过渡。
• maxwellg强调了自己在家制作高质量咖啡的体验，并指出好咖啡使得对劣质咖啡更加难以忍受。
• gorfian_robot以讽刺的语气建议不喜欢咖啡的人直接选择其他饮品，如即饮茶。
• Quenby则关注现磨咖啡对比预磨咖啡的差别，并询问其他人对不同冲泡工具的看法。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是浅烘与深烘咖啡的口味及其适用场景，尤其是在不同文化背景下对烘焙程度的偏好。
• 另一个讨论点是咖啡制作的简便性与复杂性之间的平衡，一些人喜欢简化过程（如速溶咖啡），而另一些人则享受复杂的制作过程（如手冲、烘豆）。
• 还有部分讨论涉及咖啡与其他饮品（如茶、热巧克力）的比较，以及个人口味偏好的多样性。

43945585.article_content:
Coffee for people who don't like coffee
I grew up on
Jolt Cola
. After the original Jolt left Sweden in 2009, my friend group tried dozens of colas to replace it. Other greats like Premier Extreme Cola also eventually disappeared. In 2013,
Volt Cola
came to save the day, and I was back on the juice.
If not for some health concerns.
All that sugar. Dad always reminds me:
You'll get diabetes. Have a coffee.
But I never liked it. Bitter and sour at the same time. On top of that, it's served scalding hot.
Even so, for health, I find myself yet again giving it a go.
Youtube coffee legend James Hoffmann introduced me to the concept of lightly roasted coffee. Here in Sweden, it is customary to roast and brew coffee the same color as your soul: dark and ragged. The idea that coffee can have any taste other burnt rubber was interesting.
I acquired a cheap grinder and a
Clever Dripper
.
The beans
Then I tried a lot of coffees. These are the few beans that I think taste good (on most days). My preference is light and juicy coffee.
Kichawir
Hunkute
I will add to this list as I find new coffees.
If you have bean recommendations,
hit me up on Matrix
.
Google is your friend for finding roasters.
2025-05-10

data.title: Y Combinator says Google is a monopolist, no comment about its OpenAI ties
data.author: mastazi
data.article_summary: 知名创业投资机构Y Combinator（YC）在美国针对谷歌垄断案中提交了一份法庭意见书，指责谷歌通过成为默认搜索引擎等反竞争行为，抑制了美国创业生态系统的发展，特别是在网络搜索和AI领域。YC指出，谷歌的垄断地位使其和风投公司在资助可能挑战谷歌的创新企业时犹豫不决，导致市场停滞。YC建议谷歌开放其搜索索引，以促进竞争，并希望政府在五年内若未见改变，可强制谷歌剥离部分业务。尽管YC与谷歌在某些领域有合作，但YC也与谷歌的竞争对手OpenAI有紧密联系，后者正直接与谷歌在搜索领域竞争。谷歌则认为政府的惩罚提议过于激进，可能损害消费者和开发者利益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google是否为垄断者，以及Y Combinator（YC）和OpenAI在AI领域的竞争与反垄断问题。

不同观点：
• **Google并非垄断者**：benoau认为，基于LLM的搜索正由DuckDuckGo等第三方提供，并且用户可以从多个模型中选择，因此Google不能被视为垄断者。
• **Google是垄断者**：mountainriver和teleforce认为，Google凭借其广泛使用的产品（如Google Search、Gmail、YouTube等）已经形成了垄断，这种垄断对市场健康不利。teleforce进一步指出，Google拥有强大的护城河，尤其是在AI领域。
• **YC与Google的竞争关系**：dpiers指出，由于Google将Gemini免费捆绑到Google Workspace中，他们正在放弃ChatGPT Enterprise，表明OpenAI在反竞争环境中并不安全，YC的初创公司也是如此。
• **YC与Google的垄断讨论**：cadamsdotcom认为，YC的垄断地位并不能否定Google的垄断地位，并批评TechCrunch引入无关的虚伪论点。nand_gate则认为，YC有能力通过专注于质量而不是数量来颠覆Google的垄断地位。
• **广告问题**：mortsnort强调，Google通过在搜索结果中出售广告，使得互联网变得广告泛滥，影响了用户体验。

补充讨论：
• **NotebookLM的评价**：teleforce对Google的NotebookLM产品给予高度评价，认为其在减少幻觉和提供研究帮助方面非常有效，甚至愿意为此付费。
• **开放搜索索引的讨论**：arealaccount提到，有人建议Google开放其搜索索引，以便其他公司可以利用这些数据训练LLM模型，这涉及到反垄断和市场公平竞争的问题。
• **组织结构的批评**：portnoyd批评了YC和Google的组织结构，认为这些公司的顶层设计故意模糊了实际受益者，并建议应直接针对这些高层设计而非公司留下的书面痕迹。

争议焦点：
• Google是否为垄断者，及其在AI领域的市场影响力。
• YC与Google之间的竞争关系，以及YC是否能通过改变策略来颠覆Google的垄断地位。
• 反垄断问题的具体表现，如Google是否应开放其搜索索引以促进市场公平竞争。

43978224.article_content:
Fabled startup investor and accelerator Y Combinator has some choice words for Google in an amicus brief it just submitted in the U.S.’s monopoly case against the search giant.
In the
brief
, YC charged that Google is a “monopolist” that has “stunted” the U.S. startup ecosystem by making VC firms like itself hesitate to fund web search and AI startups in what it calls a “kill zone” around Google.
“Google has chilled independent firms like YC from funding and accelerating innovative startups that could otherwise have challenged Google’s dominance,” YC wrote in the filing. “The result is a landscape that has been artificially stunted and stagnant.”
YC’s brief says it’s currently seeking to fund startups developing question-based and agentic AI tools that could transform how people interact with information on the internet. But YC says there’s a “clear risk” that Google will use its monopoly power to slow down the future of those markets.
“Google has effectively frozen the web search and text advertising markets for over a decade,” YC wrote.
The brief, filed May 9, was
spotted
on X by VC Sheel Mohnot, the general partner of Better Tomorrow Ventures and a prolific social media poster.
But YC isn’t calling for an immediate breakup of Google, as its CEO Garry Tan
made clear in a reply to Mohnot.

Exhibit at TechCrunch Sessions: AI

Rather, YC is arguing Google should curb practices it considers anti-competitive, like paying Apple billions of dollars to make Google the iPhone’s default search engine. It also wants Google to do things it argues would help startups, like opening up Google’s search index so others can train LLMs on it.
For perspective, Google’s search algorithms have been its highly prized secret since its inception. For YC to ask the government to force Google to open it up to competitive LLMs is almost like demanding the government make Microsoft Windows open source, or forcing Amazon to freely deliver packages for competitors.
If Google doesn’t implement such changes within a five-year time frame, then YC advocates for the government to force Google to divest or spin out parts of itself. YC CEO Tan
characterized
this idea in an X post as a “spinoff hammer” threat. He also posted that “we love Google” but wants “little tech” to succeed, too, in a
separate X thread
.
YC released an amicus brief re: US v Google yesterday.
We love Google and what it represents as a paragon of US-led tech and innovation. We also want to make sure the excesses of big tech make way for tomorrow's little tech.
— Garry Tan (@garrytan)
May 10, 2025
To recap, last year
Google lost a massive antitrust case over its dominance of the search market
. While Google appeals the decision, the U.S. government is mulling potential punishments (“remedies”) that Google might be required to implement,
such as spinning off Chrome.
Those remedies are expected to be
delivered
by August 2025.
YC’s stance may come as a surprise to those who have followed its latest partnerships with Google: Most notably, Google Cloud
gave YC startups access to a dedicated cluster of Nvidia GPUs
last year. Google co-founder Larry Page also
made a rare in-person appearance
to speak at a YC event in December.
Google
has also acquired
at least two YC-backed startups: Flutter in 2014, and Fridge
in 2011.
It also
invested in YC startup Infisical
through its Gradient fund in 2023.
However, YC is also closely tied to OpenAI, which is
now directly competing against Google on search
. OpenAI’s CEO Sam Altman used to run YC, while OpenAI was the first group
affiliated
with YC Research.
That’s something Mohnot
pointed to
on X, writing that the biggest beneficiary of YC’s proposed remedies, by far, would be OpenAI, rather than YC’s famously early-stage startups, while commenting that the amicus brief “paints Google as more powerful than it is.”
TechCrunch asked YC how it would respond to this critique, and whether it has any specific examples of areas that it probably would have funded had it not been for Google. So far, YC hasn’t responded to our comment request.
Google didn’t respond to a request for comment about YC’s amicus brief, either. However, it
argued
in a blog post last year that the DOJ’s proposals are “radical and sweeping” and would hurt consumers, business, and developers.
